paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
original_question: For every graph G and every edge e of G, is χ⋆ℓ(G) ≤ χ⋆ℓ(G-e)+2, where χ⋆ℓ denotes the list packing number and G-e is the graph obtained by deleting e?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. A list assignment for $G$ is a function $L$ that assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ a set $L(v)$ of colors. For a positive integer $k$, a $k$-fold list assignment is one with $|L(v)|=k$ for all $v\in V$. Given a $k$-fold list assignment $L$, an $L$-packing is a collection $(c_1,c_2,\dots,c_k)$ of $k$ proper colorings of $G$ such that:
(i) for every vertex $v$, $c_i(v)\in L(v)$ for each $i$; and
(ii) for every vertex $v$, the colors $c_1(v),c_2(v),\dots,c_k(v)$ are pairwise distinct (i.e. $\{c_1(v),\dots,c_k(v)\}=L(v)$).
The list packing number $\chi^\star_\ell(G)$ is the smallest $k$ such that, for every $k$-fold list assignment $L$ for $G$, an $L$-packing exists.

For an edge $e\in E$, let $G-e$ denote the graph obtained from $G$ by deleting the edge $e$.

Question: Is it true that for every graph $G$ and every edge $e$ of $G$,
$$\chi^\star_\ell(G) \le \chi^\star_\ell(G-e) + 2\,?$$
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem at the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings (2023). A direct web search for the specific inequality and for recent results on edge-deletion stability of the list packing number returned no resolution; related work (e.g. on well-definedness of $\chi^\star_\ell$) exists but does not settle this particular bound. No published solution was located.

original_question: For each fixed integer t>1, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph G of treewidth at most t, determines the value of the list packing number χ⋆ℓ(G)?
self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. A list assignment for G is a function L that assigns to every vertex v∈V a finite set L(v) of colors. A proper L-coloring of G is a function c: V→⋃_v L(v) such that c(v)∈L(v) for every v∈V and c(u)≠c(v) whenever uv∈E. 

For an integer k≥1, a k-fold L-packing of G is a sequence (c_1,c_2,…,c_k) of proper L-colorings of G with the additional property that, for every vertex v∈V, the colors c_1(v),c_2(v),…,c_k(v) are pairwise distinct (so they form a k-subset of L(v)). The list packing number χ⋆_ℓ(G) is defined as the smallest integer k such that, for every list assignment L with |L(v)|=k for all v∈V, there exists a k-fold L-packing of G.

The treewidth of G is defined in the usual way via tree decompositions: it is the minimum, over all tree decompositions (T,{X_t}_{t∈V(T)}) of G, of (max_t |X_t|)−1.

status_search_result: List packing was introduced recently (Cambie et al.) and the list packing number χ⋆_ℓ has been studied for several graph classes, but no published result establishes a polynomial-time algorithm to compute χ⋆_ℓ(G) on graphs of bounded treewidth. paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
original_question: For non-complete graphs G of order n, where δ(G) is the minimum degree and rc(G) is the rainbow connection number, does there exist a constant c≥0 such that δ(G) ≥ n/2+c always implies rc(G)=2? Here an edge-colored graph is rainbow connected if every two vertices are connected by a path whose edges all have different colors, and rc(G) is the minimum number of colors needed for such a coloring.
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple connected graph. An edge-coloring of G (not necessarily proper) is called a rainbow coloring if for every pair of distinct vertices u, v ∈ V there exists a u–v path all of whose edges receive pairwise distinct colors. The rainbow connection number rc(G) is the smallest number of colors in such an edge-coloring. Let δ(G) denote the minimum degree of G and let n = |V(G)|.

It is known that if δ(G) ≥ n/2 + log n then rc(G) = 2, while there exist graphs with δ(G) ≥ n/2 − 1 and rc(G) > 2 (e.g., two cliques of order n/2 joined by a single edge).

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant c ≥ 0 such that for every non-complete graph G of order n,
    δ(G) ≥ n/2 + c   implies   rc(G) = 2 ?
status_search_result: The best known sufficient condition is δ(G) ≥ n/2 + log n implying rc(G) = 2 (Krivelevich–Yuster type result, refined in subsequent work), while δ(G) ≥ n/2 − 1 is insufficient. Whether a constant additive term c suffices instead of log n appears to remain an open question; no source found establishing or refuting the existence of such a constant.

paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
original_question: Does there exist a 5-edge-connected 5-regular graph that is Class 2, meaning it is not edge-colorable with Δ(G) colors?
self_contained_problem:
A graph $G$ is said to be $k$-regular if every vertex has degree exactly $k$, and $k$-edge-connected if removing any set of fewer than $k$ edges leaves the graph connected. The chromatic index $\chi'(G)$ is the smallest number of colors needed to color the edges of $G$ so that no two edges sharing a vertex receive the same color. By Vizing's theorem, $\chi'(G) \in \{\Delta(G), \Delta(G)+1\}$, where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree. A graph $G$ is called Class 1 if $\chi'(G) = \Delta(G)$ and Class 2 if $\chi'(G) = \Delta(G)+1$.

Does there exist a 5-edge-connected 5-regular graph that is Class 2 (i.e., whose chromatic index equals $6$)?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in workshop problem collections and is closely connected with conjectures (Berge–Fulkerson, Fan–Raspaud) for 5-edge-connected 5-regular graphs studied by Ma, Mattiolo, Steffen and Wolf. No resolution (either an example or a proof of non-existence) appears in the literature retrieved.

paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
original_question: Can one describe exactly all subcubic K3-free graphs of Class 2, where subcubic means maximum degree at most 3, K3-free means triangle-free, and Class 2 means the graph is not edge-colorable with Δ(G) colors?
self_contained_problem:
A graph $G$ is called subcubic if its maximum degree $\Delta(G)$ is at most $3$, and triangle-free (equivalently $K_3$-free) if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices. By Vizing's theorem, the chromatic index $\chi'(G)$ satisfies $\chi'(G)\in\{\Delta(G),\Delta(G)+1\}$; the graph $G$ is said to be of Class 1 if $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)$ and of Class 2 if $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)+1$.

Provide an exact structural description (characterization) of all subcubic triangle-free graphs that are of Class 2.
status_search_result: The problem of characterizing all Class 2 subcubic graphs (and even the triangle-free subcase) is a long-standing open question in edge-coloring theory; the general problem of recognizing Class 2 graphs is NP-hard even for cubic graphs (Holyer), and no exact structural description for the triangle-free subcubic case appears in the literature. The web search returned only partial or related results (specific subclasses such as planar, bipartite, or K4-minor-free), with no claim of a complete characterization.

paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
original_question: When a graph G has a Type-A order or a Type-B order, can such an order be found in polynomial time? A Type-A order requires each vertex to have an odd number of earlier neighbors or none, and a Type-B order additionally permits a vertex to have an even number of earlier neighbors if it has no later neighbors.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. For a linear ordering $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n$ of $V$, call the vertices appearing before $v_i$ in the order the "earlier neighbors" of $v_i$ (restricted to $N(v_i)$), and those appearing after $v_i$ the "later neighbors" of $v_i$.

Define two types of vertex orderings:
- A Type-A order is a linear ordering of $V$ such that every vertex $v_i$ has either zero earlier neighbors or an odd number of earlier neighbors.
- A Type-B order is a linear ordering of $V$ such that every vertex $v_i$ satisfies at least one of: (i) it has an odd number of earlier neighbors, (ii) it has no earlier neighbors, or (iii) it has an even number of earlier neighbors and no later neighbors.

Question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph $G$, decides whether $G$ admits a Type-A order (respectively, a Type-B order) and, if so, produces such an order?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the collection of open problems from the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings (2024). No subsequent work resolving the polynomial-time recognition/construction of Type-A or Type-B vertex orders was located in available search results.

paper_title: Open Problems in Grid Labeling
context_brief: Labelings of C_{4m+2} x P_{2n+1} grids
original_question: For positive integers m and n, determine whether the Cartesian-product grid graph C_{4m+2} x P_{2n+1} admits each of the following three labelings: an a-valuation, a graceful labeling, and a harmonious labeling. Here P_r is the path with r vertices, C_r is the cycle with r vertices, and G x H is the Cartesian product graph whose vertices are ordered pairs and whose edges join pairs that agree in one coordinate and are adjacent in the other. A graceful labeling of a connected graph with e edges assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e so that the absolute differences on edges are exactly 1 through e; an a-valuation is a graceful labeling with a threshold separating the endpoint labels of every edge; a harmonious labeling assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e - 1 so that edge sums are distinct modulo e.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P_r$ denote the path graph on $r$ vertices and $C_r$ the cycle graph on $r$ vertices. For graphs $G$ and $H$, the Cartesian product $G \square H$ has vertex set $V(G) \times V(H)$, with two vertices $(u_1,v_1)$ and $(u_2,v_2)$ adjacent if and only if either $u_1 = u_2$ and $v_1v_2 \in E(H)$, or $v_1 = v_2$ and $u_1u_2 \in E(G)$.

For a connected graph $G$ with $e$ edges:
(i) A graceful labeling is an injection $f: V(G) \to \{0, 1, \ldots, e\}$ such that the induced edge labels $\{|f(u) - f(v)| : uv \in E(G)\}$ equal $\{1, 2, \ldots, e\}$.
(ii) An $\alpha$-valuation is a graceful labeling $f$ for which there exists an integer $k$ with $\min\{f(u), f(v)\} \le k < \max\{f(u), f(v)\}$ for every edge $uv \in E(G)$.
(iii) A harmonious labeling is an injection $g: V(G) \to \mathbb{Z}/e\mathbb{Z}$ such that the induced edge labels $\{g(u) + g(v) \pmod{e} : uv \in E(G)\}$ are all distinct (and hence form $\mathbb{Z}/e\mathbb{Z}$).

For all positive integers $m$ and $n$, determine whether the grid-like graph $C_{4m+2} \square P_{2n+1}$ admits (a) an $\alpha$-valuation, (b) a graceful labeling, and (c) a harmonious labeling.
status_search_result: Gallian's dynamic survey of graph labeling lists labelings of prism-like products $C_m \square P_n$ as a long-standing area with several unresolved cases. The specific instance $C_{4m+2} \square P_{2n+1}$ — covering gracefulness, $\alpha$-valuation, and harmonious labeling — is recorded as unresolved, with no published constructions or non-existence proofs found that settle all three questions for general $m$ and $n$.

context_brief: Harmonious labelings of even torus grids
original_question: For positive integers m and n, in all cases not already covered by m = 1 and n > 1, does the Cartesian-product torus grid C_{4m} x C_{2n} admit a harmonious labeling? Here C_r is the cycle with r vertices, C_{4m} x C_{2n} is a Cartesian-product grid on a torus, and a harmonious labeling of a connected graph with e edges assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e - 1 so that edge sums are distinct modulo e.
self_contained_problem:
Let $C_r$ denote the cycle graph on $r$ vertices, and let $G \square H$ denote the Cartesian product of graphs $G$ and $H$. paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
original_question: For the R-stadium, the boundary of the R-neighborhood of a segment, determine all maximal distance minimizers for radius r in the range r<R<5r. Also determine the sharp thresholds for existence of non-horseshoe minimizers and for guaranteed horseshoe minimizers of closed curves with prescribed minimal radius of curvature.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a nonempty compact set and $r>0$. A connected closed set $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is called a maximal distance minimizer for $M$ with radius $r$ if it minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff length $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ among all connected closed sets $\Sigma'\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying $\max_{x\in M}\mathrm{dist}(x,\Sigma')\le r$.

For $R>0$, the $R$-stadium is the set $M=\partial(N_R([AB]))$, the boundary of the closed $R$-neighborhood of a line segment $[AB]\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of positive length. A horseshoe is a planar set consisting of an arc of a circle of radius $R-r$ together with two segments of tangent lines to that arc.

Tasks:
(a) For every $r$ with $r<R<5r$, describe all maximal distance minimizers for the $R$-stadium with radius $r$.
(b) Determine the sharp threshold $R_1(r)$ such that for all $R\le R_1(r)$ there exists a maximal distance minimizer (for the $R$-stadium with radius $r$) that is not a horseshoe, and the sharp threshold $R_2(r)$ such that for all $R\ge R_2(r)$ every maximal distance minimizer is a horseshoe. More generally, for closed convex curves $M\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with prescribed minimal radius of curvature, determine the sharp thresholds guaranteeing existence of non-horseshoe minimizers and, respectively, guaranteed horseshoe-only minimizers.

paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
original_question: For explicit target sets in the maximal distance minimizer problem, determine all MDMs. Test cases include discs or balls B_R in R^d for d>=2, rectangle boundaries for small r>0, and regular n-gons, where the expected polyline structure is not fully proved even for n=3.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a non-empty compact set and let $r > 0$. For a closed set $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, define
$$F_M(\Sigma) = \sup_{y \in M} \mathrm{dist}(y, \Sigma), \qquad \mathrm{dist}(y,\Sigma) = \inf_{x \in \Sigma} |y-x|.$$
A maximal distance minimizer (MDM) for the pair $(M, r)$ is a connected compact set $\Sigma^* \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ that minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ among all connected compact sets $\Sigma$ satisfying the covering constraint $F_M(\Sigma) \le r$, i.e.
$$\Sigma^* \in \arg\min\{\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma) : \Sigma \text{ connected, compact, } F_M(\Sigma) \le r\}.$$

Determine, explicitly, the set of all MDMs in each of the following cases:
(a) $M = B_R \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is a closed ball of radius $R$, for $d \ge 2$ and all $r \in (0,R)$;
(b) $M$ is the boundary of a rectangle in $\mathbb{R}^2$, in the regime of small $r > 0$;
(c) $M$ is a regular $n$-gon in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (i.e., its boundary or its closed convex hull), for each $n \ge 3$ and all $r > 0$ (it is conjectured that each MDM is a finite polyline whose junctions form angles at least $2\pi/3$; prove or disprove this and identify the minimizers explicitly, including the case $n = 3$).
status_search_result: The problem of explicitly determining all maximal distance minimizers for discs/balls, rectangle boundaries (for small r), and regular n-gons remains open. General regularity results are known (MDMs are finite unions of simple curves meeting at angles at least 2π/3), and partial work exists for rectangles, but explicit complete classification—even for the equilateral triangle (n=3)—has not been established.

paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
original_question: For Euclidean R^d, d>=2, what is the Steiner ratio, the infimum over finite point sets of Steiner-tree length divided by minimum-spanning-tree length? In the plane, is the value sqrt(3)/2 attained by an equilateral triangle?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\geq 2$ and a finite point set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, let $\mathrm{MST}(A)$ denote the length (sum of Euclidean edge lengths) of a minimum spanning tree of $A$, and let $\mathrm{SMT}(A)$ denote the length of a Steiner minimal tree on $A$ (the infimum of total Euclidean length over all finite connected graphs in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that contain $A$ among their vertices; equivalently, over all finite trees in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose vertex set contains $A$). Define the Steiner ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$ by
$$\rho_d \;=\; \inf_{A}\, \frac{\mathrm{SMT}(A)}{\mathrm{MST}(A)},$$
where the infimum is taken over all finite subsets $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|A|\geq 2$.

(a) Determine $\rho_d$ for every $d\geq 2$.

(b) In the planar case $d=2$, decide whether $\rho_2 = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, the value attained on the vertex set of an equilateral triangle.
status_search_result: The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture asserts $\rho_2 = \sqrt{3}/2$. A 1990 proof attempt by Du and Hwang was later shown to contain serious gaps (Ivanov–Tuzhilin, 2012), and the conjecture is widely regarded as still open in the plane. The exact value of $\rho_d$ for $d\geq 3$ is also unknown; only bounds are available.

paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
original_question: For a random N-point input in Ω⊂R^d, does the Steiner-tree length have asymptotics βN^((d−1)/d), with β depending on Ω and on the random model?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain with $d \geq 2$. For a finite set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, let $\mathrm{St}(S)$ denote the length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure) of a Steiner tree of $S$, i.e. a connected set of minimal total length containing $S$ (one is allowed to add auxiliary "Steiner" points outside $S$). Fix a random model that produces an $N$-point random sample $X_N = \{X_1, \dots, X_N\} \subset \Omega$ (for instance, $N$ i.i.d. points drawn from a probability density on $\Omega$, or the points of a Poisson point process of intensity $N/|\Omega|$ on $\Omega$, or more general spatial models).

Question: Does there exist a constant $\beta = \beta(\Omega, \text{model}) > 0$ such that
$$\frac{\mathrm{St}(X_N)}{N^{(d-1)/d}} \longrightarrow \beta \qquad \text{as } N \to \infty,$$
where convergence holds almost surely (or in expectation)? Identify the class of admissible random models for which such asymptotics hold, and describe how $\beta$ depends on $\Omega$ and on the model.
category_tag: Random Steiner trees / subadditive Euclidean functionals
status_search_result: For i.i.d. uniform (and more generally absolutely continuous) samples in a bounded region of $\mathbb{R}^d$, the asymptotics $\mathrm{St}(X_N)/N^{(d-1)/d} \to \beta(d)\int_\Omega f(x)^{(d-1)/d}\,dx$ are classical, following from the Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley theorem (1959) and Steele's theory of subadditive Euclidean functionals, which explicitly covers the Steiner tree as one of the standard functionals. For more general (e.g. stationary ergodic, dependent, or non-absolutely-continuous) random models, the analogous BHH-type law is known to fail in some cases (counterexamples exist for ergodic sequences), and the precise class of random models for which the Steiner tree obeys such asymptotics remains an open question.

original_question: For random N-point Steiner-tree inputs in R^d, can one prove bounds β1N^((d−1)/d)≤E H1(S_t)≤β2N^((d−1)/d) that distinguish the Steiner problem from MST, rectilinear Steiner tree, and traveling-salesperson problems? What are good random-setting Steiner-ratio bounds?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 2$ and let $X_1,\dots,X_N$ be i.i.d. random points drawn uniformly from the unit cube $[0,1]^d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. For a finite set $T\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ the (Euclidean) Steiner tree $S_t(T)$ is a connected set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ containing $T$ that minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(S)$; denote by $\mathcal{H}^1(S_t(\{X_1,\dots,X_N\}))$ its total length. Analogously, let $\mathrm{MST}_N$, $\mathrm{RST}_N$, and $\mathrm{TSP}_N$ denote, respectively, the lengths of the Euclidean minimum spanning tree, of the rectilinear Steiner tree (where edges are axis-parallel), and of the optimal traveling-salesperson tour on the same point set.

(a) Determine explicit constants $\beta_1=\beta_1(d)$ and $\beta_2=\beta_2(d)$ with $0<\beta_1\leq\beta_2<\infty$ such that, for all sufficiently large $N$,
$$\beta_1\,N^{(d-1)/d}\ \leq\ \mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(S_t(\{X_1,\dots,X_N\}))\ \leq\ \beta_2\,N^{(d-1)/d},$$
and such that the resulting constants strictly separate the Euclidean Steiner tree functional from the corresponding asymptotic constants for $\mathrm{MST}_N$, $\mathrm{RST}_N$, and $\mathrm{TSP}_N$.

(b) Give the best possible bounds on the random-setting Steiner ratio, defined as $\liminf_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(S_t)/\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{MST}_N$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(S_t)/\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{MST}_N$, for points uniformly distributed in $[0,1]^d$.
status_search_result: Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley type results establish $N^{(d-1)/d}$ scaling for many Euclidean functionals (TSP, MST, Steiner tree), with existence of limiting constants known via subadditive/Yao methods, but the precise constants for the Euclidean Steiner tree functional in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and quantitative separation from MST/RST/TSP constants are not known. The random-setting Steiner ratio likewise remains open; even the deterministic Steiner ratio in the plane (Gilbert–Pollak conjecture) is currently considered open after the gap in Du–Hwang's proof. No source was found resolving the question.

original_question: For n terminals, among the (2n−4)!/(2^(n−2)(n−2)!) full Steiner topologies, how many can simultaneously realize a shortest Steiner solution?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Euclidean Steiner tree problem in the plane: given a finite set of n ≥ 2 points (called terminals) in ℝ², a Steiner tree is a connected planar graph whose vertex set consists of the n terminals together with possibly additional vertices (called Steiner points), with edges drawn as straight-line segments, and whose total Euclidean length is to be minimized. A Steiner topology is called full if every terminal has degree 1 in the tree and every Steiner point has degree 3. The total number of full Steiner topologies on n labeled terminals is

  T(n) = (2n − 4)! / (2^(n−2) (n − 2)!).

For a given configuration of n terminals, several distinct full Steiner topologies may admit geometric realizations that all attain the same minimum total length (a shortest Steiner tree). Determine the maximum, over all configurations of n terminals in the plane, of the number of distinct full Steiner topologies that can simultaneously be realized as a shortest Steiner tree of the configuration. Equivalently, among the T(n) full Steiner topologies, how many can simultaneously give a shortest solution to the Steiner problem?

original_question: Can one construct a nonplanar example of a unique full Steiner tree with infinitely many branching points?
self_contained_problem:
A Steiner tree for a closed set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (called the terminal set) is a connected set $S \supseteq A$ of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(S)$ among all connected sets containing $A$. A Steiner tree is called full if every terminal point is a leaf (an endpoint) of $S$. A branching point of $S$ is a point at which three edges meet; in Euclidean Steiner trees every branching point has degree exactly $3$ with three adjacent segments meeting at pairwise angles $2\pi/3$ and lying in a common plane. A Steiner tree $S$ for $A$ is called unique if it is the only connected set of minimal $\mathcal{H}^1$-measure containing $A$. The tree $S$ is called planar if $S$ is contained in some affine $2$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and nonplanar otherwise.

Question: Does there exist a closed set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (for some $d \geq 3$) admitting a unique full Steiner tree $S$ such that $S$ is nonplanar and has infinitely many branching points?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent (2025) collection of open problems on Steiner trees. Known explicit constructions of Steiner trees with infinitely many branching points (e.g., the Paolini–Stepanov–Teplitskaya 2015 example) are all planar; no nonplanar example is known.

original_question: How are Herman rings created or destroyed when a rational or transcendental map is perturbed, and what is the structure and size of the parameter sets in natural families for which Herman rings occur?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f_\lambda : \widehat{\mathbb{C}} \to \widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a holomorphic family of rational maps (or, more generally, of transcendental meromorphic maps $f_\lambda : \mathbb{C} \to \widehat{\mathbb{C}}$) depending holomorphically on a parameter $\lambda$ in some complex manifold $\Lambda$. Recall that a Herman ring of $f_\lambda$ is a periodic Fatou component $U$ of period $p \geq 1$ that is conformally isomorphic to a round annulus $A_r = \{z : 1 < |z| < r\}$ via a conformal map $\varphi : U \to A_r$ that conjugates $f_\lambda^p|_U$ to an irrational rotation $z \mapsto e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$ of $A_r$ for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}$.

Address the following:

(a) Describe the bifurcation mechanisms by which Herman rings are created and destroyed under perturbation of $\lambda$. In particular, identify the local dynamical phenomena (e.g., collisions of boundary components with the postsingular set, parabolic implosions, quasiconformal surgeries, breakdowns of invariant curves) responsible for the appearance or disappearance of a Herman ring as $\lambda$ varies, and give a classification of such bifurcations.

(b) For a given natural holomorphic family $\{f_\lambda\}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ (for example, the family of degree-$d$ Blaschke-product-like rational maps with a fixed rotation number, the complex standard family $f_\lambda(z) = \lambda z \exp\!\left(\tfrac{a}{2}(z - 1/z)\right)$, or natural families of transcendental meromorphic maps), determine the topological structure, measure-theoretic size (Lebesgue measure, Hausdorff dimension), and analytic properties (e.g., quasi-conformal rigidity, density, accessibility) of the set
$$\mathcal{H}(\{f_\lambda\}) = \{\lambda \in \Lambda : f_\lambda \text{ has a Herman ring}\}.$$
In particular, determine whether $\mathcal{H}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, whether it has nonempty interior, and how its slices by rotation number compare with the corresponding Arnold tongue structure of the associated circle dynamics.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and research on Herman rings explicitly identify the perturbation behavior of Herman rings and the structure/size of the parameter set producing them in natural families as not well understood. Partial results exist (Shishikura's quasiconformal surgery, Arnold disks for the complex standard family, recent constructions of nested and higher-period Herman rings, non-existence results for certain meromorphic maps with omitted values), but the general question of bifurcation mechanisms and the measure-theoretic/topological structure of the Herman-ring parameter locus remains open.

paper_title: Solution of Huntington's "Unsolved Problem in Boolean Algebra"
original_question: Let K be a class containing at least two elements, let T be a subclass of K, let + be a binary operation whose value (a + b) is in K whenever a and b are in K, and let a' be a unary operation whose value is in K whenever a is in K. Assume the following postulates from Huntington's sixth postulate system for Boolean algebra, other than Postulate 1.1: if a is in K, then ((a + a)' + a) is in T; if a and b are in K, then (b' + (a + b)) is in T; if a and b are in K, then ((a + b)' + (b + a)) is in T; if a, b, and c are in K, then ((b' + c)' + ((a + b)' + (a + c))) is in T; and if (a' + b) is in T and (b' + a) is in T, then a = b. Is Postulate 1.1 independent of these other postulates, where Postulate 1.1 says that if a is in T and (a' + b) is in T, then b is in T? Equivalently, can one construct a system (K, T, +, ') that satisfies all the other listed postulates but does not satisfy Postulate 1.1?
self_contained_problem:
Let K be a class containing at least two elements, let T be a subclass of K, let + be a binary operation on K (so a + b ∈ K whenever a, b ∈ K), and let ' be a unary operation on K (so a' ∈ K whenever a ∈ K). Consider the following postulates:

(P2) For every a ∈ K, ((a + a)' + a) ∈ T.
(P3) For all a, b ∈ K, (b' + (a + b)) ∈ T.
(P4) For all a, b ∈ K, ((a + b)' + (b + a)) ∈ T.
(P5) For all a, b, c ∈ K, ((b' + c)' + ((a + b)' + (a + c))) ∈ T.
(P6) For all a, b ∈ K, if (a' + b) ∈ T and (b' + a) ∈ T, then a = b.

Let Postulate 1.1 be the statement: for all a, b ∈ K, if a ∈ T and (a' + b) ∈ T, then b ∈ T.

Question: Is Postulate 1.1 independent of the postulates (P2)–(P6)? Equivalently, does there exist a system (K, T, +, ') that satisfies (P2)–(P6) but does not satisfy Postulate 1.1?
status_search_result: The question, posed by Huntington as an "unsolved problem," was resolved by exhibiting a concrete model (K, T, +, ') satisfying postulates (P2)–(P6) while violating Postulate 1.1, thereby establishing the independence of Postulate 1.1. The result is reported as a theorem stating that Postulate 1.1 fails to hold in the constructed system.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: In a convex planar magnetic billiard with a strong constant magnetic field, where trajectories are made from short Larmor arcs and total integrability means that the relevant phase space is foliated by invariant graphs carrying action-minimizing orbits, must every totally integrable magnetic billiard be the circular billiard?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a planar magnetic billiard defined as follows. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded strictly convex domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. A constant magnetic field of strength $B>0$ perpendicular to the plane forces a charged particle moving in $\Omega$ to travel along circular Larmor arcs of fixed (small) radius $r = 1/B$; upon hitting $\partial\Omega$ the particle reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) and continues along a new Larmor arc of the same radius. Assume the magnetic field is strong, i.e. $r$ is much smaller than the minimal radius of curvature of $\partial\Omega$, so that every trajectory consists of short Larmor arcs joined by reflections. The associated billiard map acts on a phase space (parametrized, e.g., by the arc-length coordinate on $\partial\Omega$ together with the angle of the outgoing arc). The magnetic billiard is called totally integrable if this phase space is foliated by invariant graphs (continuous sections over $\partial\Omega$) each of which carries action-minimizing orbits of the magnetic billiard.

Question: Must every totally integrable convex planar magnetic billiard with a strong constant magnetic field be a circular billiard (i.e., $\partial\Omega$ a round circle)?
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open question in recent surveys on integrable billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry. Partial results exist: Bialy (2012) proved Hopf-type rigidity showing that magnetic billiards on constant curvature surfaces totally foliated by invariant curves must be circular, and Bialy–Mironov (2020) gave non-integrability/Gutkin-type results for strong magnetic fields. However, the full conjecture that every totally integrable strong-magnetic-field convex billiard is the circle does not appear to be resolved.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: For Newton equations u double prime = -partial V/partial u generated by the time-periodic Lagrangian L = one half times velocity squared minus V(u,t), where V is periodic in both u and t, total integrability on the whole phase space occurs exactly when V is independent of u, while potentials of the form V(nu+mt) are integrable near infinity. Are there any other periodic potentials V for which the system is totally integrable at infinity, meaning for sufficiently large absolute momentum?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Newton's equation
  ü = -∂V/∂u,
where u ∈ ℝⁿ, generated by the Lagrangian
  L(u, u̇, t) = ½|u̇|² − V(u, t),
with V : ℝⁿ × ℝ → ℝ smooth and periodic in each component of u and in t (with respect to some lattice in ℝⁿ × ℝ). The corresponding Hamiltonian system on T*ℝⁿ × ℝ/ℤ is called totally integrable at infinity if there exists R > 0 such that the region {(u, p, t) : |p| ≥ R} is foliated by invariant Lagrangian tori on which the dynamics is conjugate to a linear flow (equivalently, the time-1 map admits a neighborhood of infinity filled by invariant Lagrangian tori homologous to the zero section).

Known cases:
 • V independent of u gives total integrability on the whole phase space.
 • Potentials of the form V(u, t) = W(ν·u + m t) for fixed (ν, m) ∈ ℤⁿ × ℤ are totally integrable at infinity.

Question: Are there any other periodic potentials V(u, t) for which the system is totally integrable at infinity? Equivalently, classify all periodic potentials V whose associated time-periodic Newton system possesses, for sufficiently large momentum, a foliation by invariant Lagrangian tori homologous to the zero section.
status_search_result: For spatial dimension n ≥ 3, Bialy (Calc. Var. PDE, 2016) proved that if a neighborhood of infinity is filled by invariant Lagrangian tori homologous to the zero section then V must be (a function of) the linear combination ν·u + mt — i.e., no new examples beyond the known ones. The statement fails for n = 1, and the n = 2 case remains open.

original_question: Let (N,g) be an orientable closed hyperbolic surface and let D*N be its unit disk cotangent bundle with canonical symplectic form d lambda. Is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity c_HZ(D*N,d lambda) finite?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(N,g)$ be a closed orientable hyperbolic surface, i.e. a closed orientable smooth surface of genus at least two equipped with a Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Using the metric, identify the cotangent bundle $T^*N$ with the tangent bundle, and let
$$D^*N \;=\; \{(q,p)\in T^*N : |p|_g \le 1\}$$
be the unit disk cotangent bundle, equipped with the canonical symplectic form $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the Liouville one-form on $T^*N$.

Recall the Hofer–Zehnder capacity of a (possibly non-compact) symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$: a smooth function $H\colon M\to\mathbb{R}$ is called HZ-admissible if
(i) $H$ is compactly supported in the interior of $M$,
(ii) there exist open subsets $U,V\subset M$ with $U\neq\varnothing$ such that $H\equiv\min H$ on $U$ and $H\equiv\max H$ on $M\setminus V$,
(iii) $0\le H\le\max H$, and
(iv) every non-constant periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian vector field $X_H$ defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega = -dH$ has period strictly greater than $1$.
Then
$$c_{HZ}(M,\omega) \;=\; \sup\{\max H : H \text{ is HZ-admissible}\} \;\in\; [0,\infty].$$

Question. Is $c_{HZ}(D^*N,\, d\lambda) < \infty$?
status_search_result: Finiteness of the Hofer–Zehnder capacity of unit disk cotangent bundles is known under various topological hypotheses (e.g. nonzero Hurewicz map $\pi_2(N)\to H_2(N;\mathbb{Z})$, or $N$ rationally inessential), via work of Irie, Albers–Frauenfelder–Oancea, and others using symplectic homology with local coefficients. Closed orientable hyperbolic surfaces are aspherical with $\pi_2=0$ and are essential, so none of the known criteria apply. Recent literature (including 2023–2024 papers by Bimmermann and collaborators on disc cotangent bundles over surfaces) explicitly notes that finiteness of $c_{HZ}(D^*N)$ for closed orientable surfaces of genus $\ge 2$ remains an open question, while finiteness is known for non-orientable surfaces.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: For Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed symplectic manifolds, if the number of periodic orbits is not finite, is the growth rate of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits at least quadratic, meaning that the lower logarithmic growth of the primitive-periodic-orbit count P(T) is at least 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and let $\varphi\colon M\to M$ be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e. the time-one map of a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian flow on $M$. A periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k\in\mathbb{N}$ is a point $x\in M$ with $\varphi^{k}(x)=x$; it is primitive if $k$ is its minimal such period. Two periodic orbits are geometrically distinct if their underlying $\varphi$-orbits in $M$ are disjoint. For $T\geq 1$, let
$$P(T) \;=\; \#\bigl\{\text{geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of }\varphi\text{ with period }\leq T\bigr\},$$
and define the lower logarithmic growth rate
$$\underline{\gamma}(\varphi) \;=\; \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\log P(T)}{\log T}.$$
Question: Suppose that $\varphi$ has infinitely many geometrically distinct periodic orbits. Is it always true that
$$\underline{\gamma}(\varphi) \;\geq\; 2,$$
that is, that the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of $\varphi$ grows at least quadratically in the period?
status_search_result: The question of growth rates of primitive periodic orbits for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms is a well-known open direction beyond the Conley conjecture. Generic results yield only sub-linear growth (e.g., k/log k for primes), and more recent work (such as growth bounds via Floer barcodes) addresses related but distinct quantitative versions. No source confirms a proof or disproof of an unconditional quadratic lower bound on $P(T)$ for general Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with infinitely many periodic orbits, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: For Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of complex projective space CP^n, does the quadratic lower bound for the growth of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits hold whenever there are infinitely many periodic orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\mathbb{CP}^n, \omega_{\mathrm{FS}})$ denote complex projective space equipped with the Fubini–Study symplectic form. A Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi \in \mathrm{Ham}(\mathbb{CP}^n, \omega_{\mathrm{FS}})$ is the time-one map of a (time-dependent) Hamiltonian flow generated by some smooth $H \colon S^1 \times \mathbb{CP}^n \to \mathbb{R}$. A periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k$ is a fixed point of $\varphi^k$; two periodic orbits are geometrically distinct if they are different as subsets of $\mathbb{CP}^n$, and a periodic orbit is called primitive of period $k$ if $k$ is the minimal positive integer for which the corresponding point is fixed by $\varphi^k$. For $T \geq 1$, let
$$N(\varphi, T) \; := \; \#\bigl\{\text{geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of } \varphi \text{ with period} \le T\bigr\}.$$

Prove or disprove: for every $\varphi \in \mathrm{Ham}(\mathbb{CP}^n, \omega_{\mathrm{FS}})$ which has infinitely many geometrically distinct periodic orbits, there exists a constant $c = c(\varphi) > 0$ such that
$$N(\varphi, T) \; \geq \; c\, T^2 \qquad \text{for all sufficiently large } T.$$
status_search_result: Searches on Ginzburg–Gürel and related work on the Conley conjecture and growth of periodic orbits on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ indicate this remains an open problem: while existence of infinitely many periodic orbits (Conley-type results) and various partial growth bounds are known under additional hypotheses (e.g. presence of a hyperbolic fixed point, or for pseudo-rotations), the quadratic lower bound conjecture for $\mathbb{CP}^n$ has not been established in general.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: If a Hamiltonian map on a compact symplectic manifold has an additional fixed point that is not forced by Arnold-Floer theory, such as a hyperbolic fixed point or a non-contractible fixed point, and this extra fixed point forces infinitely many periodic orbits, does the number of primitive periodic orbits necessarily satisfy a quadratic lower growth bound?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) symplectic manifold, and let $\varphi : M \to M$ be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e. the time-one map of a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian flow on $M$. A fixed point $x$ of $\varphi$ is called homologically necessary (or Arnold–Floer forced) if its existence is guaranteed by the Arnold conjecture lower bounds derived from Floer/Morse homology of $M$ (for instance, by the rank of $H_*(M;\mathbb{Q})$ or the sum of Betti numbers). Suppose that $\varphi$ has at least one fixed point in addition to those forced by Arnold–Floer theory — for example, a hyperbolic fixed point, or a non-contractible fixed point (a fixed point whose associated orbit loop is not contractible in $M$) — and assume that the presence of this extra fixed point forces $\varphi$ to possess infinitely many periodic points (i.e. integer $k \geq 1$ and fixed points of $\varphi^k$ giving distinct periodic orbits).

A primitive periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k$ is an orbit $\{x, \varphi(x), \dots, \varphi^{k-1}(x)\}$ where $k$ is the minimal positive integer with $\varphi^k(x) = x$. Let $N(T)$ denote the number of primitive periodic orbits of $\varphi$ of minimal period at most $T$.

Question: Under the hypotheses above, must one have a quadratic lower bound
$$N(T) \geq c\, T^2$$
for some constant $c > 0$ and all sufficiently large $T$?
status_search_result: The question of quadratic growth of the number of primitive periodic orbits of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms forced by an "extra" (non-homologically-necessary) fixed point appears to be open. Results of Ginzburg–Gürel establish that a hyperbolic extra fixed point forces infinitely many periodic orbits on many closed symplectic manifolds, and generic lower bounds of the order $k/\log k$ are known, but a general quadratic lower bound on the count of primitive periodic orbits is conjectural rather than proven.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: Which fiber-wise convex domains in the cotangent bundle of the sphere arise as induced billiard domains W_T associated to convex billiard tables T in Euclidean space?
self_contained_problem:
Let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth, strictly convex, bounded domain (a convex billiard table). The billiard flow on $T$ can be encoded symplectically as follows. Consider the boundary sphere $S^{n-1} = \partial B^n$ of the unit ball and its cotangent bundle $T^*S^{n-1}$ with its canonical symplectic form. To the billiard table $T$ one associates an "induced billiard domain" $W_T \subset T^*S^{n-1}$, defined so that the billiard map of $T$ corresponds to a symplectomorphism of $W_T$ (built from the Gauss/support data of $\partial T$); the resulting domain $W_T$ is fiber-wise convex, meaning that for every $q \in S^{n-1}$ the intersection $W_T \cap T_q^*S^{n-1}$ is a convex subset of the cotangent fiber.

Problem: Characterize precisely which fiber-wise convex domains $W \subset T^*S^{n-1}$ arise as induced billiard domains $W_T$ for some smooth strictly convex bounded domain $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. That is, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a fiber-wise convex domain $W \subset T^*S^{n-1}$ for there to exist a convex billiard table $T \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $W = W_T$.
status_search_result: No published characterization was located. The problem is posed as an open problem in a list of open questions on billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry, and web search did not return a resolution or partial result addressing the characterization of induced billiard domains as fiber-wise convex subsets of $T^*S^{n-1}$.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: Let M be a closed manifold that is not a K(pi,1), let Sigma be a closed connected hypersurface in T*M, and let H be a Hamiltonian for which Sigma is the regular level H^{-1}(c). Is there an epsilon greater than zero such that, for almost every nearby energy value s in (c-epsilon,c+epsilon), the level H^{-1}(s) carries a contractible periodic orbit?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold that is not aspherical (i.e., $M$ is not a $K(\pi,1)$-space, so some higher homotopy group $\pi_k(M)$ with $k\ge 2$ is nontrivial). Equip the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ with its standard symplectic structure $\omega = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the Liouville one-form. Let $\Sigma \subset T^*M$ be a closed connected smooth hypersurface, and let $H \colon T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$ be a smooth Hamiltonian such that $\Sigma = H^{-1}(c)$ is a regular level set for some $c \in \mathbb{R}$. A periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow of $H$ on a level set $H^{-1}(s)$ is called contractible if its underlying loop in $T^*M$ is contractible (equivalently, contractible in $M$ via the projection $T^*M \to M$).

Question: Does there exist $\varepsilon > 0$ such that, for almost every $s \in (c-\varepsilon, c+\varepsilon)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure, the level set $H^{-1}(s)$ carries a contractible periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow of $H$?
status_search_result: The contractible almost-existence problem in cotangent bundles is established in the symplectically aspherical setting (e.g., when $M$ is a $K(\pi,1)$), but for general closed manifolds $M$ that are not $K(\pi,1)$ the existence of contractible periodic orbits on almost every nearby energy level is listed as an open problem in symplectic topology. Search results confirm related results (relative Hofer–Zehnder capacity, noncontractible orbits for non-simply-connected $M$) but do not provide a resolution in the non-aspherical case.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: For generalized tiling billiards in periodic polygonal tilings of the plane with Snell refraction coefficient -1, is there a finite list of generic dynamical archetypes, such as dense behavior in open sets and integrable behavior with periodic or linearly escaping trajectories?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a periodic polygonal tiling of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, in which the plane is partitioned into polygonal cells whose collection is invariant under a lattice $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of translations. A generalized tiling billiard trajectory is a piecewise-linear oriented curve in $\mathbb{R}^2$ that moves along straight segments inside each cell and, upon crossing an edge $e$ shared by two adjacent cells, refracts according to Snell's law with refraction coefficient $-1$: if $\theta$ is the angle that the incoming segment makes with $e$, the outgoing segment makes angle $-\theta$ with $e$ (equivalently, the refracted ray is the reflection of the incoming ray with respect to the edge $e$, but continuing into the neighboring cell rather than bouncing back).

A trajectory is called:
- periodic if it is a closed curve;
- linearly escaping (drift-periodic) if it is invariant under a non-trivial translation of $\Lambda$ and escapes to infinity;
- dense in an open set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ if its closure contains $U$.

Call a "generic dynamical archetype" for a given periodic polygonal tiling a qualitative description of the asymptotic behavior of trajectories that holds for a full-measure (or otherwise generic) set of initial conditions; examples include "every generic trajectory is periodic", "every generic trajectory is linearly escaping", or "the closure of a generic trajectory contains an open set".

Question: As the periodic polygonal tiling of the plane varies over all such tilings, does the collection of generic dynamical archetypes that occur for generalized tiling billiards with Snell refraction coefficient $-1$ form a finite list?
status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) on generalized tiling billiards in cyclic polygons and wind-tree variants establish dynamical results for specific tiling families (triangles, cyclic quadrilaterals) but explicitly note that a general theory is lacking. No source indicates a proven finite classification of generic dynamical archetypes for arbitrary periodic polygonal tilings, so the problem appears open.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: For brick tiling billiards in which every other row of a square tiling is shifted by a parameter theta, determine the dynamics when theta is irrational, since rational theta gives periodicity of all orbits.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the tiling of the plane by unit squares arranged so that the squares in every other horizontal row are translated horizontally by a fixed parameter θ ∈ [0,1) (a "brick tiling" with offset θ). A tiling billiard trajectory is the piecewise-linear path of a point particle that travels in straight lines inside each tile and, upon crossing an edge between two adjacent tiles, refracts according to the law of negative refraction (the reflected direction is the reflection of the incoming direction across the edge being crossed, so the trajectory crosses the edge with the angle of incidence equal to the angle of refraction but on the opposite side of the normal).

It is known that when θ ∈ ℚ, every (nonsingular) trajectory of this billiard system is periodic (in fact, with a uniform bound on the period depending on the denominator of θ).

Problem: Determine the dynamical behavior of tiling billiard trajectories on the brick tiling with shift parameter θ when θ is irrational. In particular, describe whether trajectories are periodic, drift-periodic, bounded, escaping, recurrent, equidistributed, etc., and identify the underlying dynamical structure (e.g. interval exchange, rotation, or otherwise) governing their long-term behavior.
status_search_result: Recent work (S. Park, M.A. thesis, University of Maine, 2025) treats brick tiling billiards with rational offset p/q, proving every nonsingular trajectory is periodic or drift-periodic with period at most 4|2q−1|. No publication located that resolves the dynamics for irrational θ; the irrational case appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: Find real-world systems from areas such as physics, mechanics, biology, or economics that can be modeled as locally conformal symplectic flows or maps, where the symplectic structure is locally rescaled and may encode non-uniform or spatially varying dissipation.
self_contained_problem:
A locally conformal symplectic (LCS) structure on a smooth manifold $M^{2n}$ is a non-degenerate 2-form $\omega$ together with a closed 1-form $\eta$ (the Lee form) satisfying $d\omega = \eta \wedge \omega$. Equivalently, $M$ is covered by open sets $U_\alpha$ on each of which $\omega|_{U_\alpha} = e^{f_\alpha}\omega_\alpha$ for some smooth function $f_\alpha$ and some genuine symplectic form $\omega_\alpha$, with the conformal factors patched together by the cohomology class of $\eta$. An LCS flow (respectively LCS map) is a smooth flow (respectively diffeomorphism) preserving the LCS structure up to local conformal rescaling; infinitesimally, this allows non-uniform, spatially varying contraction or expansion of phase-space volume, generalizing the uniform dissipation rate of conformal (globally conformal) symplectic systems.

Problem. Identify and describe concrete real-world dynamical systems — drawn from physics (e.g., mechanics with non-uniform friction, electromagnetic or acoustic media with spatially varying damping, thermodynamic systems), biology (e.g., population or neural dynamics with heterogeneous dissipation), or economics (e.g., market models with state-dependent damping) — whose continuous-time or discrete-time evolution is naturally modeled by an LCS flow or LCS map with a non-exact Lee form $\eta$. In particular, exhibit explicit choices of $(M,\omega,\eta)$ and the generating Hamiltonian (or diffeomorphism) for which the local conformal factor genuinely depends on the phase-space point, so that the model cannot be reduced to a globally conformal symplectic system.
status_search_result: The literature contains examples of (globally) conformal symplectic and conformal Hamiltonian systems modeling uniform dissipation — e.g., the Duffing oscillator, damped acoustic waves, and certain optimization dynamics — but no canonical real-world models requiring the strictly locally (non-globally) conformal symplectic setting with a non-exact Lee form have been identified in the searched sources. The question of finding such concrete applied models therefore appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: In the simplified locally conformal symplectic cotangent-bundle equations for a Tonelli Hamiltonian with eta pulled back from the base, what is the physical interpretation of the force term proportional to minus the Lagrangian times the eta one-form?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $T^*M$ denote its cotangent bundle, equipped with the canonical symplectic form $\omega_0 = d\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the tautological one-form. Let $\pi : T^*M \to M$ be the projection, and let $\eta$ be a closed one-form on $M$, whose pullback to $T^*M$ we also denote by $\eta$. The pair $(T^*M, \omega_0)$ together with $\eta$ defines a locally conformal symplectic (LCS) structure via the Lichnerowicz differential $d_\eta \alpha := d\alpha + \eta \wedge \alpha$. For a smooth function $H : T^*M \to \mathbb{R}$, the LCS Hamiltonian vector field $X_H$ is defined by $\iota_{X_H} \omega_0 = -d_\eta H$.

Assume that $H$ is a Tonelli Hamiltonian, i.e. $H$ is $C^2$, fiberwise strictly convex, and superlinear in the fibers of $T^*M$. Let $L : TM \to \mathbb{R}$ be the Legendre-dual Tonelli Lagrangian of $H$. paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: For a closed immersed submanifold M of Euclidean space, define a generalized n-periodic billiard trajectory as an n-gon inscribed in M that is an extremal of perimeter. What lower bounds, in terms of the topology of M and of the immersion, can be proved for the number of such generalized periodic trajectories?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a closed immersed smooth submanifold of Euclidean space. For an integer $n \geq 2$, define a generalized $n$-periodic billiard trajectory inscribed in $M$ to be an ordered $n$-tuple of points $(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ on $M$ (an inscribed $n$-gon) that is a critical point of the perimeter functional
$$L(x_1, \dots, x_n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \|x_{i+1} - x_i\|, \qquad x_{n+1} := x_1,$$
where the variation is taken along the submanifold $M$ at each vertex. (Equivalently, at each vertex $x_i$ the difference of the unit vectors pointing to the neighboring vertices is normal to $M$ at $x_i$.)

Two such trajectories are identified if they differ by a cyclic permutation or reversal of their vertices.

Problem. Establish lower bounds, in terms of the topology of $M$ and of its immersion into $\mathbb{R}^N$ (e.g., dimension, codimension, homology, characteristic numbers), for the number of geometrically distinct generalized $n$-periodic billiard trajectories inscribed in $M$.
status_search_result: For the classical case where $M$ is a smooth closed convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^d$, lower bounds on the number of $n$-periodic (Euclidean and Finsler) billiard trajectories are known: for prime $n$ one has at least $(d-2)(n-1)+2$ geometrically distinct trajectories, with stronger estimates in general position. Extensions exist for outer/symplectic billiards on submanifolds. However, the general problem of lower bounds for arbitrary closed immersed submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Euclidean space remains open, with only partial results in special cases.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: Do chaotic symplectic billiards exist in convex domains with C^1-smooth boundary?
self_contained_problem:
Symplectic billiards are defined as follows. Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex domain whose boundary $\partial D$ is a $C^1$ curve. For an ordered pair of points $(x, y) \in \partial D \times \partial D$ with $x \neq y$, the symplectic billiard map $T$ sends $(x, y)$ to $(y, z)$, where $z \in \partial D$ is the unique point such that the tangent line to $\partial D$ at $y$ is parallel to the chord $xz$ (equivalently, $z$ is characterized by maximizing/critical-value of the area functional $A(x,y,z) = \tfrac12\,\omega(z-x, y)$, where $\omega$ is the standard symplectic (area) form on $\mathbb{R}^2$). This map preserves the measure $\omega \wedge \omega$ on $\partial D \times \partial D$.

The symplectic billiard dynamical system $(T, \mu)$ is called chaotic if it has positive metric entropy with respect to its invariant measure (equivalently, a positive-measure set of orbits has a positive Lyapunov exponent).

Question: Does there exist a bounded convex domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$-smooth boundary such that the associated symplectic billiard map is chaotic?
status_search_result: The question appears in a recent compilation of open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry (2025/2026), where it is listed as open. Numerical evidence is mentioned suggesting the stadium as a candidate, but no proof of existence (or nonexistence) of chaotic symplectic billiards in convex $C^1$ domains has been published.

original_question: In a smooth Euclidean billiard domain with a generic point source of light, after optical reflection at the boundary, does the time-t wave front become dense in the domain as t tends to infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, considered as a billiard table: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $\Omega$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting $\partial\Omega$. Fix a point $p \in \Omega$ and consider the family of all unit-speed billiard trajectories emanating from $p$ in every direction; the time-$t$ wave front $W_t(p) \subset \overline{\Omega}$ is the set of points reached at time exactly $t$ along these trajectories (that is, points whose billiard distance from $p$, measured along a trajectory that has undergone the prescribed sequence of reflections, equals $t$). 

Question: For a generic choice of $\Omega$ (smooth Euclidean billiard domain) and generic choice of point source $p \in \Omega$, does the wave front $W_t(p)$ become dense in $\Omega$ as $t \to \infty$? Equivalently, is it true that for every nonempty open set $U \subset \Omega$ there exists $T$ such that $W_t(p) \cap U \neq \emptyset$ for all $t \geq T$?

No source was found resolving the general case.

paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
original_question: When a smooth oval is approximated by n-gons and the quality of approximation is measured by the area of the symmetric difference between the oval and the polygon, is the resulting optimal-approximation function of n related to a billiard-type dynamical system?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex compact set (a "smooth oval") with $C^\infty$ boundary $\partial K$. For each integer $n \geq 3$, define
$$\delta(n; K) \;=\; \inf_{P}\, \mathrm{Area}\bigl( (K \setminus P) \cup (P \setminus K) \bigr),$$
where the infimum is taken over all (not necessarily inscribed or circumscribed) convex polygons $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with at most $n$ vertices, and $\mathrm{Area}$ denotes Lebesgue measure of the symmetric difference between $K$ and $P$.

Question: Is the function $n \mapsto \delta(n; K)$, together with the geometry of the optimal approximating $n$-gons (e.g.\ their vertex configurations as $n$ varies), governed by — or naturally identifiable with — the orbits / invariants of some billiard-like dynamical system associated with the oval $K$ (for instance an outer/inner/symplectic billiard map, or a comparable map on $\partial K$ or on chords of $K$)? Equivalently, exhibit such a dynamical system that produces the optimal $n$-gons and the asymptotic behavior of $\delta(n; K)$, or prove that no such billiard-type description exists.

However, no source identified in the search establishes (or refutes) a precise correspondence between the optimal $n$-gon sequence and a billiard-type dynamical system on the oval. The question, posed as an open problem on quantitative symplectic geometry / billiards, does not appear to have been resolved in the literature.

paper_title: On an unsolved problem from the theory of Boolean algebras
original_question: Let A be a set and let S(A) denote the Boolean algebra of all subsets of A. A principal ideal of S(A) is the ideal consisting of all subsets of one fixed subset X of A. Suppose A has cardinality less than the first aleph inaccessible in the weak sense, with the parallel strict-sense variant stated in the source. Is every sigma-ideal I of S(A) for which the quotient Boolean algebra S(A)/I is complete necessarily principal?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a nonempty set and let $S(A)$ denote the Boolean algebra $(\mathcal{P}(A), \cup, \cap, \setminus, \emptyset, A)$ of all subsets of $A$. An ideal $I \subseteq S(A)$ is called a $\sigma$-ideal if it is closed under countable unions, i.e. whenever $\{X_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq I$ one has $\bigcup_n X_n \in I$. An ideal $I$ is called principal if there exists a fixed subset $X_0 \subseteq A$ such that $I = \{Y \subseteq A : Y \subseteq X_0\}$. The quotient Boolean algebra $S(A)/I$ is called complete if every subset of $S(A)/I$ has a supremum in $S(A)/I$.

Recall that an uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ is weakly inaccessible if it is a regular limit cardinal, and strongly inaccessible if in addition $2^\lambda < \kappa$ for every $\lambda < \kappa$. Let $\aleph^w$ denote the least weakly inaccessible cardinal and $\aleph^s$ the least strongly inaccessible cardinal (each treated as $\infty$ if none exists).

Question: Assume $|A| < \aleph^w$ (respectively $|A| < \aleph^s$). Is it true that every $\sigma$-ideal $I$ of $S(A)$ for which the quotient $S(A)/I$ is a complete Boolean algebra must be a principal ideal?
status_search_result: The problem is classically connected to Ulam's work on measurable cardinals. The existence of a non-principal σ-ideal $I$ on a set $A$ with $S(A)/I$ complete is equivalent to the existence of a measurable cardinal $\le |A|$ (Tarski; via the theory of two-valued measurable cardinals). Since every measurable cardinal is (strongly, hence weakly) inaccessible, the assumption $|A| < \aleph^w$ (or $|A| < \aleph^s$) forces $|A|$ to be below the least measurable cardinal, and therefore every such σ-ideal is principal. Thus the question has an affirmative answer under the stated cardinality hypothesis.

paper_title: An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2
original_question: Does there exist a positive real number alpha such that, for every integer n greater than or equal to 0, if alpha times (3/2)^n is written as g_n + r_n with g_n the greatest integer not greater than alpha times (3/2)^n and r_n its fractional part, then 0 <= r_n < 1/2? Equivalently, do any Z-numbers exist for the base 3/2 and the half-interval [0, 1/2)?
self_contained_problem: For a positive real number $\alpha$ and a non-negative integer $n$, write $\alpha\,(3/2)^n = g_n + r_n$, where $g_n = \lfloor \alpha\,(3/2)^n \rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $\alpha\,(3/2)^n$ and $r_n = \{\alpha\,(3/2)^n\} \in [0,1)$ is its fractional part. Call $\alpha$ a $Z$-number if $0 \le r_n < 1/2$ for every integer $n \ge 0$. Does there exist any $Z$-number, i.e., does there exist a positive real $\alpha$ such that the fractional part of $\alpha\,(3/2)^n$ lies in $[0,1/2)$ for all $n \ge 0$?
status_search_result: Mahler's 3/2 problem on the existence of Z-numbers remains open. Mahler (1968) conjectured no Z-numbers exist. Partial results exist (e.g., Flatto–Lagarias–Pollington bounds on the discrepancy function, and a 2024 preprint resolving a restricted integer version), but the general existence question is unresolved.

paper_title: An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2
original_question: For sequences alpha times (3/2)^n with alpha a positive real number and n = 0, 1, 2, ..., can a theory analogous to the theory developed by Mahler for fractional parts lying in [0, 1/2) be established when the fractional parts are required to lie in subintervals of [0, 1) whose length is smaller than 1/2, possibly even arbitrarily small?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive real number $\alpha$ and a nonnegative integer $n$, let $\{\alpha(3/2)^n\}$ denote the fractional part of $\alpha(3/2)^n$. It is known (after Mahler) that one can develop a substantive theory describing the set of $\alpha>0$ for which $\{\alpha(3/2)^n\}\in[0,1/2)$ holds for every $n=0,1,2,\dots$ (so-called $Z$-numbers); in particular, the set of such $\alpha$ in any interval $[N,N+1)$ with $N$ a positive integer is finite, and quantitative bounds on its cardinality are available.

Develop an analogous theory in which the target interval $[0,1/2)$ is replaced by a subinterval $I\subset[0,1)$ of length $\ell<1/2$, and in particular for $\ell$ arbitrarily small. That is, for an interval $I\subset[0,1)$ with $|I|<1/2$, study the set
$$S_I=\{\alpha>0:\{\alpha(3/2)^n\}\in I\text{ for all }n=0,1,2,\dots\},$$
and establish structural and quantitative results (finiteness in bounded intervals, density bounds, existence/non-existence statements) parallel to those known in the case $I=[0,1/2)$.
status_search_result: The general problem (Mahler's 3/2 problem) remains open, and even the existence of Z-numbers is unresolved. However, partial analogues for smaller target intervals have been established: Flatto–Lagarias–Pollington proved that for any real ξ≠0 and coprime integers p>q>1, the fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n} cannot all lie in an interval of length strictly less than 1/p (giving 1/3 for 3/2); Dubickas and others have sharpened these results, exhibiting forbidden subintervals and quantitative bounds. A fully analogous theory for arbitrarily small intervals is not established.

paper_title: An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2
original_question: For coprime integers p and q satisfying p > q >= 2, and for a positive real number alpha, what analogous questions and theory can be developed for the fractional parts of the products alpha times (p/q)^n for n = 0, 1, 2, ...?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ and $q$ be coprime integers with $p > q \geq 2$, and let $\alpha$ be a positive real number. Consider the sequence of fractional parts
$$\{\alpha (p/q)^n\}, \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots,$$
where $\{x\} = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$. Develop a theory analogous to the classical case $(p,q) = (3,2)$ for this sequence. In particular, address the following questions:

(a) For which $\alpha > 0$ is the sequence $\{\alpha (p/q)^n\}$ equidistributed modulo $1$?

(b) Define $\Omega(p/q) = \inf_{\alpha > 0}\left(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\{\alpha (p/q)^n\} - \liminf_{n\to\infty}\{\alpha (p/q)^n\}\right)$. Determine or bound $\Omega(p/q)$.

(c) Does there exist a positive real number $\alpha$ such that $\{\alpha (p/q)^n\} < 1/q$ for all $n \geq 0$ (a "$(p/q)$-analogue" of a $Z$-number)? More generally, for which subintervals $I \subset [0,1)$ of length less than $1$ does there exist $\alpha > 0$ with $\{\alpha (p/q)^n\} \in I$ for every $n$?

(d) Describe the set of $\alpha > 0$ for which the orbit $\{\alpha(p/q)^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ avoids a prescribed subinterval of $[0,1)$.

paper_title: Logical connections between some open problems concerning nil rings
original_question: Suppose a ring R contains a one-sided nil ideal A. Must A be contained in a two-sided nil ideal of R?
self_contained_problem:
Let R be an associative ring (not assumed to have a unit). A subset S of R is called nil if every element of S is nilpotent, i.e. for each s ∈ S there exists a positive integer n (depending on s) such that s^n = 0. A one-sided ideal of R means a left ideal or a right ideal of R; a two-sided ideal means an ideal that is both a left and a right ideal.

Suppose that R contains a one-sided nil ideal A (that is, A is a left ideal or a right ideal of R, and every element of A is nilpotent). Must there exist a two-sided ideal B of R such that B is nil and A ⊆ B?
category_tag: Köthe conjecture / nil ideals in rings
status_search_result: This is Köthe's conjecture (posed by G. Köthe in 1930), which is equivalent to the question of whether every one-sided nil ideal of a ring is contained in a two-sided nil ideal. It remains open in general as of 2026, though it is known to hold for several classes of rings (e.g., PI rings, right Noetherian rings). A related conjecture of Amitsur on nil polynomial rings was disproved by Smoktunowicz, but the original Köthe conjecture itself is still unresolved.

paper_title: Logical connections between some open problems concerning nil rings
original_question: If R is a nil ring, must the polynomial ring R[x] also be a nil ring?
self_contained_problem:
A ring R (not necessarily with unit) is called nil if every element of R is nilpotent, i.e., for each r ∈ R there exists a positive integer n (depending on r) such that r^n = 0. Given a nil ring R, the polynomial ring R[x] is the ring of polynomials in one commuting indeterminate x with coefficients in R, with the usual addition and multiplication.

Question: Must R[x] be a nil ring whenever R is a nil ring? Equivalently, is it true that for every nil ring R and every polynomial f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + ⋯ + a_k x^k ∈ R[x], there exists a positive integer n with f(x)^n = 0 in R[x]?

paper_title: Logical connections between some open problems concerning nil rings
context_brief: Finitely generated radical weakly nil rings
original_question: If R is a finitely generated radical ring in Jacobson's sense that is also weakly nil, must R be a nil ring? Here weakly nil means that there exists a multiplicatively closed subset S of nilpotent elements of R such that every element of R is a finite sum of elements of S.
self_contained_problem:
Call a (not necessarily unital, associative) ring $R$ weakly nil if there exists a multiplicatively closed subset $S$ of $R$, all of whose elements are nilpotent, such that every element of $R$ can be written as a finite sum of elements of $S$. Recall that $R$ is a radical ring in Jacobson's sense if $R$ coincides with its Jacobson radical, equivalently, if for every $a\in R$ there exists $b\in R$ with $a+b+ab=a+b+ba=0$ (so that $1+a$ is invertible in any unitalization). A ring $R$ is nil if every element of $R$ is nilpotent.

Question: If $R$ is a finitely generated radical ring (in Jacobson's sense) that is weakly nil, must $R$ be a nil ring?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source establishing a resolution of this specific question about finitely generated radical weakly nil rings. The problem is listed among open problems related to nil rings (and connected in spirit to the Köthe conjecture), and no published solution was located.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
original_question: Assume that a natural λ-structure has been constructed on K'(X). For a proper morphism f:X→Y of complete intersection type, and more generally for a relative scheme X over a locally ringed topos Y satisfying the corresponding relative hypotheses, can one prove a Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch formula without projectivity assumptions, using the Todd class of f defined from the relative cotangent complex T_f? Can the same ideas also prove the analogous formula for complex analytic or rigid-analytic spaces, beyond the then-known case of a locally free sheaf on a nonsingular compact complex variety over a point?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let f: X → Y be a proper morphism of locally complete intersection type between (suitable) schemes (or, more generally, let X be a relative scheme over a locally ringed topos Y satisfying analogous relative hypotheses). Assume that on the K-theory groups K'(X) of coherent sheaves there is a natural λ-ring structure, and let T_f denote the relative cotangent complex of f. Define the Todd class Td(T_f) of f by means of this relative cotangent complex (via the usual formal series in its Chern classes).

Problem.
(a) Prove a Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch formula of the form
    ch(f_* α) = f_*(ch(α) · Td(T_f))
for every α ∈ K'(X), without assuming that f is projective (i.e., not requiring a factorization through a projective bundle or any global immersion into a smooth Y-scheme).

(b) Establish the analogous formula for proper morphisms in the categories of complex analytic spaces and of rigid analytic spaces, going beyond the case of a single locally free sheaf on a nonsingular compact complex variety mapped to a point.
status_search_result: The algebraic part has been substantially advanced: O'Brian–Toledo–Tong (1985) established a Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch formula for proper holomorphic maps of complex manifolds; Navarro & Navarro (2017, "On the Riemann–Roch formula without projective hypothesis") proved GRR for proper maps between smooth schemes via A^1-homotopy techniques; and Navarro proved a Riemann–Roch theorem for homotopy-invariant K-theory and projective lci morphisms between finite-dimensional noetherian schemes, without smoothness. Recent works (e.g., Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch for complex analytic ∞-prestacks, 2026) continue extending the complex/rigid-analytic case. A fully general GRR for arbitrary proper lci morphisms in the relative-topos and rigid-analytic settings as originally envisaged is not uniformly settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
context_brief: proper support instead of proper morphism
original_question: In the finiteness and Riemann-Roch questions for a morphism f and a complex L on X, can the properness hypothesis on f be replaced by the weaker hypothesis that the cohomology sheaves H^i(L) of the complexes under consideration have supports that are proper over Y?
self_contained_problem: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of (locally noetherian) schemes, and let $L$ be a bounded complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules (with coherent or appropriate constructible cohomology). The classical finiteness theorem and Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem for the higher direct images $R^i f_* L$ are typically formulated under the assumption that $f$ is a proper morphism. Investigate whether, in such finiteness statements and in the Riemann–Roch formula relating the Chern character of $Rf_* L$ to that of $L$ (via the Todd class of the relative tangent complex), the hypothesis that $f$ be proper can be weakened to the following condition: for every $i$, the support of the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal{H}^i(L)$ is proper over $Y$ (i.e., the restriction of $f$ to $\mathrm{Supp}\,\mathcal{H}^i(L)$ is a proper morphism to $Y$). Formulate and prove (or disprove) the resulting finiteness and Riemann–Roch theorems under this weaker "proper support" hypothesis in place of properness of $f$.
category_tag: Riemann-Roch and finiteness for non-proper morphisms
status_search_result: The problem, a remark in Grothendieck's list of open problems in intersection theory, asks for an extension of finiteness and Riemann–Roch theorems to morphisms that are merely "proper on supports." Such generalizations are known in various settings (e.g., for coherent sheaves with proper support, Riemann–Roch for proper-support derived categories has been developed by various authors), but a definitive, all-encompassing answer to Grothendieck's original formulation could not be confirmed via search.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
context_brief: integral comparison of Chow and K-theory gradeds
original_question: For a smooth quasi-projective scheme X over a field, let A(X) be the Chow ring, let Gr'_top(X) be the graded ring associated with the topological filtration by codimension of supports on K'(X), and let Gr'(X) be the graded ring associated with the λ-filtration. Are the comparison formulas between A(X), Gr'_top(X), and Gr'(X) true integrally, not merely modulo torsion? Equivalently, are the formulas labeled (4.4) and (4.5), relating the maps φ:A(X)→Gr'_top(X) and ψ:Gr'_top(X)→A(X), valid exactly rather than only modulo torsion, so that in particular φ^2:A^2(X)→Gr'_top^2(X) is an isomorphism? Later notes in the source report that the relevant formulas were established without neglecting torsion by Mumford and Jouanolou.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective scheme over a field. Denote by $A(X) =  igoplus_p A^p(X)$ the Chow ring of cycles modulo rational equivalence, graded by codimension. Let $K'(X) = K_0'(X)$ be the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves on $X$ (which, by smoothness, coincides with $K_0(X)$ and is a ring). Equip $K'(X)$ with two decreasing filtrations:

(i) the topological filtration by codimension of supports, $F^p_{\mathrm{top}} K'(X)$, generated by classes of coherent sheaves whose support has codimension $\geq p$, with associated graded ring $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$;

(ii) the $\lambda$-filtration (Grothendieck's $\gamma$-filtration) $F^p_\gamma K'(X)$, with associated graded ring $\mathrm{Gr}'(X)$.

There are natural ring homomorphisms
$$\varphi : A(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X), \qquad \psi : \mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X) \longrightarrow A(X),$$
whose compositions in either order equal multiplication by an integer factor (built from $(p-1)!$ in codimension $p$) modulo torsion, in the standard comparison formulas linking $A(X)$, $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$, and $\mathrm{Gr}'(X)$.

Question: Do these comparison formulas relating $\varphi$ and $\psi$ hold exactly (integrally), and not merely modulo torsion? In particular, is the map
$$\varphi^2 : A^2(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}'^{\,2}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$$
an isomorphism for every smooth quasi-projective $X$ (including, e.g., the case $\dim X = 3$)?
status_search_result: The integral form of the comparison formulas between the Chow ring and the graded of $K'(X)$ for the topological and $\lambda$-filtrations was established by Jouanolou (and, in the surface/threefold setting, by Mumford), removing the "modulo torsion" caveat. In particular $\varphi^2 : A^2(X) \to \mathrm{Gr}'^{\,2}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$ is known to be an isomorphism. The result is now standard and appears in the literature on Riemann–Roch and the $\gamma$-filtration.
