paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
original_question: Let G be a semi-simple simply connected algebraic group over the complex numbers and consider the natural homomorphism from the Chow ring A(G) to the integral cohomology H^*(G(C),Z) of the associated compact complex manifold. Is this homomorphism injective? More generally, when G has torsion, does this map detect the positive-degree part of A(G) in the way suggested by the comparison with torsion primes of G(C)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a semi-simple, simply connected linear algebraic group over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$, and let $G(\mathbb{C})$ denote its associated compact (real) Lie group (equivalently, the underlying complex manifold endowed with its classical topology). Let $A(G) = \bigoplus_{i\ge 0} A^i(G)$ denote the Chow ring of $G$ (the ring of algebraic cycles on $G$ modulo rational equivalence), and let $H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}), \mathbb{Z})$ denote its integral singular cohomology ring. There is a natural cycle-class ring homomorphism
$$ \mathrm{cl} : A(G) \longrightarrow H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}), \mathbb{Z}), $$
which doubles degrees ($A^i(G) \to H^{2i}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$).

(1) Is the homomorphism $\mathrm{cl}$ injective for every such $G$?

(2) More precisely, let $A^{+}(G) = \bigoplus_{i>0} A^i(G)$. It is known that the torsion primes of $G(\mathbb{C})$ (the primes $p$ for which $H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$ has $p$-torsion) are exactly the primes dividing the order of the finite group $A^{+}(G)$. Does the cycle map $\mathrm{cl}$ in fact detect $A^{+}(G)$ in a manner compatible with this coincidence of torsion primes — for instance, is $\mathrm{cl}$ restricted to $A^{+}(G)$ injective?

As a known partial fact one may use: for $G = G_2$ over $\mathbb{C}$, the cycle map $\mathrm{cl}$ is non-zero in positive degrees.
status_search_result: A direct affirmative or negative resolution of the injectivity of the cycle class map $A(G)\to H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$ for all semi-simple simply connected complex algebraic groups was not located. Related work (Totaro, Pandharipande, Yagita, Gu, and others) computes Chow rings of classifying spaces $BG$ and exceptional groups and shows interesting torsion phenomena, but a definitive published statement settling the conjecture for $G$ itself in full generality could not be confirmed from the search.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
context_brief: comparison from Gr' to Chow and topology
original_question: When X is smooth and quasi-projective over a field, does there exist a ring homomorphism g:Gr'(X)→A(X) to the Chow ring that sends Chern classes in Gr'(X) to the corresponding Chow-theoretic Chern classes? Does the analogous problem also have a solution for a compact topological space X, namely a ring homomorphism from Gr'(X), the graded ring of K'(X) for the λ-filtration, to H^{2*}(X,Z) that sends Chern classes to ordinary integral Chern classes?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth quasi-projective variety over a field k. Denote by K'(X) = K_0(X) the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves (equivalently, of locally free sheaves, since X is smooth), endowed with its natural ring structure and with the λ-ring structure given by exterior powers. Let F^•K'(X) be the associated γ-filtration (equivalently, the Chern filtration), and set
   Gr'(X) := ⊕_{p≥0} F^p K'(X) / F^{p+1} K'(X),
the associated graded ring. For each vector bundle E on X and each integer p ≥ 0, one has Chern classes c_p^{K}(E) ∈ Gr'(X) defined via the λ-operations. Let A(X) = ⊕_p A^p(X) denote the Chow ring of X (cycles modulo rational equivalence with the intersection product), and let c_p(E) ∈ A^p(X) denote the Chow-theoretic Chern classes.

(a) Does there exist a graded ring homomorphism
        g : Gr'(X) ⟶ A(X)
that sends c_p^{K}(E) to c_p(E) for every vector bundle E on X and every p ≥ 0?

(b) (Topological analogue.) Let X be a compact topological space. Let K'(X) be the topological K-theory ring, equipped with its λ-operations and γ-filtration, and let Gr'(X) be the associated graded ring, with Chern classes c_p^{K}(E) ∈ Gr'(X) for each complex vector bundle E on X. Does there exist a graded ring homomorphism
        Gr'(X) ⟶ H^{2*}(X, ℤ) = ⊕_p H^{2p}(X, ℤ)
sending c_p^{K}(E) to the ordinary integral Chern class c_p(E) ∈ H^{2p}(X, ℤ) for every complex vector bundle E on X?
status_search_result: Rationally, the comparison maps are isomorphisms via the Chern character / Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch. Integrally, the relationship between the γ-filtration on K-theory and the Chow ring (resp. integral cohomology in the topological case) is delicate: it is known that the associated graded for the γ-filtration is in general only related to CH(X) by a surjection up to torsion, and recent works (e.g. Karpenko–Merkurjev on Chow filtrations on representation rings, Yagita's notes on filtrations of K-theory, Totaro's work on Chow rings of classifying spaces) show that the existence of a natural integral ring map Gr_γ K(X) → CH(X) sending Chern classes to Chern classes does not hold in full generality and depends on subtle conditions (e.g. whether the E_∞-page of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence is generated by Chern classes). The precise question as posed by Grothendieck for arbitrary smooth quasi-projective X (and for arbitrary compact spaces) does not appear to be resolved by a definitive yes/no in the literature found.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
original_question: If no regularity hypothesis is imposed on Y, even when X and Y are of finite type over the complex numbers and f:X→Y is a regular immersion of codimension 1, can one nevertheless construct a cohomological Gysin homomorphism with reasonable properties, in particular one that makes the Riemann-Roch comparison square (6.3) commute?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a regular closed immersion of codimension $1$ between schemes of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. Assume no regularity (smoothness or non-singularity) hypothesis on $Y$. 

Recall that for $f$ a regular immersion between smooth varieties one has a cohomological Gysin homomorphism
$$f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}} : H^{*}(X) \longrightarrow H^{*+2}(Y)$$
(where $H^{*}$ denotes a suitable cohomology theory, e.g. singular cohomology of the associated analytic space, or $\ell$-adic/Betti/Hodge cohomology), and a $K$-theoretic Gysin homomorphism
$$f^{!}_{K} : K_{0}(X) \longrightarrow K_{0}(Y),$$
related to one another, via the Chern character $\mathrm{ch}$ and the Todd class, by a commutative Riemann–Roch comparison square
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
K_{0}(X) & \xrightarrow{\;f^{!}_{K}\;} & K_{0}(Y) \\
\downarrow{\scriptstyle \mathrm{ch}(-)\cdot \mathrm{Td}(X)} & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle \mathrm{ch}(-)\cdot \mathrm{Td}(Y)} \\
H^{*}(X) & \xrightarrow{\;f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}}\;} & H^{*+2}(Y).
\end{array}
$$

Question: When $Y$ is allowed to be singular (only of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$), can one construct a cohomological Gysin homomorphism $f^{!}_{\mathrm{coh}}$ with reasonable functorial properties such that the above Riemann–Roch comparison square remains commutative? Equivalently, give a plausible definition of such a homomorphism, or prove that no such well-behaved construction can exist.
status_search_result: Modern developments (notably work on Gysin morphisms for regular immersions in motivic homotopy theory, including extensions of Gabber's construction, and Riemann–Roch results for homotopy invariant K-theory and projective local complete intersection morphisms over noetherian schemes without smoothness assumptions) provide partial cohomological Gysin maps for regular immersions allowing singular targets. However, it is not clear from publicly available sources that the specific question — producing a cohomological Gysin homomorphism on classical cohomology of singular complex varieties making the explicit Riemann–Roch comparison square commute for codimension-1 regular immersions into arbitrary singular targets — has been settled in the form originally posed. Status is best classified as unknown.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
context_brief: mod-2 product independence for divisor intersections
original_question: Let Y be a singular projective scheme of dimension 4, and let X be a closed one-dimensional subscheme that is globally the intersection of three positive divisors D_1, D_2, and D_3. Is the element c_1(D_1)c_1(D_2)c_1(D_3) in H^6(Y,Z/2Z), obtained as the product of their mod-2 Chern classes, independent of the particular choice of the divisors D_i whose intersection is X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Y$ be a (possibly singular) projective scheme of dimension $4$ over an algebraically closed field, and let $X \subset Y$ be a closed subscheme of dimension $1$. Suppose that $X$ can be written globally as a scheme-theoretic intersection $X = D_1 \cap D_2 \cap D_3$ of three effective (positive) Cartier divisors $D_1, D_2, D_3$ on $Y$. For each such divisor $D_i$, let $c_1(D_i) \in H^2(Y, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ denote its mod-$2$ first Chern class (in a suitable cohomology theory such as étale cohomology), and consider the cup product
$$c_1(D_1)\, c_1(D_2)\, c_1(D_3) \in H^6(Y, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}).$$
Question: Is this element of $H^6(Y, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ independent of the particular choice of effective divisors $D_1, D_2, D_3$ whose intersection equals $X$? That is, if $D_1', D_2', D_3'$ is another triple of effective Cartier divisors with $D_1' \cap D_2' \cap D_3' = X$, does one have
$$c_1(D_1)\, c_1(D_2)\, c_1(D_3) = c_1(D_1')\, c_1(D_2')\, c_1(D_3')$$
in $H^6(Y, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$?
category_tag: mod-2 Chern classes and intersection theory
status_search_result: No specific published resolution of this particular mod-2 independence question for triple divisor intersections on a singular 4-dimensional projective scheme was located. The question appears in a classical list of open problems in intersection theory and its current status could not be verified from available sources.

paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
original_question: Let Y be a closed subset of X and let L be a perfect complex on X whose restriction to X−Y is zero in the derived-category sense, so that the cohomology sheaves of L are supported on Y. Can one define Chern classes with support in Y, c_i^Y(L), lying in cohomology with support H_Y^{2i}(X,Z_ℓ(i)) or in the corresponding ordinary cohomology with support, so that their images under the canonical map to ordinary cohomology recover the general Chern classes of perfect complexes? Can these supported Chern classes be used in a proof or strengthened formulation of cohomological Riemann-Roch, with or without denominators?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a noetherian scheme (or a sufficiently nice algebraic variety/scheme on which étale cohomology with $\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i)$ coefficients is defined) and let $Y \subseteq X$ be a closed subset with open complement $U = X \setminus Y$. Let $L^\bullet$ be a perfect complex of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules whose restriction $L^\bullet|_U$ is acyclic (equivalently, zero in the derived category of $U$), so that all cohomology sheaves $\mathcal{H}^j(L^\bullet)$ are supported on $Y$.

(a) Construct, for every $i \geq 0$, Chern classes with support
$$c_i^Y(L^\bullet) \in H_Y^{2i}(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(i))$$
(or in the analogous ordinary cohomology with support in $Y$), that are functorial in $(X,Y,L^\bullet)$, additive on distinguished triangles in the appropriate Grothendieck-group sense, and such that under the canonical "forget supports" map
$$H_Y^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i)) \longrightarrow H^{2i}(X,\mathbb{Z}_\ell(i))$$
the class $c_i^Y(L^\bullet)$ is sent to the ordinary $i$-th Chern class $c_i(L^\bullet)$ of the perfect complex $L^\bullet$.

(b) Using such classes $c_i^Y(L^\bullet)$, formulate and prove a refined version of the cohomological Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem — both the version with denominators and the version without denominators — that incorporates families of supports, i.e. that takes place naturally in cohomology with support and recovers the usual Riemann–Roch formula after forgetting supports.
category_tag: Chern classes with support and Riemann-Roch
status_search_result: Localized/supported Chern classes for perfect complexes acyclic off a closed subset have been constructed in various settings (e.g. via MacPherson-style local Chern character constructions of Baum–Fulton–MacPherson, Iversen, and Bloch, and more recently in motivic/refined Gysin frameworks). The Riemann–Roch theorem without denominators has been proved by Jouanolou and extended into motivic homotopy theory and higher K-theory. However, a fully general formulation incorporating families of supports and giving a strengthened cohomological Riemann–Roch with supports remains an active topic; no single reference appears to settle the question in the broad generality stated.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
original_question: Let f: C^2 -> C^2 be an entire holomorphic mapping. Must the Euclidean volume of the image f(C^2), measured in the usual Euclidean volume on C^2, be infinite?
self_contained_problem: Equip $\mathbb{C}^2$ with its standard Euclidean (Lebesgue) volume, identifying $\mathbb{C}^2$ with $\mathbb{R}^4$. Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2$ be an entire holomorphic mapping, i.e. a map $f(z_1,z_2)=(f_1(z_1,z_2),f_2(z_1,z_2))$ whose components are entire holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{C}^2$. Consider the image set $f(\mathbb{C}^2)\subset\mathbb{C}^2$ and its 4-dimensional Lebesgue (Euclidean) measure $\mathrm{vol}\bigl(f(\mathbb{C}^2)\bigr)$. Must $\mathrm{vol}\bigl(f(\mathbb{C}^2)\bigr) = \infty$ for every such $f$? Equivalently, does there exist an entire holomorphic mapping $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ whose image has finite Euclidean volume?
category_tag: Several complex variables / entire holomorphic mappings
status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a resolution of this question. It is consistent with the literature on holomorphic mappings $\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}^n$ (e.g. Rosay–Rudin and subsequent work), where many natural questions about the image of such mappings remain unresolved. No source found that proves the Euclidean volume of $f(\mathbb{C}^2)$ must be infinite, nor one that exhibits an entire $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ with finite-volume image.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
original_question: Let D be a normal-crossings divisor in P^n, and let f: C -> P^n \ D be a holomorphic curve whose image misses D. If deg(D) is at least n+2, must the image f(C) lie in an algebraic subvariety of P^n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{P}^n$ denote complex projective space of dimension $n\geq 2$, and let $D\subset \mathbb{P}^n$ be a normal-crossings divisor (i.e.\ at each point of its support, $D$ is locally cut out by a product of distinct smooth analytic branches meeting transversally). Write $\deg(D)$ for the degree of $D$ as a hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^n$. Suppose $f:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{P}^n\setminus D$ is a nonconstant holomorphic map whose image avoids $D$.

Question: If $\deg(D)\geq n+2$, must the image $f(\mathbb{C})$ be contained in a proper algebraic subvariety of $\mathbb{P}^n$?
status_search_result: The question is a form of the logarithmic Green–Griffiths / Lang conjecture for complements of normal-crossings divisors in projective space. Known unconditional algebraic-degeneracy results require very high degree bounds (e.g. effective bounds of the form $d \geq n^{(n+1)^{n+5}}$ for generic hypersurfaces), and the sharp threshold $\deg(D)\geq n+2$ remains unresolved in general; only partial results (generic divisors, special configurations of hyperplanes/hypersurfaces) are available.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
original_question: Can one define a subclass of holomorphic mappings f: C^m -> P^n that gives a reasonable geometric and analytic value-distribution theory in higher codimension: every map in the subclass should satisfy the Nevanlinna inequality N(D,r) <= T(r)+O(1), the Liouville-type relation integral over D in |D| of delta(D) dmu(D)=0 for divisors in a complete linear system, and the functorial restriction property that f restricted to C^k remains in the subclass whenever f:C^m -> P^n is in the subclass?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a holomorphic mapping. For an effective divisor $D$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ whose support does not contain the image of $f$, let $N(D,r)$ denote the counting function of $f^{-1}(D)$ and $T(r)$ the (Cartan) characteristic function of $f$, defined in the usual sense of Nevanlinna value-distribution theory. For a complete linear system $|D|$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ with measure $d\mu$ induced by a unitary structure, let $\delta(D)=1-\limsup_{r\to\infty} N(D,r)/T(r)$ be the Nevanlinna defect.

Construct, for every pair $(m,n)$ with $1\le m\le n$, a non-empty class $\mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ of holomorphic maps $f:\mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{P}^n$ such that all of the following hold:

(i) (First Main Theorem inequality) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every effective divisor $D$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ whose support omits $f(\mathbb{C}^m)$,
$$N(D,r) \le T(r) + O(1).$$

(ii) (Liouville-type defect relation) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every complete linear system $|D|$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$,
$$\int_{D \in |D|} \delta(D)\, d\mu(D) = 0.$$

(iii) (Functorial restriction) For every $f \in \mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ and every linear embedding $\iota:\mathbb{C}^k \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}^m$ with $1\le k\le m$, the restriction $f \circ \iota$ belongs to $\mathcal{F}_{k,n}$.

Determine whether such a class $\mathcal{F}_{m,n}$ exists in higher codimension (i.e., when $m<n$), and if so, give an explicit characterization that is broad enough to be geometrically and analytically natural.
status_search_result: The problem of identifying a natural subclass of holomorphic mappings from $\mathbb{C}^m$ to $\mathbb{P}^n$ in higher codimension that simultaneously satisfies a First Main Theorem inequality, a Liouville-type integrated defect relation, and a functorial restriction property is a long-standing program in higher-dimensional Nevanlinna theory. Existing approaches (Griffiths, Ahlfors, Stoll, and the differentiably non-degenerate framework) handle special cases (equidimensional or non-degenerate maps), and the Ahlfors theorem is noted as one of the few global treatments of higher codimension. No general construction satisfying all three properties simultaneously appears in the literature; the question remains open.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
context_brief: curves on surfaces of general type
original_question: Let V be an algebraic surface with positive canonical bundle, and let f:C -> V be a holomorphic mapping. Must the image f(C) lie in an algebraic curve in V?
self_contained_problem: Let $V$ be a smooth complex projective algebraic surface whose canonical bundle $K_V$ is ample (so that $V$ is of general type with positive canonical class). Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to V$ be a non-constant holomorphic mapping from the complex plane into $V$. Must the image $f(\mathbb{C})$ be contained in a (proper) algebraic curve in $V$? Equivalently, must every entire holomorphic curve in such a surface $V$ be algebraically degenerate?
status_search_result: This is the Green-Griffiths(-Lang) conjecture specialized to surfaces of general type. It is known to be open in general for surfaces of general type, but has been established in important cases: McQuillan proved it for projective surfaces of general type satisfying $c_1^2 > c_2$ (positive second Segre number), via the foliation/Ahlfors-Nevanlinna theory approach. Further partial results exist for surfaces with additional structure (e.g., certain foliated surfaces, Shimura surfaces, and generic high-degree hypersurfaces in higher dimensions by Diverio-Merker-Rousseau and Demailly). The general case for arbitrary surfaces of general type remains unresolved.

paper_title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems
original_question: For a general holomorphic mapping f:C -> V from the complex line to an abelian variety V, and for a positive divisor D on V, must the image f(C) intersect D? The question excludes relying on the special case where f is a group homomorphism.
self_contained_problem: Let $V$ be a complex abelian variety of dimension $n \geq 1$, and let $D$ be an effective (positive) divisor on $V$. Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to V$ be a nonconstant holomorphic map. Without invoking the special case in which $f$ is (a translate of) a group homomorphism from $\mathbb{C}$ to $V$, must the image $f(\mathbb{C})$ intersect $D$? Equivalently, is it true that for every nonconstant entire holomorphic curve $f : \mathbb{C} \to V$ and every effective divisor $D$ on $V$, one has $f(\mathbb{C}) \cap D \neq \emptyset$?
status_search_result: By a theorem of Siu and Yeung, a nonconstant holomorphic map from the complex line to an abelian variety must intersect every ample divisor (in fact the defect vanishes). Combined with the classical Bloch theorem describing the Zariski closure of such an entire curve as a translate of an abelian subvariety, this resolves the question affirmatively for effective divisors on abelian varieties.

paper_title: Some problems of sample surveys
original_question: How can sampling for mapping purposes be developed for estimating underground reserves of coal, minerals, or similar spatially distributed resources?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded planar region (representing a geographic area), and let $Z : D 	imes [h_{\min}, h_{\max}] 	o \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ be an unknown nonnegative measurable function representing the local concentration (e.g., grade or density) of a spatially distributed underground resource such as coal or a mineral at horizontal location $x \in D$ and depth $h$. Define the total reserve as
$$R \;=\; \int_{D} \int_{h_{\min}}^{h_{\max}} Z(x,h)\, dh\, dx.$$
A sampling design consists of choosing a finite collection of borehole locations $x_1,\dots,x_n \in D$ (possibly chosen at random according to some probability law, or sequentially based on previous observations) and, at each $x_i$, observing $Z(x_i,h)$ on a depth interval (or on a finite set of depths) within $[h_{\min}, h_{\max}]$, possibly with measurement error.

Develop a theory of sampling for mapping the function $Z$ and for estimating the total reserve $R$. Specifically:

(a) Formulate a probabilistic model for $Z$ (for instance, treating $Z$ as a realization of a random field with prescribed mean and covariance structure) under which sampling designs and estimators can be compared.

(b) Construct an estimator $\widehat R$ of $R$ based on the sample $\{(x_i, Z(x_i,\cdot))\}_{i=1}^n$, and determine its bias, variance, and mean square error as functions of the sampling design and the underlying spatial covariance.

(c) Determine optimal (or admissible) sampling designs that minimize the mean square error of $\widehat R$ for fixed sample size $n$, including comparisons between simple random, systematic/grid, stratified, and adaptive sequential designs.

(d) Provide a method for producing a map (an estimate of $Z$ as a function of $(x,h)$) together with a quantitative measure of the mapping accuracy, and relate the optimal design for mapping to the optimal design for estimating $R$.
status_search_result: The general question of developing sampling methodology for mapping spatially distributed underground resources has been substantially addressed since its original posing through the development of geostatistics (kriging, variogram modeling) by Matheron and others, and through later work on optimal spatial sampling designs and adaptive/sequential designs in mining and environmental statistics. However, no single closed solution exists; many specific subproblems (optimal designs under realistic covariance models, adaptive designs, non-stationary fields) remain active research topics. The problem as posed is therefore partially solved.

context_brief: Square peg problem for Jordan curves
original_question: Does every Jordan curve in the Euclidean plane contain four points that are the vertices of a square inscribed in the curve?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma:S^1\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a Jordan curve, i.e., a continuous injective map from the circle into the Euclidean plane, and identify $\gamma$ with its image. Four points $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4\in\mathbb{R}^2$ are said to be the vertices of an inscribed square in $\gamma$ if they all lie on $\gamma$ and, after suitable ordering, form the vertices of a (non-degenerate) square in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Question: Does every Jordan curve in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contain four points that are the vertices of an inscribed square?
category_tag: Square peg problem (inscribed squares in Jordan curves)
status_search_result: The inscribed square problem (Toeplitz's square peg problem) remains open in full generality for arbitrary continuous Jordan curves. It has been resolved for many regularity classes (smooth, piecewise smooth, convex, $C^1$, locally monotone, and, by Greene–Lobb (2020), all smooth Jordan curves with any aspect ratio rectangle), but the general continuous case is still unresolved.

paper_title: Некоторые экстремальные задачи для векторных расслоений
original_question: Determine the optimal constant c for the following Minkowski-symmetry statement. For every continuous field of convex figures in γ^3_2, must there be a fiber figure K and an interior point O of K such that every chord of K passing through O is divided by O in ratio at least c:1, and the distances from O to each pair of parallel supporting lines of K are also in ratio at least c:1? The established bound is c=1/√2, and the open problem is to find the sharp value.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Grassmann bundle γ^3_2 of 2-planes in ℝ^3 over the Grassmannian G(3,2), and let a "continuous field of convex figures" on γ^3_2 be a continuous assignment, to each 2-plane P ∈ G(3,2), of a convex body K(P) lying in the fiber P (the choice depending continuously on P in the Hausdorff topology). For a convex body K in the plane and a point O in its interior, define s(K,O) as the largest c ∈ (0,1] such that:

(a) every chord of K through O is divided by O into two segments whose lengths have ratio at least c : 1 (smaller-to-larger), and
(b) for every pair of parallel supporting lines of K, the distances from O to these two lines have ratio at least c : 1.

Define
   c* = sup { c : every continuous field of convex figures on γ^3_2 contains a fiber figure K admitting an interior point O with s(K,O) ≥ c }.

It is known that c* ≥ 1/√2. Determine the exact value of c*.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate any subsequent work establishing the sharp constant for this Minkowski-symmetry statement on continuous fields of convex figures in the Grassmann bundle γ^3_2. The lower bound 1/√2 is recorded, and no improvement or matching upper bound construction was found in the search results.

paper_title: Некоторые экстремальные задачи для векторных расслоений
original_question: Determine the optimal constant r in the following Neumann-Rado-type fiber statement. For every continuous field of finite continuous mass distributions in γ^3_2, must there be a fiber plane g and a point A in g such that every line in g through A divides the mass in g into two parts whose smaller-to-larger ratio is at least r? The established bound is r=3:5, and the open problem is to find the sharp value.
self_contained_problem:
Let E_2(R^3) denote the Grassmann bundle of affine 2-planes in R^3, and let γ^3_2 denote the associated tautological fiber bundle whose fiber over a plane g ∈ E_2(R^3) is the plane g itself. A continuous field of finite continuous mass distributions in γ^3_2 is an assignment, to each fiber g, of a finite non-atomic Borel measure μ_g on g, depending continuously on g (in the weak sense). For such a field, one knows the following: there exist a fiber g and a point A ∈ g such that every line ℓ ⊂ g passing through A divides μ_g into two parts whose ratio (smaller to larger total mass) is at least 3:5.

Determine the optimal (largest) constant r ∈ (0,1] with the following property: for every continuous field of finite continuous mass distributions in γ^3_2, there exist a fiber plane g ⊂ E_2(R^3) and a point A ∈ g such that every line in g through A divides the mass μ_g into two parts whose smaller-to-larger ratio is at least r.
status_search_result: No published resolution of the sharp constant was found. The known bound r ≥ 3/5 is recorded, and the sharp value is stated as unknown. Web search did not surface a subsequent improvement.

original_question: Let a Finsler metric in γ^3_2 mean a continuous choice, in each 2-plane fiber, of a norm depending continuously on the fiber. Must every such Finsler metric have at least one fiber whose unit circle has length exactly 2π, measured in that normed plane?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ be the Grassmannian of 2-dimensional linear subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^3$, and let $\gamma^3_2 \to G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ denote the tautological rank-2 vector bundle whose fiber over a plane $P \in G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is the plane $P$ itself. By a Finsler metric on $\gamma^3_2$ we mean a continuous function $N : \gamma^3_2 \to [0,\infty)$ such that for every $P \in G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ the restriction $N|_P$ is a norm on the 2-dimensional vector space $P$. For each fiber $P$, let $S_P = \{v \in P : N(v) = 1\}$ be the unit circle of the corresponding norm, and let $\ell(S_P)$ denote its length as the boundary of a convex symmetric body in the normed plane $(P, N|_P)$, computed using the norm $N|_P$ itself (so the Euclidean unit circle has length $2\pi$).

Question: Must there exist at least one plane $P \in G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ such that $\ell(S_P) = 2\pi$?
status_search_result: No published resolution of this question could be located. The statement is explicitly recorded as not known to the author posing it, and a web search did not reveal a proof or counterexample in the literature on Finsler metrics on tautological bundles over Grassmannians.

paper_title: Некоторые экстремальные задачи для векторных расслоений
original_question: For n≥3, determine the optimal disk diameter D_n with the following property: every continuous field of planar convex figures of diameter at most 1 in γ^n_2 contains a fiber figure that lies in a Euclidean disk of diameter at most D_n. Known bounds in this setting are D_n≤sec(π/(2n+2)) for even n and n=3, and D_n≤sec(π/(2n)) for odd n≥5; the exact value is unknown.
self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 3 be an integer and let γ^n_2 denote the tautological 2-plane bundle over the real Grassmannian G_2(R^n) of 2-dimensional linear subspaces of R^n; each fiber of γ^n_2 is a Euclidean plane (a 2-dimensional subspace of R^n with the induced inner product). By a continuous field of planar convex figures in γ^n_2 we mean a continuous assignment to each point L ∈ G_2(R^n) of a compact convex subset F(L) ⊂ L (continuity taken with respect to the Hausdorff metric on compact convex sets, after locally trivializing the bundle). Such a field is said to have diameter at most 1 if diam(F(L)) ≤ 1 for every L. 

Define D_n to be the infimum of all real numbers D > 0 with the following property: every continuous field F of planar convex figures of diameter at most 1 in γ^n_2 contains at least one fiber figure F(L_0) that is contained in some Euclidean disk (inside L_0) of diameter at most D.

Determine the exact value of D_n for each n ≥ 3. It is known that
  D_n ≤ sec(π/(2n+2))  for even n and for n = 3,
  D_n ≤ sec(π/(2n))    for odd n ≥ 5.
status_search_result: No web evidence was found of a sharp determination of D_n. The problem is explicitly stated as unresolved, with only the upper bounds sec(π/(2n+2)) (for even n and n=3) and sec(π/(2n)) (for odd n ≥ 5) known; no subsequent work providing matching lower bounds or the exact value could be located.

original_question: For the tautological bundle γ^n_k, is it true that every continuous field of centrally symmetric k-dimensional convex polytopes in γ^n_k contains at least one polytope with at least 2n vertices? The case k=2 is established; the question remains in the general bundle setting.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma^n_k$ denote the tautological rank-$k$ vector bundle over the real Grassmannian $G(k,n)$ of $k$-dimensional linear subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$; its total space is $\{(L,v) : L \in G(k,n),\ v \in L\}$, with fiber $\gamma^n_k|_L = L$. A continuous field of centrally symmetric $k$-dimensional convex polytopes in $\gamma^n_k$ is an assignment $L \mapsto P(L)$ where $P(L) \subset \gamma^n_k|_L = L$ is a centrally symmetric (i.e., $P(L) = -P(L)$) convex polytope of full dimension $k$ in $L$, depending continuously on $L \in G(k,n)$ (continuity in the Hausdorff metric on compact convex subsets of fibers).

Prove or disprove: for every such continuous field $L \mapsto P(L)$, there exists at least one $L \in G(k,n)$ such that the polytope $P(L)$ has at least $2n$ vertices.
category_tag: Convex polytope fields on vector bundles
status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as open in general, with the case $k=2$ established. No subsequent publication confirming a full proof for general $k$ was located, so the general case appears still open.

original_question: Determine the optimal constant δ for planar lattice packings forced in continuous fields of convex figures in γ^3_2: what is the largest δ such that every continuous field of convex figures in γ^3_2 contains a fiber figure that admits a lattice packing of the plane with density at least δ? The established lower bound is δ≥3/4, and this bound is not sharp.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma^3_2$ denote the tautological (canonical) $2$-plane bundle over the Grassmannian $G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)\cong\mathbb{RP}^2$, whose fiber over a point $L\in G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ is the $2$-dimensional linear subspace $L\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ itself.

A continuous field of convex figures in $\gamma^3_2$ is a continuous assignment $L\mapsto K(L)$ that to every fiber $L$ associates a planar convex body $K(L)\subset L$ (continuity is with respect to the Hausdorff metric, after identifying nearby fibers via the bundle structure).

For a planar convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $\delta_L(K)$ denote its lattice packing density, i.e. the supremum, over all lattices $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ such that the translates $\{K+\lambda:\lambda\in\Lambda\}$ have pairwise disjoint interiors, of the upper density of $\bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}(K+\lambda)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Define
$$\delta^* \;=\; \inf_{\{K(L)\}}\;\sup_{L\in G_2(\mathbb{R}^3)}\delta_L\bigl(K(L)\bigr),$$
where the infimum is taken over all continuous fields of convex figures in $\gamma^3_2$.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Given an asymptotically flat Einstein initial data set (M,g,K) and a future trapped surface Sigma, must there exist an apparent horizon inside Sigma, meaning a closed spacelike 2-surface with one future null mean curvature equal to zero?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations, where $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $g$ is a complete Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor on $M$ playing the role of the second fundamental form. For a closed orientable two-sided surface $\Sigma\subset M$ with outward unit normal $
u$, induced mean curvature $H_\Sigma$ (with respect to $
u$) and $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K := \mathrm{tr}_g K - K(
u,
u)$, define the future outgoing null expansion $	heta^+ := H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ and the future ingoing null expansion $	heta^- := -H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$. The surface $\Sigma$ is called future trapped if $	heta^+<0$ and $	heta^-<0$ everywhere on $\Sigma$, and is called a (future) marginally outer trapped surface (apparent horizon) if $	heta^+\equiv 0$.

Suppose $\Sigma\subset M$ is a closed future trapped surface in such an asymptotically flat initial data set $(M,g,K)$. Must there exist a closed embedded marginally outer trapped surface $\Sigma'\subset M$ contained in the compact region bounded by $\Sigma$ and the asymptotic end (i.e., "inside" $\Sigma$)?
category_tag: Marginally outer trapped surfaces in general relativity
status_search_result: The existence of a marginally outer trapped surface (apparent horizon) inside any future trapped surface in an asymptotically flat initial data set was established by Andersson–Metzger in dimension 3, and extended to dimensions up to 7 by Eichmair using the Plateau-problem/Jang-equation approach. These results provide the MOTS Existence Theorem, confirming the existence of an outermost MOTS bounding the trapped region.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Does there exist an asymptotically flat vacuum Einstein initial data set, diffeomorphic to R^3, that contains an apparent horizon?
self_contained_problem:
An initial data set for the Einstein vacuum equations is a triple $(M,g,K)$ where $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $g$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a smooth symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R_g + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 - |K|_g^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0,$$
where $R_g$ is the scalar curvature of $g$. The data $(M,g,K)$ is called asymptotically flat if there is a compact set $C \subset M$ and a diffeomorphism from $M\setminus C$ to $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \overline{B}$ (for some closed ball $\overline{B}$) in which
$$g_{ij} = \delta_{ij} + O(|x|^{-1}), \qquad K_{ij} = O(|x|^{-2}),$$
together with appropriate decay of derivatives, so that the ADM mass and momentum are well defined.

A smooth closed $2$-surface $\Sigma \subset M$ is called an apparent horizon (a marginally outer trapped surface, MOTS) if its outward null expansion vanishes:
$$\theta_+ := H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K = 0,$$
where $H_\Sigma$ denotes the mean curvature of $\Sigma$ with respect to its outward unit normal in $(M,g)$ and $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ is the trace of $K$ restricted to $\Sigma$.

Question. Does there exist an asymptotically flat vacuum initial data set $(M,g,K)$ such that $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ and such that $M$ contains an apparent horizon?
category_tag: Einstein constraint equations and apparent horizons
status_search_result: Searches related to the existence of asymptotically flat vacuum initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ containing an apparent horizon reveal active research on MOTS, Penrose inequality, and constructions of vacuum initial data, including recent work producing smooth AF vacuum data without MOTS whose evolution forms a trapped region. However, no source directly confirms or refutes existence of such data on a manifold diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$ that already contains an apparent horizon; the status from accessible sources is inconclusive.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Does an apparent horizon persist under Einstein evolution of the initial data set, or can one exhibit an explicit counterexample to persistence?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g, K)$ be a smooth initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a 3-manifold, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations. Suppose $\Sigma \subset M$ is a smooth closed two-sided surface that is an apparent horizon at time $t=0$, that is, $\Sigma$ is (a connected component of the boundary of) the trapped region in $(M,g,K)$, equivalently a marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS) for which the outgoing null expansion $\theta_+ = H_\Sigma + \mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ vanishes. Let $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ denote the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum development of $(M, g, K)$, and consider any smooth foliation of a neighborhood of $M$ in $\mathcal{M}$ by spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces $M_t$ with $M_0 = M$.

Question: Must there exist, for every such foliation (or for some natural foliation) and for every sufficiently small $t > 0$, an apparent horizon $\Sigma_t \subset M_t$ that depends continuously on $t$ with $\Sigma_0 = \Sigma$? In other words, does an apparent horizon necessarily persist under Einstein evolution of the initial data, or can one exhibit an explicit vacuum initial data set with an apparent horizon whose Einstein evolution contains a Cauchy slice arbitrarily close to the initial slice on which no apparent horizon homologous to $\Sigma$ exists?
status_search_result: Searches did not return a definitive resolution of the persistence-of-apparent-horizons question. Related work exists on dynamical formation of MOTS and on numerical horizon-finding, and constructions are known of initial data without MOTS whose future development contains a trapped region, but no clear theorem or counterexample establishing or refuting general persistence under Einstein evolution was found. The status appears to remain unresolved.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: If M is an asymptotically flat 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and Sigma is a stable minimal 2-sphere in M, prove the Penrose inequality area(Sigma) <= 16*pi*(ADM mass)^2, and formulate and prove a corresponding inequality for initial data sets that are not time-symmetric.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, complete, asymptotically flat Riemannian $3$-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature, and let $m_{\mathrm{ADM}}(M,g)$ denote its ADM mass. Suppose $\Sigma \subset M$ is a stable minimal $2$-sphere. Prove the Penrose inequality
$$\operatorname{area}(\Sigma) \;\le\; 16\pi\, m_{\mathrm{ADM}}(M,g)^2.$$

Furthermore, formulate and prove an appropriate generalization to initial data sets that are not time-symmetric. Specifically, let $(M,g,k)$ be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations satisfying the dominant energy condition, where $g$ is a Riemannian metric on the $3$-manifold $M$ and $k$ is a symmetric $2$-tensor representing the second fundamental form of $M$ in the ambient spacetime, with ADM energy-momentum $(E,P)$ and ADM mass $m_{\mathrm{ADM}} = \sqrt{E^2 - |P|^2}$. Let $\Sigma \subset M$ be an outermost marginally outer trapped surface (apparent horizon). Show that
$$\operatorname{area}(\Sigma) \;\le\; 16\pi\, m_{\mathrm{ADM}}^2,$$
with equality characterizing initial data in the Schwarzschild spacetime.
status_search_result: The Riemannian (time-symmetric) Penrose inequality was proved by Huisken–Ilmanen (single horizon, 2001) and by Bray (general, 2001). The full spacetime Penrose inequality for non-time-symmetric initial data sets remains open in general; recent work (e.g., 2025) has established a spacetime Penrose inequality only with a suboptimal constant, and proofs exist under symmetry assumptions such as spherical symmetry. The sharp spacetime version is therefore still an open problem.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: What asymptotic conditions allow the conformal method to construct Einstein initial data sets on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold, such as a constant-mean-curvature hypersurface meeting future null infinity, thereby producing hyperboloidal initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g, K)$ be an initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $g$ a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ a symmetric $2$-tensor satisfying the Einstein constraint equations
$$R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0.$$
Suppose $M$ is the interior of a compact manifold-with-boundary $\overline{M}$ whose boundary $\partial M$ represents future null infinity, and that $(M,g)$ is asymptotically hyperbolic in the sense that there exists a defining function $\rho$ for $\partial M$ and a smooth metric $\bar g = \rho^2 g$ on $\overline{M}$ with $|d\rho|_{\bar g} = 1$ on $\partial M$. Suppose further that $\mathrm{tr}_g K$ is constant on $M$ (a CMC slice), modeling a hyperboloidal hypersurface meeting future null infinity transversally.

In the conformal method one prescribes a conformal background $(\tilde g, \sigma, \tau)$ — where $\tilde g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, $\sigma$ a transverse-traceless symmetric $2$-tensor with respect to $\tilde g$, and $\tau$ the prescribed mean curvature — and seeks a positive conformal factor $\phi$ and a vector field $W$ such that
$$g = \phi^4 \tilde g, \qquad K = \phi^{-2}(\sigma + \mathcal{L}_{\tilde g} W) + \tfrac{\tau}{3}\, g,$$
solve the constraint equations, where $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde g}$ denotes the conformal Killing operator of $\tilde g$. This reduces the constraints to the coupled Lichnerowicz–vector equations for $(\phi, W)$ on $M$.

Problem. Determine the precise asymptotic conditions on the conformal data $(\tilde g, \sigma, \tau)$ at $\partial M$ — including the rates of decay or polyhomogeneous expansion of $\tilde g - \bar g$, $\sigma$, and $\tau - \tau_\infty$ near $\rho = 0$, as well as compatibility/boundary conditions at $\partial M$ — under which the conformal method produces a solution $(\phi, W)$ giving a vacuum hyperboloidal initial data set $(M, g, K)$ that is asymptotically hyperbolic with the prescribed asymptotic geometry, with $\mathrm{tr}_g K$ constant, and such that $\partial M$ corresponds to future null infinity of the resulting maximal Cauchy development.
status_search_result: Substantial partial results exist: Andersson–Chruściel–Friedrich and subsequent work established existence of CMC hyperboloidal solutions of the conformal constraints under suitable asymptotic conditions, while showing that generic solutions admit only polyhomogeneous (logarithmic) expansions at conformal infinity rather than smooth ones. Recent work (e.g. on parabolic-hyperbolic formulations and on hyperboloidal data without logarithmic singularities, 2024–2025) further characterizes subclasses of asymptotic data yielding smooth or Bondi-regular development. A complete characterization of the optimal asymptotic conditions for the conformal method in this setting is not yet established, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Classify the possible smoothness properties of hyperboloidal initial data at conformal infinity, and identify the weakest such conditions under which a positivity proof for the Bondi mass can be completed.
self_contained_problem:
Consider an asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data set $(M,g,K)$ for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a 3-manifold with a conformal boundary at infinity $\mathscr{I}$, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ is a symmetric 2-tensor representing the second fundamental form. Suppose $M$ admits a conformal compactification: there exists a defining function $\Omega$ for $\mathscr{I}$ such that the rescaled metric $\tilde g=\Omega^{2}g$ extends to the boundary with some prescribed regularity (e.g. $C^{k}$ up to the boundary, $C^{\infty}$, or polyhomogeneous with controlled logarithmic terms).

The Trautman–Bondi mass $m_{\mathrm{TB}}$ of such a data set is defined as a boundary integral at $\mathscr{I}$ involving the conformally rescaled geometry.

Problem: Classify the possible smoothness/regularity behaviors of hyperboloidal initial data at conformal infinity $\mathscr{I}$ (e.g. finite differentiability up to the boundary, full smoothness, polyhomogeneous expansions, possibly with logarithmic terms), and determine the weakest such regularity condition at $\mathscr{I}$ under which a proof of the positivity of the Trautman–Bondi mass, namely $m_{\mathrm{TB}}\ge 0$ with equality only for Minkowski space, can be carried out for data satisfying the vacuum (or dominant-energy) constraint equations.
status_search_result: Positivity of the Trautman–Bondi mass has been established under several regularity assumptions at conformal infinity (e.g. polyhomogeneous and $C^1$-up-to-boundary conformal rescalings, and in higher dimensions). Recent work (2025) identifies conditions under which hyperboloidal data are free of logarithmic singularities, and the Bondi mass acts as a selector for such data. However, a complete classification of admissible regularity classes and identification of the optimal (weakest) hypotheses ensuring positivity remains an active area of investigation, so the problem is partially solved rather than fully closed.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Under what conditions on the stress-energy tensor must a static asymptotically flat spacetime metric be spherically symmetric, especially in the perfect-fluid case known as the static star conjecture?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ that is static and asymptotically flat: there exists a smooth, complete, hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field $\xi$ on $M$, and outside a compact set the spatial slice (the quotient by the $\xi$-flow) is diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the metric and lapse function approaching the standard flat values at the appropriate decay rates. Suppose the Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g = 8\pi T$ hold on $M$ for a stress-energy tensor $T$ supported in a compact "matter region" $\Omega \subset M$.

(a) Identify general structural conditions on the stress-energy tensor $T$ (for example, energy conditions, isotropy, equation-of-state hypotheses) which force the metric $g$ to be spherically symmetric, i.e. to admit an effective $SO(3)$ action by isometries whose orbits are the level sets of a radial function.

(b) (Static star conjecture.) In the special case where $T$ is the stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid,
$$T_{\alpha\beta} = (\rho + p)\, u_\alpha u_\beta + p\, g_{\alpha\beta},$$
with $u$ the unit timelike four-velocity aligned with $\xi/\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$ inside $\Omega$, energy density $\rho \geq 0$, pressure $p \geq 0$ vanishing on $\partial\Omega$, and a barotropic equation of state $p = p(\rho)$ satisfying physically reasonable monotonicity conditions, prove that $(M,g)$ must be spherically symmetric, with $\Omega$ a metric ball.
category_tag: Static star rigidity in general relativity
status_search_result: The static star (fluid ball) conjecture remains open in full generality. Partial results are known: spherical symmetry has been established under additional hypotheses such as the existence of a spherically symmetric comparison model with the same equation of state and surface potential (Beig–Simon, Lindblom–Masood-ul-Alam), and recent work (Coutinho–Leandro and others) has further refined these conditions, but a fully general rigorous proof for arbitrary physically reasonable equations of state has not been obtained.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Suppose two disjoint Cauchy surfaces in an asymptotically flat vacuum spacetime carry isometric initial data. Must the spacetime be stationary, meaning that it admits a timelike Killing vector field?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, $4$-dimensional, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat solution of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$. Recall that a Cauchy surface is a smooth spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ such that every inextendible causal curve in $M$ meets $\Sigma$ exactly once, and the induced Cauchy data on $\Sigma$ consists of the pair $(h,K)$ where $h$ is the Riemannian metric induced on $\Sigma$ and $K$ is the second fundamental form of $\Sigma$ in $(M,g)$. Two Cauchy data sets $(\Sigma_1,h_1,K_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,h_2,K_2)$ are called isometric if there exists a diffeomorphism $\phi:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$ with $\phi^*h_2=h_1$ and $\phi^*K_2=K_1$. The spacetime $(M,g)$ is said to be stationary if it admits a smooth Killing vector field that is timelike in the asymptotic region.

Question: Suppose $(M,g)$ admits two disjoint Cauchy surfaces $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ whose induced vacuum Cauchy data $(\Sigma_1,h_1,K_1)$ and $(\Sigma_2,h_2,K_2)$ are isometric. Must $(M,g)$ be stationary, i.e., must it admit a Killing vector field that is timelike at infinity?
category_tag: Stationarity and Killing fields in vacuum spacetimes
status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as an open question in mathematical relativity. Searches on standard sources (arXiv, surveys on open problems in general relativity) do not turn up a proof or counterexample for the general asymptotically flat vacuum case; partial results exist only under strong additional hypotheses. No conclusive resolution was found.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Prove the existence of nonsingular asymptotically flat static spherically symmetric solutions of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Yang–Mills (EYM) equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime with gauge group SU(2): the coupled system consisting of Einstein's field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}$, where $T_{\mu\nu}$ is the stress-energy tensor of a Yang-Mills connection $A$ with curvature $F$, together with the Yang-Mills equations $D^\mu F_{\mu\nu} = 0$ for $A$ on the resulting spacetime. Seek static, spherically symmetric solutions; with the standard ansatz, the metric takes the form
$$ ds^2 = -A(r) C(r)^2\, dt^2 + A(r)^{-1}\, dr^2 + r^2 (d\theta^2 + \sin^2\theta\, d\phi^2), $$
and the Yang-Mills connection is given by a single real "magnetic" potential $w(r)$. The reduced equations are
$$ r A' = 1 - A - \frac{(1-w^2)^2}{r^2} - 2 A (w')^2,\qquad r^2 A w'' + \big(r(1-A) - \tfrac{(1-w^2)^2}{r}\big) w' + w(1-w^2) = 0, $$
together with an ODE for $C$. Prove the existence of a globally defined, nonsingular (i.e. $A(r) > 0$ for all $r \ge 0$ with $A(0)=1$ and $w(0)=\pm 1$), asymptotically flat (i.e. $A(r) \to 1$, $C(r) \to 1$, $w(r) \to \pm 1$ as $r \to \infty$ with finite ADM mass) solution $(A, C, w)$ on $[0,\infty)$. Equivalently, establish the existence of static spherically symmetric soliton (particle-like) solutions of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations on $\mathbb{R}^{3+1}$.
status_search_result: The existence of nonsingular, asymptotically flat, static, spherically symmetric soliton solutions of the SU(2) Einstein–Yang–Mills equations (the Bartnik–McKinnon solutions, originally found numerically) was rigorously proved by Smoller, Wasserman, Yau, and McLeod in the early 1990s in "Smooth Static Solutions of the Einstein/Yang-Mills Equations" (Comm. Math. Phys., 1991/1993), with further work establishing a countable family parametrized by the number of zeros of $w$. The problem is therefore solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Analyze the time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills equations, analogously to the known analysis of the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field equations.
status_search_result: The fully time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills system has been studied in special cases (e.g., Bondi-coordinate formulations of the EYM–Higgs equations, global existence of certain homogeneous or small-data solutions, and numerical studies of critical collapse by Choptuik, Bizoń and others), but a complete rigorous analysis paralleling that achieved for the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field system (Christodoulou's program: global well-posedness in BV, weak cosmic censorship, critical collapse) has not been carried out. The broad program therefore remains open, with only partial results available.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Find an Einstein-Yang-Mills analogue of the Majumdar-Papetrou superposition of extremal Reissner-Nordstrom solutions.
self_contained_problem:
Background. The Majumdar–Papapetrou family of solutions to the source-free Einstein–Maxwell equations on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold consists of static metrics of the form
  g = -U(x)^{-2} dt^2 + U(x)^2 (dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2),
together with electromagnetic potential A = U(x)^{-1} dt, where U: R^3 \ {p_1,...,p_N} -> (0,∞) is any positive harmonic function on Euclidean R^3 with isolated singularities at points p_1,...,p_N. After analytic extension, each singularity p_k becomes a degenerate (extremal) Killing horizon, so the solution describes an arbitrary number of extremal Reissner–Nordström black holes held in static equilibrium by the exact balance of their gravitational attraction and electrostatic repulsion. The defining feature is that the linearity of the harmonic equation for U allows arbitrary superposition of single-black-hole solutions.

Problem. Construct a non-Abelian Einstein–Yang–Mills analogue of this Majumdar–Papapetrou superposition. More precisely: for a compact non-Abelian gauge group G (e.g. SU(2)), find static, asymptotically flat solutions of the coupled Einstein–Yang–Mills equations on R x (R^3 \ {p_1,...,p_N}) which (i) describe an equilibrium configuration of N ≥ 2 extremal black-hole-type horizons located at prescribed points p_1,...,p_N in R^3, with (ii) the metric and Yang–Mills connection determined by a superposition principle reducing the problem to a (possibly non-linear) elliptic system on R^3 with isolated singularities, and which (iii) reduces to the Majumdar–Papapetrou solution upon restriction of the gauge field to an Abelian subgroup. Alternatively, prove that no such Einstein–Yang–Mills multi-black-hole equilibrium analogue of Majumdar–Papapetrou exists.
status_search_result: Web searches reveal extensive work on Majumdar–Papapetrou solutions in Einstein–Maxwell theory and on single-horizon Einstein–Yang–Mills black holes (e.g., Smoller–Wasserman–Yau existence theorems, Wu–Yang ansatz solutions, Bogomol'nyi-type equations in Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs), as well as recent spinning generalizations of Majumdar–Papapetrou by Teo–Wan in Einstein–Maxwell. However, no construction of a genuine non-Abelian Einstein–Yang–Mills multi-black-hole equilibrium analogue of the Majumdar–Papapetrou superposition was found, nor a no-go theorem ruling it out. The status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: For the vacuum Einstein equations, prove a theorem saying that if an approximate metric g_e has Ricci curvature small in a suitable norm, then there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric g close to g_e in that norm.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge 3$ (Riemannian or Lorentzian setting may be specified). The vacuum Einstein equations on $M$ are the equation $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ for the Ricci curvature of a metric $g$. Call a metric $g_e$ on $M$ an "approximate vacuum metric" if $\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)$ is small in some suitable function-space norm $\|\cdot\|_X$ on symmetric $(0,2)$-tensors (for example, a weighted Hölder or Sobolev norm appropriate to the asymptotic geometry of $(M,g_e)$).

Problem. Formulate and prove a perturbation/stability theorem of the following form: there exist constants $\varepsilon>0$ and $C>0$, depending only on $(M,g_e)$ through controlled geometric quantities, such that whenever $g_e$ is an approximate vacuum metric with
$$\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)\|_X < \varepsilon,$$
there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric $g$ on $M$ (a solution of $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$) satisfying
$$\|g - g_e\|_X \le C\,\|\mathrm{Ric}(g_e)\|_X.$$

In particular, identify suitable norms $X$, geometric/analytic non-degeneracy hypotheses on the linearization of the Ricci operator (modulo diffeomorphism gauge) at $g_e$, and asymptotic conditions on $(M,g_e)$ under which such a quantitative existence-and-closeness statement holds.
status_search_result: No direct evidence was found that a general "approximate-implies-exact" theorem for Ricci-flat metrics, in the broad form requested, has been established. Partial results exist in specific settings (e.g., gluing constructions, asymptotically flat or asymptotically hyperbolic perturbation results, and stability theorems near non-degenerate Einstein metrics), but a general statement encompassing all relevant cases does not appear to be settled. Status is therefore marked unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Give precise conditions under which post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions converge to, or at least approximate, a global solution of the Einstein equations.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein field equations of general relativity, $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R(g)\, g = 8\pi T$, for a Lorentzian metric $g$ on a $4$-manifold, possibly coupled to a matter model (e.g., a perfect fluid of compact spatial support or a vacuum source). Two formal approximation schemes for solutions are commonly used:

(a) The post-Newtonian (PN) expansion: a formal expansion of $g$ and the matter variables in powers of $1/c$ (equivalently, in a small parameter $\varepsilon$ measuring the ratio of typical velocities to the speed of light), assuming slow motion and weak fields.

(b) The post-Minkowskian (PM) expansion: a formal expansion of $g = \eta + \sum_{n\geq 1} G^n h^{(n)}$ around the Minkowski metric $\eta$ in powers of Newton's constant $G$, without an a priori slow-motion assumption.

Formulate and prove precise conditions—on the initial data, the matter model, the gauge, and the regime (e.g., isolated systems with prescribed asymptotic flatness, bounded velocities, compact support, etc.)—under which:

1. The PN and/or PM series, possibly after suitable regularization of the divergent integrals that arise at higher orders, converges to a global-in-time solution of the Einstein equations; or, failing convergence,

2. The truncations of these series at order $N$ provide a genuine asymptotic approximation to such a global solution, in the sense that for each $N$ there exist function-space norms $\|\cdot\|_N$ and constants $C_N$ with
$$\bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PN},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, \varepsilon^{N+1}, \qquad \bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PM},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, G^{N+1},$$
uniformly on appropriate space-time regions.

Identify the obstructions (e.g., the logarithmic terms appearing at $4$PN order in harmonic gauge, the nonlinear far-field tail effects) and determine the largest class of initial data and matter configurations for which (1) or (2) can be rigorously established.
status_search_result: The rigorous mathematical justification of the convergence (or asymptotic validity) of post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions remains an open problem. Living Reviews and recent literature note that there is no proof that the PN approximation is even an asymptotic sequence in general, and divergences (e.g., at 4PN order in harmonic coordinates) and far-field tail terms involving logarithms remain serious obstructions. Establishing global existence and uniqueness results adequate to underpin the expansions for general compact matter sources is also lacking.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Find a simple usable approximation scheme that accurately determines the gravitational radiation produced by an isolated astrophysical system, and in particular prove the quadrupole radiation formula.
self_contained_problem:
Consider an isolated astrophysical system modeled as a solution of the Einstein vacuum (or Einstein–matter) field equations
\[ R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac12 R\, g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}, \]
on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold which is asymptotically flat at spatial and null infinity, with compactly supported (or sufficiently localized) stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ describing the matter source.

Develop a simple, usable approximation scheme (for example, a controlled post-Newtonian or post-Minkowskian expansion together with a near-zone/far-zone matching) that accurately determines the gravitational radiation emitted to null infinity by such an isolated source. In particular, give a mathematically rigorous derivation, within general relativity (not merely linearized theory), of the quadrupole radiation formula
\[ \frac{dE}{dt} \;=\; -\frac{G}{5c^{5}}\,\Big\langle \dddot{Q}_{ij}\,\dddot{Q}^{ij}\Big\rangle, \]
where
\[ Q_{ij}(t) \;=\; \int \rho(t,\mathbf{x})\Big(x_i x_j - \tfrac{1}{3}\delta_{ij}|\mathbf{x}|^{2}\Big)\,d^{3}x \]
is the trace-free mass quadrupole moment of the source, $\rho$ is its mass-energy density, and $\langle\,\cdot\,\rangle$ denotes a suitable time average. The derivation must:
(i) start from the full nonlinear Einstein equations,
(ii) yield error estimates controlled by an explicit small parameter (e.g. the ratio of source velocity to the speed of light, or the ratio of Schwarzschild radius to source size), and
(iii) justify the formula as an asymptotic statement about energy flux through future null infinity.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Blanchet and Damour developed a multipolar post-Minkowskian formalism that systematically expands the vacuum Einstein equations exterior to the source and matches it to a post-Newtonian near-zone expansion, leading to a derivation of the quadrupole formula and its higher-order corrections. Damour also provided derivations valid in the Newtonian limit. These results are widely accepted within the post-Newtonian framework and are central to gravitational-wave template construction, but a fully rigorous mathematical proof from the nonlinear Einstein equations with controlled error bounds (in the sense of mathematical relativity) remains incomplete. Hence the broader problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: In what sense does a Regge spacetime, modeled as a piecewise linear manifold with piecewise linear metric data, approximate a smooth vacuum spacetime, and what analogous convergence statement holds for numerical-relativity spacetimes?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$. A Regge spacetime is a four-dimensional piecewise linear manifold $(K,\ell)$ obtained by gluing flat Lorentzian 4-simplices along their tetrahedral faces, where the geometry is specified entirely by the assignment $\ell$ of squared edge lengths to the 1-simplices of $K$; curvature is concentrated as conical defects (deficit angles) on the 2-simplices ("bones"), and the Regge equations of motion are obtained by varying the Regge action $S_R(K,\ell)=\tfrac{1}{8\pi G}\sum_{\sigma^2}A(\sigma^2)\,\varepsilon(\sigma^2)$, where $A(\sigma^2)$ is the area of the bone $\sigma^2$ and $\varepsilon(\sigma^2)$ its deficit angle.

(a) Formulate and prove a precise sense in which a sequence $\{(K_n,\ell_n)\}_{n\ge 1}$ of Regge spacetimes satisfying the Regge equations of motion converges, as the simplicial refinement is increased (e.g., the maximal edge length tends to zero, subject to suitable non-degeneracy/fatness conditions on the simplices), to a smooth solution $(M,g)$ of the vacuum Einstein equations. Specify in what topology or measure-theoretic sense the discrete metric data $\ell_n$, the associated curvature distributions, and the Regge action approximate $g$, the Riemann/Ricci tensor of $g$, and the Einstein–Hilbert action of $g$.

(b) Formulate and prove an analogous convergence statement for spacetimes produced by numerical relativity: given a convergent family of numerical solutions to a well-posed formulation of the Einstein evolution equations on a sequence of grids with resolution tending to zero, identify the appropriate function-space topology and norms in which the numerical spacetimes approach a smooth (or suitably regular) vacuum solution, together with explicit convergence rates.
category_tag: Regge calculus and numerical relativity convergence
status_search_result: Several partial results are known: Cheeger–Müller–Schrader proved that the Regge action and curvature converge in the sense of measures to their continuum counterparts under fatness conditions on the simplices; Barrett established a convergence criterion in the linearized regime; and more recent works (e.g., on the definition of curvature in Regge calculus, 2024) refine these. A fully general convergence theorem for nonlinear vacuum Regge solutions to smooth Einstein vacuum solutions, and a comparably general statement for numerical-relativity spacetimes, does not appear to be established.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Prove a uniqueness theorem for maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces assuming only the dominant energy condition, rather than the timelike convergence condition or existence of a timelike Killing field.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime, i.e., a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian manifold admitting a Cauchy hypersurface. A spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ is called maximal if its mean curvature with respect to the future-directed timelike unit normal vanishes identically. Assume that the stress-energy tensor $T_{ab}$ of $(M,g)$ (via the Einstein equations $G_{ab} = 8\pi T_{ab}$, or directly as a symmetric 2-tensor) satisfies the dominant energy condition: for every future-directed causal vector $v^a$, the vector $-T^a{}_b v^b$ is future-directed causal.

Prove (or disprove) the following uniqueness statement: under the dominant energy condition alone — without assuming the timelike convergence condition ($\mathrm{Ric}(v,v) \geq 0$ for all timelike $v$) and without assuming the existence of a timelike Killing vector field on $(M,g)$ — any two maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces in $(M,g)$ must coincide (or, more generally, characterize the situations in which uniqueness fails).
status_search_result: Classical uniqueness results for maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces (e.g., Brill–Flaherty, Marsden–Tipler) require the timelike convergence condition or a timelike Killing field. Recent work on initial data rigidity under the dominant energy condition (e.g., Hirsch–Kazaras–Khuri–Zhang and related results) addresses rigidity aspects of DEC, but a general uniqueness theorem for maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces under DEC alone does not appear to be established in the literature found. Status remains unclear.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: If an asymptotically flat spacetime has a Cauchy surface without horizons, must the spacetime contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented, globally hyperbolic, asymptotically flat spacetime of dimension $3+1$ satisfying the dominant energy condition. Recall that a Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma \subset M$ is a smooth spacelike hypersurface that is met exactly once by every inextendible causal curve in $M$. The hypersurface $\Sigma$ is said to be "without horizons" if it contains no apparent horizons, i.e., no compact two-surface in $\Sigma$ on which the outgoing null expansion vanishes (so $\Sigma$ contains no trapped or marginally trapped surfaces). A Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma$ is called maximal if its mean curvature (with respect to the future-pointing unit normal in $M$) vanishes identically, and $\Sigma$ is asymptotic at spatial infinity to a hyperplane of constant time in the asymptotic Minkowski coordinates.

Question: If $(M,g)$ admits a Cauchy hypersurface without horizons (in the sense above), must $(M,g)$ contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface?
status_search_result: Existence of maximal hypersurfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes is classically addressed by Bartnik's interior-barrier construction (1984) and subsequent work, but a general theorem asserting existence whenever the spacetime has a Cauchy surface free of (apparent) horizons does not appear in the literature. Surveys of open problems in mathematical relativity list this as an unresolved question, and no proof or counterexample is found in available sources.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Is there a timelike geodesically complete, inextendible Lorentzian manifold satisfying an energy condition and containing a partial Cauchy surface with a trapped surface?
self_contained_problem:
Does there exist a Lorentzian manifold (M, g) of dimension at least 4 with the following properties simultaneously?

(i) (M, g) is time-oriented and inextendible (there is no isometric embedding of (M, g) as a proper open subset into a strictly larger connected time-oriented Lorentzian manifold of the same dimension).

(ii) (M, g) is timelike geodesically complete, i.e. every affinely parametrized timelike geodesic extends to all values of its affine parameter in R.

(iii) (M, g) satisfies a (non-trivial) energy condition such as the null energy condition Ric(v,v) ≥ 0 for all null vectors v, or the strong energy condition Ric(v,v) ≥ 0 for all timelike vectors v.

(iv) (M, g) contains an acausal, edgeless spacelike hypersurface Σ (a partial Cauchy surface).

(v) Σ contains a closed (compact without boundary) spacelike submanifold S of codimension 2 that is a trapped surface, meaning that both families of future-directed null geodesics issuing orthogonally from S have everywhere negative mean curvature (i.e., both null mean curvatures of S are everywhere negative).

Equivalently, does there exist an example showing that one cannot drop the global hyperbolicity hypothesis from Penrose-type singularity theorems while keeping inextendibility, an energy condition, a partial Cauchy surface, and a trapped surface, and still force timelike geodesic incompleteness?
status_search_result: Penrose-type singularity theorems show that a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying an energy condition and containing a noncompact Cauchy surface together with a trapped surface must be timelike geodesically incomplete. Without global hyperbolicity (only assuming a partial Cauchy surface) and with inextendibility imposed, the existence/nonexistence of such a complete example remains a recognized open question in mathematical relativity; recent surveys and rigidity results (e.g., on rigid singularity theorems and trapped sets in globally hyperbolic spacetimes) do not appear to resolve this version. No source found that explicitly closes the problem.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: Show that if condition (G) fails, or if there is a hidden infinity, in a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition, then the spacetime contains a trapped surface; thereby prove that such a cosmological spacetime is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R x M and is static.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{n+1}, g)$ be a cosmological spacetime, that is, a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold admitting a compact Cauchy hypersurface. Assume that $(M,g)$ satisfies the timelike convergence condition, $\mathrm{Ric}(X,X) \ge 0$ for every timelike vector $X$.

Recall the following notions:
- (Condition G) Every inextendible timelike geodesic in $(M,g)$ has both past and future endpoints on the "cosmological boundary" in the sense that no incomplete timelike geodesic ray escapes to a "hidden" portion of the spacetime; equivalently, the spacetime contains no timelike line confined to a region invisible from any Cauchy surface (a "hidden infinity").
- A hidden infinity is a region of $(M,g)$ where future or past inextendible causal geodesics fail to be captured by the family of Cauchy surfaces, allowing observers/geodesics to "escape" without completing.
- A trapped surface is a compact spacelike codimension-2 submanifold $\Sigma \subset M$ whose two future-directed null mean curvature vectors are both past-directed timelike (i.e., both null expansions are negative).

Prove the following:

(a) If condition (G) fails, or if $(M,g)$ contains a hidden infinity, then $(M,g)$ contains a trapped surface.

(b) Consequently, any cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete, or it splits isometrically as a metric product $(\mathbb{R} \times N, -dt^2 \oplus h)$ for some compact Riemannian manifold $(N,h)$ and is static.
status_search_result: The problem is connected to Bartnik's splitting conjecture for cosmological spacetimes, which remains a major open problem in mathematical relativity. Recent works (e.g., Galloway–Ling on CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting, 2019; Ling on omniscient foliations, 2022; examples without CMC foliations, 2023) make partial progress but do not resolve the conjecture in full. No source verifies the specific implication "(G) fails or hidden infinity ⇒ trapped surface" in full generality.

paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
original_question: For continuous or Holder-continuous Lorentzian metrics, are length-maximizing timelike geodesics unique, what physical meaning would nonuniqueness of the timelike geodesic initial-value problem have, and should such nonuniqueness count as a spacetime singularity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a Lorentzian metric $g$ of low regularity — either continuous ($C^0$) or Hölder-continuous ($C^{0,\alpha}$ for some $0<\alpha<1$) — and assume that $(M,g)$ is time-oriented and globally hyperbolic so that, between causally related points $p \le q$, length-maximizing causal curves exist.

A locally Lipschitz curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is called timelike if its tangent vector is timelike almost everywhere, and length-maximizing between its endpoints if its Lorentzian length $L(\gamma)=\int_a^b \sqrt{-g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)}\,dt$ equals the time-separation $\tau(\gamma(a),\gamma(b))=\sup\{L(\sigma):\sigma\text{ future-directed causal from }\gamma(a)\text{ to }\gamma(b)\}$.

Address the following:

(a) For Lorentzian metrics $g$ of regularity $C^0$ or $C^{0,\alpha}$ ($0<\alpha<1$), determine whether the length-maximizing timelike geodesic between two chronologically related points $p\ll q$ is unique. That is, decide whether there can exist two distinct (up to reparametrization) length-maximizing future-directed timelike curves from $p$ to $q$, and characterize the regularity threshold at which uniqueness fails.

(b) Analogously, study the timelike geodesic initial-value problem: given a point $p\in M$ and a future-directed timelike vector $v\in T_pM$, decide whether there exists a unique inextendible locally length-maximizing timelike geodesic with initial data $(p,v)$ in the low-regularity setting.

(c) Provide a physical interpretation of nonuniqueness phenomena from (a) and (b) in the context of general relativity, and determine whether such nonuniqueness of geodesics (timelike worldlines of freely falling observers) should be regarded as a singularity of the spacetime $(M,g)$.
