paper_title: Tensegrity frameworks: Dynamic analysis review and open problems
original_question: How can a tensegrity framework be designed by generating a new topology, including which nodes are connected, which kind of edge is used for each connection, the spatial nodal configuration, and the edge stresses, so that the resulting structure achieves a desired performance criterion such as stiffness, stiffness-to-mass ratio, or deformation under external forces while satisfying the geometrical and statical constraints required for a feasible tensegrity realization?
self_contained_problem:
A tensegrity framework consists of a finite set of nodes $V = \{p_1, \ldots, p_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (with $d \in \{2,3\}$) together with a set of edges $E$, where each edge $e \in E$ is labeled as either a cable (which can only sustain tensile axial force, i.e., stress $\sigma_e \ge 0$) or a strut (which can only sustain compressive axial force, $\sigma_e \le 0$). A self-equilibrated tensegrity realization is a quadruple $(V, E, \tau, \sigma)$, where $\tau: E \to \{\text{cable}, \text{strut}\}$ is the edge-type assignment and $\sigma: E \to \mathbb{R}$ is a stress assignment, satisfying:
(i) Static equilibrium at every node in the absence of external load: for each node $p_i$, $\sum_{e=\{i,j\} \in E} \sigma_e (p_j - p_i) = 0$.
(ii) Sign feasibility: $\sigma_e \ge 0$ if $\tau(e) = \text{cable}$ and $\sigma_e \le 0$ if $\tau(e) = \text{strut}$.
(iii) Prestress stability: the tangent stiffness matrix $K(V,E,\sigma) = K_E + K_G$ (sum of elastic and geometric stiffness matrices) is positive semidefinite, with kernel consisting only of rigid-body motions.

Given a design domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, a candidate node set or generation rule, a maximum number of nodes/edges, and a performance functional $\mathcal{P}$ (for example, overall stiffness with respect to a prescribed load, the stiffness-to-mass ratio, or the maximum deformation under a specified external load case), provide a constructive procedure that simultaneously determines:
(a) the connectivity pattern (which pairs of nodes are joined by an edge),
(b) the edge-type labeling $\tau$ for each edge (cable or strut),
(c) the spatial nodal positions $\{p_i\} \subset \Omega$, and
(d) a feasible self-stress $\sigma$,
so that the resulting tensegrity realization satisfies conditions (i)–(iii) and optimizes the performance functional $\mathcal{P}$.

Formulate and solve this combined topology, geometry, and prestress design problem for general performance criteria, beyond the case of a fixed pre-specified topology where only $\sigma$ and node positions are computed.
status_search_result: The literature treats this as an active, largely open challenge. Most established form-finding methods assume a given topology and solve only for nodal coordinates and self-stresses; jointly generating topology, edge types, geometry, and prestress for arbitrary performance criteria remains under active investigation, with recent partial advances via mixed-integer programming, rank-constrained LMIs, and scheme-matrix algorithms but no general solution.

paper_title: Tensegrity frameworks: Dynamic analysis review and open problems
original_question: For tensegrity structures whose desired set point or path has already been chosen by form finding, static design, or dynamic path planning, what passive or active control techniques can compensate for inaccuracies or absence of a dynamic model and for unknown external perturbations, so that the structure does not oscillate when it should remain still and can follow the desired path?
self_contained_problem:
A tensegrity structure is a prestressed pin-jointed framework consisting of a finite set of rigid bars (struts) in compression and a set of elastic cables in tension, in static equilibrium under the internal self-stress. Denote by q(t) ∈ R^n the vector of nodal coordinates (configuration) of such a structure and by its dynamics the (generally nonlinear, possibly nonsmooth due to cable slackening) equations of motion of the form M(q) q̈ + C(q, q̇) q̇ + g(q) = B(q) u + w(t), where u ∈ R^m collects the control inputs (for example, rest-length actuations of selected cables or forces applied at selected nodes), w(t) is an unknown bounded external perturbation, and M, C, g, B are only partially known. Suppose that a desired equilibrium configuration q* (chosen by form finding or static design) or a desired feasible trajectory q*(t) (chosen by dynamic path planning) has been prescribed.

Design a passive control law (a choice of mechanical damping elements and prestress) and/or an active feedback control law u = K(q, q̇, t) with the following properties simultaneously:
(i) Robustness to model uncertainty: the closed-loop tracking error e(t) = q(t) − q*(t) (or e(t) = q(t) − q* in the regulation case) remains uniformly bounded and converges to a neighborhood of zero whose size can be made arbitrarily small, despite inaccurate or absent knowledge of M, C, g, B.
(ii) Disturbance rejection: the same property holds in the presence of unknown but bounded perturbations w(t).
(iii) Vibration suppression at rest: when q* is a constant set point, the closed-loop response exhibits no sustained oscillations, i.e., q̇(t) → 0 asymptotically.
(iv) Admissibility: the control respects the unilateral constraint that cables can only transmit tension (no compression), and the prestress remains within feasible bounds throughout the motion.

Provide such a control design, together with a proof of its stability and performance guarantees, for general tensegrity structures.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction in the dynamic analysis of tensegrity structures. While various partial control schemes (PID, LQR, sliding mode, adaptive, and passivity-based controllers) have been proposed in the literature for specific tensegrity classes, no general control technique is known that simultaneously handles arbitrary model inaccuracies, unknown bounded perturbations, vibration suppression at rest, and cable unilaterality for all tensegrity structures. Recent works continue to address restricted versions of this problem, indicating it remains open in its full generality.

paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
original_question: For ongoing self-stabilizing consensus, where a sequence of consensus instances has input vectors and output values over time, and where stability means changing the output as few times as possible when successive input vectors allow the previous output to remain valid, what is the most stable consensus function when the only validity restriction is that the common output must equal at least t + 1 process inputs?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed system of n processes, up to t of which may fail, that repeatedly solves consensus. Time is divided into a sequence of consensus instances k = 1, 2, 3, .... At each instance k, every nonfaulty process supplies an input value, yielding an input vector v_k ∈ V^n (with ⊥ marking processes that have not supplied a value). A consensus function is a (deterministic) mapping f that, given the history of input vectors v_1, ..., v_k and previous outputs o_1, ..., o_{k-1}, produces a common output o_k ∈ V satisfying the following validity restriction: o_k must equal at least t + 1 of the entries of v_k (so the chosen value is supported by at least t + 1 process inputs at instance k).

Define the (in)stability of f on an infinite execution as the number of indices k ≥ 2 for which o_k ≠ o_{k-1}, restricted to executions in which the previous output o_{k-1} would still satisfy the validity restriction at instance k (i.e., o_{k-1} equals at least t + 1 entries of v_k). The stability of f is its worst-case instability over all such admissible input sequences.

Problem: Determine a consensus function f satisfying the above validity restriction that is most stable, i.e., that minimizes (over all such f) the number of times the output is forced to change across the sequence of instances when the previous output remains a valid choice. Equivalently, characterize the optimal trade-off and exhibit an optimal rule (and prove its optimality).
status_search_result: Recent literature on self-stabilizing and stabilizing consensus (2022–2025) addresses related models — Byzantine-tolerant self-stabilizing consensus, multivalued consensus, and topological characterizations of stabilizing consensus — but none of the located works explicitly identify or prove optimal the most stable ongoing consensus function under the "t+1 supporting inputs" validity restriction. No source claims a resolution of this particular optimization problem, so it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Feynman integrals as generalized functions on path space: things done and open problems
original_question: For quantum fields phi, vacuum vector Omega, time-ordering operator T, and a test function f, is the time-ordered vacuum expectation value <Omega, T exp(i phi(f)) Omega> holomorphic as a function of f after continuation from Schwinger functions to the corresponding time-ordered Minkowski functions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi$ denote a (scalar) quantum field on Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1}$, regarded as an operator-valued tempered distribution acting on a common dense invariant domain in a Hilbert space containing a distinguished vacuum vector $\Omega$. Let $T$ denote the time-ordering operation, and for a real Schwartz test function $f \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1};\mathbb{R})$ set $\phi(f) = \int \phi(x) f(x)\, dx$. Assume that the theory satisfies the Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader framework, so that the associated Euclidean Schwinger $n$-point functions exist and admit analytic continuation to time-ordered Minkowski $n$-point functions, and that the formal generating series
$$ Z(f) \;=\; \bigl\langle \Omega,\; T\, e^{i\phi(f)}\,\Omega \bigr\rangle \;=\; \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{i^n}{n!} \int \bigl\langle \Omega,\, T\,\phi(x_1)\cdots\phi(x_n)\,\Omega\bigr\rangle\, f(x_1)\cdots f(x_n)\, dx_1\cdots dx_n $$
makes sense (after the Schwinger-to-Minkowski continuation) as a function of $f$ on an appropriate complex neighborhood of $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1};\mathbb{R})$ inside the complexified test-function space $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^{1,d-1};\mathbb{C})$.

paper_title: On open problems of F. Qi
context_brief: best constants in a finite exponential-sum inequality
original_question: Let n be an integer at least 2, and let x_1, x_2, ..., x_n be nonnegative real numbers. Determine the best possible real exponents alpha_n and lambda_n and positive finite constants beta_n and mu_n, if such constants exist, for a two-sided inequality of the form beta_n sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{alpha_n} <= exp(sum_{i=1}^n x_i) <= mu_n sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{lambda_n} that is to hold for all such n-tuples of nonnegative real numbers.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. For nonnegative real numbers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$, determine all quadruples $(\alpha_n, \lambda_n, \beta_n, \mu_n)$, where $\alpha_n, \lambda_n \in \mathbb{R}$ and $0 < \beta_n, \mu_n < \infty$, such that the two-sided inequality
$$\beta_n \sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{\alpha_n} \;\leq\; \exp\!\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\Big) \;\leq\; \mu_n \sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{\lambda_n}$$
holds for every $n$-tuple $(x_1, \ldots, x_n) \in [0, \infty)^n$. In particular, find the best possible (sharpest) values of the exponents $\alpha_n, \lambda_n$ and the corresponding optimal constants $\beta_n, \mu_n$, or show that no such constants exist.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Bifurcation branches for the critical equation
original_question: For the same unit-ball problem -Δu = u^5 + λu in Ω ⊂ R^3 with zero Dirichlet boundary condition, sign-changing solution branches are known to emanate from eigenvalues associated with nonradial sign-changing eigenfunctions when λ ≥ λ1. Do any such branches reach the interval 0 < λ < λ1/4, or must they instead have vertical asymptotes at values λ ≥ λ1/4?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^3:|x|<1\}$ be the open unit ball, and consider the Brezis–Nirenberg-type problem with critical Sobolev exponent
$$
\begin{cases} -\Delta u = u^5 + \lambda u & \text{in } \Omega,\\ u=0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega, \end{cases}
\qquad (*)
$$
where $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter. Let $0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\lambda_3<\cdots$ denote the Dirichlet eigenvalues of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$, with associated eigenspaces $E_k$. It is known that for $\lambda\geq\lambda_1$ there exist sign-changing solutions of $(*)$ (and no positive solution), and that in the bifurcation diagram (with horizontal axis $\lambda$ and vertical axis some norm of $u$) continua of sign-changing solutions of $(*)$ emanate from those eigenvalues $\lambda_k$ ($k\geq 2$) whose eigenspace $E_k$ contains a non-radial sign-changing eigenfunction.
 
Determine whether any such bifurcation branch of sign-changing solutions can extend into the parameter interval $0<\lambda<\lambda_1/4$, or whether instead every such branch must remain confined to $\lambda\geq\lambda_1/4$ (for instance by possessing a vertical asymptote at some value $\lambda\geq\lambda_1/4$).
status_search_result: Recent work (including a 2025 preprint claiming a complete resolution of Brezis' first open problem) establishes existence of infinitely many sign-changing nonradial solutions of the 3D Brezis–Nirenberg equation on the ball for the full parameter range, but the specific question of whether bifurcation branches emanating from eigenvalues with nonradial sign-changing eigenfunctions actually reach the interval $(0,\lambda_1/4)$ or instead have vertical asymptotes at $\lambda\geq\lambda_1/4$ does not appear to be explicitly settled in the literature found. Status is therefore unclear.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Simpler proof for small-ε Ginzburg-Landau uniqueness
original_question: Find a simpler proof of the theorem of Pacard and Rivière asserting that, for sufficiently small ε > 0, the radial solution Uε is the unique solution of the disk Ginzburg-Landau system -Δu = ε^{-2}u(1 - |u|^2), u=x on ∂Ω.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and for each $\varepsilon > 0$ consider the Ginzburg–Landau boundary value problem for maps $u : \overline{\Omega} \to \mathbb{R}^2$,
$$-\Delta u = \varepsilon^{-2}\, u\,(1 - |u|^2) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u(x) = x \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega.$$
It is known that this problem admits a radial solution $U_\varepsilon(x) = f_\varepsilon(|x|)\,\frac{x}{|x|}$, where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ satisfies $f_\varepsilon(0) = 0$, $f_\varepsilon(1) = 1$, and the corresponding ODE obtained by substitution. It is also known (a theorem of Pacard and Rivière) that there exists $\varepsilon_0 > 0$ such that for every $0 < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_0$, the radial solution $U_\varepsilon$ is the unique solution of this boundary value problem.

Problem: Provide a proof of this uniqueness statement that is substantially simpler than the original argument of Pacard and Rivière (whose proof relies on a long and technical analysis using weighted Hölder spaces and a delicate linearization study).
status_search_result: Subsequent work has produced simpler and more direct uniqueness proofs in related settings: e.g., Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu established uniqueness of vortexless minimizers and of the degree-one vortex using Hardy-decomposition / positivity-of-radial-profile arguments. These results recover and simplify aspects of the Pacard–Rivière theorem, indicating substantial progress, though it is not clear that the full original statement has been reproven by elementary means.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let p > 2 and let Ω be the unit disk in R^2 with boundary condition g(x)=x on ∂Ω. For the p-Ginzburg-Landau energy Eε,p(u) = (1/p)∫Ω |∇u|^p + (1/(4ε^2))∫Ω (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on W^{1,p}_g(Ω; R^2), if uε is any minimizer or any critical point, does uε(x) converge to x/|x| for every x in Ω \ {0} as ε → 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the open unit disk and let $p > 2$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, consider the $p$-Ginzburg–Landau energy
$$E_{\varepsilon,p}(u) \;=\; \frac{1}{p}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^p\,dx \;+\; \frac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_\Omega \bigl(|u|^2 - 1\bigr)^2\,dx,$$
defined on the affine Sobolev space
$$W^{1,p}_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2) \;=\; \bigl\{\, u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2) : u(x) = g(x) = x \text{ for } x \in \partial\Omega \,\bigr\}.$$
Let $u_\varepsilon \in W^{1,p}_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ be either a minimizer of $E_{\varepsilon,p}$ or, more generally, an arbitrary critical point of $E_{\varepsilon,p}$ on $W^{1,p}_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$.

Prove or disprove: as $\varepsilon \to 0$,
$$u_\varepsilon(x) \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{x}{|x|} \qquad \text{for every } x \in \Omega \setminus \{0\}.$$
status_search_result: The literature contains partial progress on asymptotics of p-Ginzburg–Landau minimizers (e.g., convergence in W^{1,p} and C^{1,α} for radial or higher-dimensional analogues, and stability of radial minimizers for 2 < p ≤ 4), but no source confirms the asymptotic radial symmetry x/|x| for arbitrary minimizers or critical points on the unit disk with boundary data g(x)=x. The problem is listed as an open problem and appears to remain open.

context_brief: Finite potential energy for entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions
original_question: For any smooth solution u: R^2 → R^2 of the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation -Δu = u(1 - |u|^2) satisfying |u(x)| → 1 as |x| → ∞, must the potential-energy integral ∫_{R^2} (|u|^2 - 1)^2 be finite?

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2
original_question: Let Ω = B^3 be the unit ball in R^3 and let g: ∂Ω ≃ S^2 → S^2 be a smooth boundary map of degree zero. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map u: Ω → S^2 satisfying -Δu_i = u_i|∇u|^2 for i=1,2,3 in Ω, |u(x)|=1 in Ω, and u=g on ∂Ω?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit ball, with boundary $\partial \Omega = S^2$. Let $g : S^2 \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree zero. A map $u : \Omega \to S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, $u = (u_1, u_2, u_3)$, is called a harmonic map if $|u(x)| = 1$ for all $x \in \Omega$ and the harmonic map equation
$$-\Delta u_i = u_i\, |\nabla u|^2 \qquad (i = 1, 2, 3)$$
holds in $\Omega$ (in the sense of distributions).

Question: Does there exist a continuous map $u : \overline{\Omega} \to S^2$ which is harmonic in $\Omega$ (in the above sense) and which satisfies the Dirichlet boundary condition $u = g$ on $\partial \Omega$?
status_search_result: The question is the long-standing open problem of R. Schoen (mid-1980s) on existence of a continuous harmonic map from $B^3$ to $S^2$ with prescribed degree-zero smooth boundary data. It is referenced as an open problem in surveys by Hardt–Lin, Hardt, and Brezis, and no resolution is recorded in the literature retrieved. Status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Possible separation between existence and continuous minimization
original_question: In the degree-zero harmonic-map setting from B^3 to S^2, can it happen that no minimizer exists for the energy infimum over continuous competitors, yet a continuous harmonic map with the prescribed boundary data still exists?
self_contained_problem:
Let $B^3$ denote the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and $S^2$ the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^3$. For a map $u\in H^1(B^3;S^2)$ the Dirichlet energy is
$$E(u)=\int_{B^3}|\nabla u|^2\,dx.$$
Fix a smooth boundary datum $g:\partial B^3\to S^2$ of topological degree zero, and let
$$\mathcal{C}_g=\{u\in C^0(\overline{B^3};S^2)\cap H^1(B^3;S^2):u|_{\partial B^3}=g\}.$$
Set $I(g)=\inf\{E(u):u\in\mathcal{C}_g\}$. A continuous harmonic map with boundary datum $g$ is a map $u\in\mathcal{C}_g$ that is weakly harmonic (i.e.\ $-\Delta u=u|\nabla u|^2$ in the sense of distributions).

Question: Does there exist a smooth boundary datum $g:\partial B^3\to S^2$ of degree zero for which:
(i) the infimum $I(g)$ is not attained by any $u\in\mathcal{C}_g$ (no continuous minimizer exists), yet
(ii) there nevertheless exists a continuous harmonic map $u\in\mathcal{C}_g$ with $u|_{\partial B^3}=g$?
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems and is connected to a long-standing question of R. Schoen on the existence of continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2 with prescribed boundary data. No resolution appears in available sources; the problem remains open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Vanishing singular interaction for relaxed-energy minimizers
original_question: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed energy R for H^1_g(Ω;S^2) maps in the degree-zero B^3 setting, and let S(u) be the singular-interaction term in the representation R(u)=∫Ω|∇u|^2+S(u), equivalently encoded by the distributional Jacobian Ju. Must S(u)=0, equivalently Ju=0, or equivalently must there exist continuous maps un in H^1_g(Ω;S^2) converging strongly to u in H^1?
self_contained_problem:
Let Ω = B^3 ⊂ ℝ^3 be the open unit ball and let g : ∂Ω → S^2 be a smooth boundary datum of topological degree zero. Define
   H^1_g(Ω; S^2) = { u ∈ H^1(Ω; ℝ^3) : |u(x)| = 1 a.e., u|_{∂Ω} = g }.
For u ∈ H^1_g(Ω; S^2) the distributional Jacobian is
   Ju = (1/2) d(u^* ω_{S^2}) ∈ 𝒟'(Ω),
where ω_{S^2} is the area 2-form on S^2. Since deg g = 0, Ju is exact and may be written as the boundary of an integer-multiplicity 1-current; let L(u) denote the length of a mass-minimizing such connection joining the topological singularities of u (with the convention L(u) = 0 when no singularities are present). The relaxed Dirichlet energy on H^1_g(Ω; S^2) is
   R(u) = ∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx + 8π L(u) = ∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx + S(u),
and R coincides with the sequentially weak-H^1 lower-semicontinuous envelope of the Dirichlet energy restricted to H^1_g(Ω; S^2) ∩ C(Ω̄).

Question: Suppose u is a minimizer of R over H^1_g(Ω; S^2). Must one have S(u) = 0 (equivalently Ju = 0), or equivalently must there exist a sequence (u_n) ⊂ H^1_g(Ω; S^2) ∩ C(Ω̄) with u_n → u strongly in H^1(Ω; ℝ^3)?

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Geometric proof and sharp constant for a degree estimate
original_question: For continuous maps f:S^1→S^1, Theorem 5.2 states that |deg f| is bounded by a constant C times the double integral of |x-y|^{-2} over pairs (x,y) with |f(x)-f(y)| ≥ √3. Is there a simpler and more geometric proof of this theorem, what is the best possible constant C, and is that best constant achieved?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle, and for a continuous map $f \in C(S^1; S^1)$ let $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ denote its topological degree. It is known that there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for every $f \in C(S^1; S^1)$,
$$|\deg f| \;\le\; C \int_{S^1}\int_{S^1} \mathbf{1}_{\{|f(x)-f(y)|\ge \sqrt{3}\}} \, \frac{dx\,dy}{|x-y|^2},$$
where $\mathbf{1}_{\{\cdot\}}$ is the indicator function and $|\cdot|$ on the right-hand side denotes Euclidean distance in $\mathbb{R}^2 \supset S^1$.

Provide a simple, geometric proof of this inequality. Determine the best (smallest) possible constant $C$ for which the inequality holds for all $f \in C(S^1; S^1)$, and decide whether this optimal constant is attained by some map $f$.
status_search_result: The question of finding a simpler/geometric proof, the sharp constant $C$, and whether it is attained in the Bourgain–Brezis–Mironescu type degree estimate on $S^1$ is repeatedly listed as an open problem in surveys on topological degree estimates; subsequent works (e.g., on limiting Bourgain–Brezis estimates and related Jacobian problems) discuss existence and generalizations but do not establish the sharp constant or its attainment.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Minimal nonlocal energy in a prescribed degree class
original_question: For 1 < p < ∞ and integer d, let mp,d be the infimum of the p-th W^{1/p,p} seminorm among maps f:S^1→S^1 of degree d. Is mp,d = |d| mp,1 for every d? Is the infimum defining mp,d achieved? If this linear formula fails, is there an explicit formula for lim_{d→∞} mp,d/d = inf_{d>0} mp,d/d?
self_contained_problem:
Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $d\in\mathbb{Z}$. For maps $f\in W^{1/p,p}(\mathbb{S}^1;\mathbb{S}^1)$ (i.e. measurable maps from the unit circle to itself in the fractional Sobolev space of order $1/p$ and integrability $p$), the topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ is well-defined. The Gagliardo seminorm is
$$|f|_{W^{1/p,p}}^p := \int_{\mathbb{S}^1}\int_{\mathbb{S}^1} \frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy.$$
Define
$$m_{p,d} := \inf\bigl\{\,|f|_{W^{1/p,p}}^p \;:\; f\in W^{1/p,p}(\mathbb{S}^1;\mathbb{S}^1),\ \deg f = d\,\bigr\}.$$

(a) Is it true that $m_{p,d} = |d|\,m_{p,1}$ for every $d\in\mathbb{Z}$ and every $1<p<\infty$?

(b) Is the infimum defining $m_{p,d}$ attained?

(c) If the equality in (a) fails, is there an explicit formula for
$$\lim_{d\to+\infty}\frac{m_{p,d}}{d} = \inf_{d>0}\frac{m_{p,d}}{d}?$$

(It is known that the answers to (a) and (b) are affirmative when $p=2$.)
category_tag: fractional Sobolev maps to the circle
status_search_result: A recent preprint (2025) establishes existence of degree-one minimizers in $W^{1/p,p}(\mathbb{S}^1,\mathbb{S}^1)$ for $p\in[p',2]$ with $p'\approx 1.13924$, providing a partial affirmative answer to the attainment question (b) in a restricted range of $p$. The linear identity $m_{p,d}=|d|m_{p,1}$ for all $d$ and the explicit limit formula in (c) appear to remain open in general; only the case $p=2$ is fully settled.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Borderline regularity for hearing the degree
original_question: Suppose f,g:S^1→S^1 have equal Fourier coefficient moduli |an(f)|=|an(g)| for every n∈Z. The equality deg f=deg g is known when f,g ∈ W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1), and also for Hölder maps of exponent α>1/3. Does the same conclusion hold when f,g ∈ W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) with p>3, or when f,g are Hölder with exponent α≤1/3? What happens under the asymmetric stronger assumptions f ∈ W^{1/p,p}, 2<p≤3, g ∈ W^{1/q,q}, q>3, or f ∈ C^{0,α}, α>1/3, g ∈ C^{0,β}, β≤1/3?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle. For a measurable map $h:S^1\to S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$, write its Fourier coefficients as
$$a_n(h)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} h(\theta)\,e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta,\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
For sufficiently regular maps $h:S^1\to S^1$ (e.g., continuous), let $\deg h\in\mathbb{Z}$ denote the topological (winding) degree. For $1\le p<\infty$ and $s\in(0,1)$, the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of measurable maps $h:S^1\to S^1$ with
$$\iint_{S^1\times S^1}\frac{|h(x)-h(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{1+sp}}\,dx\,dy<\infty,$$
and $C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ denotes Hölder-continuous maps of exponent $\alpha\in(0,1]$.

It is known that if $f,g\in W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1)$ satisfy $|a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)|$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $\deg f=\deg g$; in particular this conclusion holds when $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha>1/3$.

Questions:
(a) Does the conclusion $\deg f=\deg g$ remain true if instead $f,g\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ for some $p>3$?
(b) Does it remain true if $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha\le 1/3$?
(c) Is it true under the asymmetric hypotheses $f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ with $2<p\le 3$ and $g\in W^{1/q,q}(S^1;S^1)$ with $q>3$?
(d) Is it true under the asymmetric hypotheses $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha>1/3$ and $g\in C^{0,\beta}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\beta\le 1/3$?
category_tag: Fractional Sobolev maps and topological degree
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any publication resolving this question. The problem is listed as an open problem in a compilation of favorite open problems by Brezis, and no follow-up work indicating a solution was found in available search results.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Function-dependent summation for hearing the degree
original_question: Given an individual map f in C(S^1;S^1), or more generally in VMO(S^1;S^1), does there exist a summation process σ_{n,ε} that may depend on f and recovers the degree from Fourier magnitudes by lim_{ε→0} Σ_{n∈Z} n |an(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε} = deg f?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$. For $f \in L^2(S^1; \mathbb{C})$, let $a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} f(e^{i\theta}) e^{-in\theta}\, d\theta$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, denote its Fourier coefficients. Recall that any $f \in C(S^1; S^1)$ (continuous maps from the circle to itself), and more generally any $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1; S^1)$ (maps of vanishing mean oscillation taking values in $S^1$), admits a well-defined integer topological degree $\deg f$.

A summation process is a family $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})_{n \in \mathbb{Z},\, \varepsilon > 0}$ of real numbers such that, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, the sum $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\, |a_n(f)|^2\, \sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ is absolutely convergent.

Question: Given an individual map $f \in C(S^1; S^1)$ (respectively, $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1; S^1)$), does there exist a summation process $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})$, possibly depending on $f$, such that
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\, |a_n(f)|^2\, \sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \;=\; \deg f \,?$$
category_tag: Fourier coefficients and topological degree of circle maps
status_search_result: The question (whether the degree of a VMO or continuous map of the circle can be recovered from the moduli of its Fourier coefficients via an f-dependent summation process) is part of the "Can one hear the degree?" program. While Bourgain–Kozma showed that |a_n(f)| does not determine deg f in general, the existence of an f-dependent summation process recovering the degree remains open according to available surveys on degree theory and Fourier series.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Distances between H^1 homotopy classes on S^2
original_question: For maps f:S^2→S^2 in H^1, let Ed be the class of maps of degree d, and define Dist_{H^1}(Ed1,Ed2)=sup_{f∈Ed1} inf_{g∈Ed2} ||∇(f-g)||_{L^2}. Is Dist_{H^1}(Ed1,Ed2)^2 = 8π|d1-d2| for all integers d1,d2? Even more basically, is Dist_{H^1}(Ed1,Ed2)=Dist_{H^1}(Ed2,Ed1) for all d1,d2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2$ denote the standard unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and let $H^1(S^2;S^2)$ be the space of measurable maps $f:S^2\to S^2$ with $\int_{S^2}|\nabla f|^2\,d\sigma<\infty$ (where $\nabla$ is the tangential gradient on $S^2$). Every $f\in H^1(S^2;S^2)$ has a well-defined integer Brouwer degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$, and for each $d\in\mathbb{Z}$ define the homotopy class
$$E_d=\{f\in H^1(S^2;S^2):\deg f=d\}.$$
For $d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}$ define the asymmetric distance
$$\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})=\sup_{f\in E_{d_1}}\inf_{g\in E_{d_2}}\|\nabla(f-g)\|_{L^2(S^2)}.$$

(a) Prove or disprove that
$$\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})^2=8\pi\,|d_1-d_2|\qquad\text{for all }d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}.$$

(b) Prove or disprove the (a priori weaker) symmetry statement
$$\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})=\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_2},E_{d_1})\qquad\text{for all }d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
status_search_result: The upper bound $\mathrm{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})^2\le 8\pi|d_1-d_2|$ is established, and the matching lower bound is known in the case $d_2>d_1\ge 0$ (work of Brezis–Mironescu–Shafrir on distances between homotopy classes of $W^{s,p}(S^N;S^N)$, including the 2016 article in ESAIM COCV and the HAL preprint hal-01308505). The general equality for all integers $d_1,d_2$, and even the symmetry question, do not appear resolved in the literature located.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded smooth convex subset of R^N with N≥10, and consider -Δu=λe^u in Ω, u>0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω. Let u* be the extremal weak solution obtained as λ increases to the critical parameter λ*. Is u* unbounded? If some convex domains have bounded u* for f(u)=e^u, can one find another smooth increasing convex superlinear nonlinearity f, possibly depending on Ω and satisfying f(0)>0 and f(t)/t→∞, for which the corresponding extremal solution u* is not in L∞(Ω)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth convex domain with $N \ge 10$. For a smooth function $f:[0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(0)>0$, $f$ increasing and convex, and $\lim_{t\to\infty} f(t)/t = +\infty$, consider the family of problems
$$-\Delta u = \lambda f(u) \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u > 0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
for $\lambda > 0$. It is known that there exists a critical parameter $\lambda^* = \lambda^*(\Omega,f) \in (0,\infty)$ such that for every $\lambda \in (0,\lambda^*)$ the problem admits a minimal classical solution $u_\lambda$, the family $\{u_\lambda\}$ is increasing in $\lambda$, and the pointwise limit
$$u^*(x) := \lim_{\lambda \nearrow \lambda^*} u_\lambda(x)$$
defines the so-called extremal weak solution of the problem at $\lambda = \lambda^*$.

(a) Taking $f(u) = e^u$, is the extremal solution $u^*$ necessarily unbounded (i.e. $u^* \notin L^\infty(\Omega)$) for every bounded smooth convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ with $N \ge 10$?

(b) If there exist bounded smooth convex domains $\Omega$ for which the extremal solution corresponding to $f(u) = e^u$ is bounded, does there always exist some smooth function $f$ (possibly depending on $\Omega$) satisfying the conditions $f(0)>0$, $f$ increasing and convex, and $f(t)/t \to \infty$ as $t \to \infty$, such that the corresponding extremal solution $u^*$ is not in $L^\infty(\Omega)$?
category_tag: Extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
status_search_result: For general (not necessarily exponential) nonlinearities, the regularity of extremal solutions in dimensions $N\le 9$ was settled by Cabré–Figalli–Ros-Oton–Serra, and constructions show that for $N\ge 10$ there exist domains and nonlinearities $f$ producing singular extremal solutions, addressing part (b) affirmatively in a strong sense. However, for the specific case $f(u)=e^u$ on general bounded smooth convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N\ge 10$, the question of whether $u^*$ must be unbounded remains open in general (it is known only on balls via Joseph–Lundgren).

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: On the torus T^N with N≥2, does there exist a constant C such that every test function ψ satisfies the Bourgain-Brezis type estimate ||ψ - ∫ψ||_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} ≤ C ||∇ψ||_{H^{-1/2}+L^1}? This is the strengthened estimate needed to derive the H^{1/2}+W^{1,1} phase estimate by the same duality method used for the weaker L^{N/(N-1)} estimate.
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\geq 2$ and let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the $N$-dimensional torus. For $s\in\mathbb{R}$, denote by $H^s(\mathbb{T}^N)$ the usual $L^2$-based Sobolev space defined via Fourier series, and by $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)$ the Sobolev space of integrable functions whose distributional gradient lies in $L^1$. For two Banach spaces $X,Y$ of distributions, define the sum space $X+Y$ with norm
$$\|f\|_{X+Y}=\inf\{\|g\|_X+\|h\|_Y : f=g+h,\ g\in X,\ h\in Y\}.$$
For a vector field $V=(V_1,\dots,V_N)$ with components in $X+Y$, set $\|V\|_{X+Y}=\sum_{j}\|V_j\|_{X+Y}$.

Question: Does there exist a constant $C=C(N)$ such that for every smooth function $\psi:\mathbb{T}^N\to\mathbb{R}$,
$$\Big\|\psi-\int_{\mathbb{T}^N}\psi\Big\|_{H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)} \;\leq\; C\,\|\nabla\psi\|_{H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)}\,?$$
status_search_result: A direct resolution of this specific sum-space inequality on the torus does not appear in the literature found. Related Bourgain–Brezis-type limiting estimates have seen progress (e.g., affirmative answers for Euclidean Lorentz-space analogues for div-curl systems), but the precise torus question with the $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ / $H^{-1/2}+L^1$ pairing appears not to be confirmed solved.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Elementary proof for the p=1 constant-function criterion
original_question: Find a more direct and elementary proof, in the spirit of Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung, of the p=1 case of the theorem asserting that if a measurable u satisfies λΦ_{λ,p}(u)→0 as λ→∞, then u is constant, where Φ_{λ,p}(u) is the measure of pairs (x,y) for which |u(x)-u(y)|^p/|x-y|^{p+N} ≥ λ.
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 1$ and, for a measurable function $u:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}$ (or on a ball $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$), $p\ge 1$, and $\lambda>0$, define
$$\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)\;=\;\Big|\Big\{(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega:\;\frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{p+N}}\ \ge\ \lambda\Big\}\Big|,$$
where $|\cdot|$ denotes the $2N$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. It is known that if
$$\lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)\;=\;0,$$
then $u$ is constant almost everywhere. For $p>1$ this admits a direct proof in the style of Brezis–Van Schaftingen–Yung (using simple covering/rearrangement arguments). For $p=1$, the only known proof is indirect, going through a substantially deeper statement.

Problem: Provide a direct, elementary proof of the $p=1$ case — i.e. show, by arguments in the spirit of the $p>1$ proof of Brezis–Van Schaftingen–Yung and without appealing to the deeper machinery, that any measurable $u$ satisfying $\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,1}(u)\to 0$ as $\lambda\to\infty$ is almost everywhere constant.
status_search_result: The p=1 case is known (proved by Poliakovsky as a corollary of a deeper result), but the request for an elementary, direct proof in the spirit of Brezis–Van Schaftingen–Yung does not appear to be addressed in the literature found. Related elementary approaches (e.g. via Vitali covering) cover 1≤p<∞ for related characterizations but reportedly break down at p=1 in the relevant range. No source confirming a direct elementary proof for this specific Φ_{λ,1} statement was located.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Liminf control of Sobolev and BV seminorms
original_question: With Ω and Φ_{λ,p}(u) as above, for every 1<p<∞ does there exist C=C(p,N,Ω) such that all measurable u satisfy ||∇u||_{L^p}^p ≤ C liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,p}(u), interpreting ||∇u||_{L^p}=∞ when u∉W^{1,p}(Ω)? Similarly, for p=1 does there exist C=C(N,Ω) such that ||∇u||_M ≤ C liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,1}(u), where ||∇u||_M is total variation for BV functions and ∞ outside BV?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded domain (or $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^N$). For $\lambda>0$, $1\le p<\infty$, and a measurable function $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$, define
$$\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)\;=\;\int\!\!\!\int_{\{(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega\;:\;|u(x)-u(y)|>\lambda|x-y|^{1+N/p}\}}\frac{dx\,dy}{|x-y|^{N}},$$
i.e. the (weighted) measure of the set of pairs $(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega$ for which $|u(x)-u(y)|>\lambda|x-y|^{1+N/p}$, measured with the weight $|x-y|^{-N}$.

Adopt the convention that $\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}=\infty$ whenever $u\notin W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and that the total variation $\|\nabla u\|_{\mathcal{M}(\Omega)}=\infty$ whenever $u\notin BV(\Omega)$.

(a) For every $1<p<\infty$, does there exist a constant $C=C(p,N,\Omega)$ such that for every measurable function $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$
$$\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^{p}\;\le\;C\,\liminf_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)\,?$$

(b) For $p=1$, does there exist a constant $C=C(N,\Omega)$ such that for every measurable function $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$
$$\|\nabla u\|_{\mathcal{M}(\Omega)}\;\le\;C\,\liminf_{\lambda\to\infty}\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,1}(u)\,?$$
status_search_result: Recent works (Brezis–Seeger–Van Schaftingen–Yung in Analysis & PDE 17 (2024) and Nguyen's 2025 preprint on nonlocal characterizations of Sobolev norms and total variation) discuss sharp upper bounds in terms of $\limsup \lambda^p\nu_\gamma(E_{\lambda,\gamma/p}[u])$ and related $L^{p,\infty}$ quasinorm characterizations, but the $\liminf$ control formulated here — particularly the BV case ($p=1$) — is not established in the literature found and is still cited as open. The status is therefore open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Sharp relative isoperimetric inequality for the cube
original_question: Let Q be the unit cube in R^N, N≥2. For 0≤t≤1, define f_N(t) as the infimum of the relative perimeter P(S) over measurable subsets S⊂Q with volume |S|=t, where P(S) counts only boundary inside Q. An explicit formula is known for N=2. Is there a similar formula for f_N(t) when N≥3? In particular, is f_N(t) identically 1 near t=1/2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q=(0,1)^N$ denote the open unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N\geq 2$. For a measurable set $S\subset Q$, write $\mathbf{1}_S$ for its characteristic function, $|S|=\|\mathbf{1}_S\|_{L^1}$ for its volume, and define the relative perimeter
$$P(S)=\|\nabla\mathbf{1}_S\|(Q),$$
the total variation of the distributional gradient of $\mathbf{1}_S$ measured only inside $Q$ (so that the part of $\partial S$ lying on $\partial Q$ is not counted). For each $t\in[0,1]$ define the isoperimetric profile of the cube
$$f_N(t)=\inf\{P(S): S\subset Q\text{ measurable},\ |S|=t\}.$$
For $N=2$ an explicit formula for $f_2(t)$ is known. 

(a) Find an explicit formula for $f_N(t)$ when $N\geq 3$.

(b) Prove or disprove: there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that $f_N(t)\equiv 1$ for all $t\in[\tfrac12-\varepsilon,\tfrac12+\varepsilon]$ (equivalently, that minimizers of volume near $1/2$ are obtained by slicing the cube by a hyperplane parallel to a face).
status_search_result: Part (b) — that $f_N(t)\equiv 1$ for $t$ sufficiently close to $1/2$ — was settled affirmatively by F. Glaudo (arXiv:2305.20051, 2023), who proved that any subset of $(0,1)^d$ with volume close enough to $1/2$ has relative perimeter at least 1, confirming the Brezis–Bruckstein conjecture in this regime. An explicit closed-form formula for $f_N(t)$ on the whole interval $[0,1]$ in dimensions $N\geq 3$ does not appear to be known.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: For a prime homogeneous ideal P contained in (x1,...,xn)^2 in S = k[x1,...,xn], is the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous generating set of P at most deg(S/P)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring with $\deg(x_i)=1$. Let $P \subset S$ be a homogeneous prime ideal contained in $(x_1,\dots,x_n)^2$ (i.e., $P$ is nondegenerate in the sense that it has no linear generators and, after a suitable embedding, contains no linear form). For a minimal homogeneous generating set $\{f_1,\dots,f_r\}$ of $P$, let $\mathrm{maxdeg}(P) := \max_i \deg(f_i)$, and let $\deg(S/P)$ denote the multiplicity (degree) of the graded ring $S/P$. Determine whether the inequality
$$\mathrm{maxdeg}(P) \le \deg(S/P)$$
holds for every such prime ideal $P$.
status_search_result: The Eisenbud–Goto regularity conjecture, which would have implied this generator-degree bound, was disproved by McCullough and Peeva (J. Amer. Math. Soc., 2018). Their construction yields homogeneous prime ideals $P_r$ in standard graded polynomial rings with $\mathrm{maxdeg}(P_r) \ge 3^{2^{r-1}}+1$ while $\deg(S/P_r) \le 2\cdot 6^{7r+5}$, so $\mathrm{maxdeg}(P_r) > \deg(S/P_r)$ for sufficiently large $r$. Hence the conjectured inequality fails in general.

original_question: Construct families of homogeneous ideals whose regularity grows polynomially, exponentially, or doubly exponentially in the number of variables while the largest degree among the minimal homogeneous generators remains bounded by a fixed constant.
status_search_result: Doubly exponential growth of regularity with bounded generator degree is known via Mayr–Meyer type constructions (e.g., Bayer–Stillman, Koh), matching the Galligo–Giusti–Caviglia–Sbarra upper bound $(2d)^{2^{n-2}}$. paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: For homogeneous ideals I satisfying specified special hypotheses, find sharp upper bounds for reg(I) in terms of the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous generating set of I.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S = k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring. For a homogeneous ideal $I \subseteq S$, let
$$d(I) := \max\{\deg(f) : f \in G\}$$
for any minimal homogeneous generating set $G$ of $I$ (this maximum is independent of the choice of minimal generating set), and let $\mathrm{reg}(I)$ denote the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $I$, defined as
$$\mathrm{reg}(I) = \max\{j - i : \beta_{i,j}(I) \neq 0\},$$
where $\beta_{i,j}(I) = \dim_k \mathrm{Tor}_i^S(I,k)_j$ are the graded Betti numbers of $I$.

In general $\mathrm{reg}(I)$ can be doubly exponential in $d(I)$ and $n$ (as in the Mayr–Meyer-type examples constructed by Bayer–Mumford and others). The problem is:

Identify natural classes $\mathcal{C}$ of homogeneous ideals $I \subseteq S$ defined by specific algebraic or geometric hypotheses (for example, prime ideals, radical ideals, ideals defining smooth/reduced/equidimensional/Cohen–Macaulay schemes, ideals with given codimension or singularity type, etc.), and for each such class, determine a sharp upper bound for $\mathrm{reg}(I)$ as a function of $d(I)$ (and possibly $n$ and $\mathrm{codim}(I)$) valid for all $I \in \mathcal{C}$, together with examples in $\mathcal{C}$ achieving the bound.
status_search_result: The problem of finding sharp upper bounds for the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of homogeneous ideals in terms of the maximal degree of a minimal generator, under various special hypotheses, is the subject of active research. Some classes have been resolved (e.g., bounds for log canonical local complete intersections, and certain monomial ideal classes), while the general question, including the Eisenbud–Goto conjecture (recently disproved in general by McCullough–Peeva but still open in restricted classes), remains open. No comprehensive sharp bound is known.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: Find classes of ideals I for which the regularity of the radical is no larger than the regularity of the ideal, reg(rad(I)) <= reg(I).
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S = k[x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n]$ the standard graded polynomial ring. For a homogeneous ideal $I \subseteq S$, let $\operatorname{reg}(I)$ denote the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $I$, that is, the smallest integer $m$ such that for every $i \geq 0$ and every $j > m + i$ one has $\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(I, k)_j = 0$ (equivalently, the minimal generators of the $i$-th syzygy module of $I$ have degree at most $m + i$). Let $\operatorname{rad}(I) = \sqrt{I}$ denote the radical of $I$.

In general, $\operatorname{reg}(\operatorname{rad}(I))$ can be strictly larger than $\operatorname{reg}(I)$. Identify and characterize broad classes of homogeneous ideals $I \subseteq S$ for which the inequality
$$\operatorname{reg}(\operatorname{rad}(I)) \leq \operatorname{reg}(I)$$
holds. In particular, find new sufficient conditions on $I$ (beyond the previously known cases such as monomial ideals, ideals with $S/I$ Buchsbaum, and certain ideals whose radical defines a smooth curve in $\mathbb{P}^3$) which guarantee this inequality.
status_search_result: The general inequality reg(rad(I)) ≤ reg(I) is known to fail (counterexamples by Chardin–D'Cruz), and it holds in specific classes (monomial ideals, Buchsbaum quotients, certain curves). Identifying further broad classes for which it holds remains an active and open line of investigation, with recent work (2025) still providing partial upper bounds for reg(rad(I)) in terms of reg(I) and related invariants.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: For finitely generated graded S-modules M and N, is reg(Tor_i^S(M,N)) bounded in terms of reg(M) and reg(N), perhaps after imposing additional hypotheses on M and N?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring over $k$, with the grading $\deg(x_i) = 1$. For a finitely generated graded $S$-module $M$ with minimal graded free resolution $\cdots \to F_1 \to F_0 \to M \to 0$ where $F_i = \bigoplus_j S(-j)^{\beta_{i,j}(M)}$, the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $M$ is defined as
$$\operatorname{reg}(M) = \sup\{\, j - i : \beta_{i,j}(M) \neq 0 \,\}.$$
For finitely generated graded $S$-modules $M$ and $N$, and for each integer $i \geq 0$, $\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M, N)$ is naturally a finitely generated graded $S$-module.

Question: Does there exist a function $f_i$ (possibly depending on $i$ and on $n$) such that
$$\operatorname{reg}\bigl(\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M, N)\bigr) \le f_i\bigl(\operatorname{reg}(M), \operatorname{reg}(N)\bigr)$$
holds for all finitely generated graded $S$-modules $M$ and $N$, possibly after imposing additional hypotheses on $M$ and $N$ (such as restrictions on the dimension of low-degree Tor modules)? If so, identify natural hypotheses under which such a bound exists and provide an explicit bound.
status_search_result: Bounds on $\operatorname{reg}(\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M,N))$ in terms of $\operatorname{reg}(M)$ and $\operatorname{reg}(N)$ are known under additional hypotheses; for example, Eisenbud–Huneke–Ulrich (2006) provide bounds when $\dim \operatorname{Tor}_1^S(M,N) \le 1$, and subsequent work (Caviglia, Chardin, and others) gives bounds in further special cases (such as when one module has finite projective dimension or when suitable dimension constraints on low Tor modules hold). In full generality, however, no such bound is known, and the general question remains open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: Find classes of ideals for which one can obtain useful upper bounds on the regularity of products of ideals in those classes.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $k$, graded in the standard way. For a homogeneous ideal $I \subseteq S$, let $\mathrm{reg}(I)$ denote the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $I$, defined as 
$$\mathrm{reg}(I) = \max\{ j - i : \beta_{i,j}(I) \neq 0 \},$$
where $\beta_{i,j}(I)$ are the graded Betti numbers of $I$.

In general, the regularity is not well-behaved under products: there exist homogeneous ideals $I, J$ for which $\mathrm{reg}(IJ) > \mathrm{reg}(I) + \mathrm{reg}(J)$, and no useful general upper bound is known relating $\mathrm{reg}(I_1 I_2 \cdots I_d)$ to invariants of the individual factors $I_1, \ldots, I_d$.

Identify natural classes $\mathcal{C}$ of homogeneous ideals in $S$ (for instance, classes defined by combinatorial, geometric, or homological conditions) for which one can prove useful upper bounds on $\mathrm{reg}(I_1 I_2 \cdots I_d)$ when $I_1, \ldots, I_d \in \mathcal{C}$, expressed in terms of natural invariants of $I_1, \ldots, I_d$ (such as their individual regularities, generating degrees, or combinatorial parameters describing them).
status_search_result: The problem is an open-ended research direction. Partial progress exists for specific classes: for edge ideals, upper bounds for products of two edge ideals in terms of co-chordal cover number have been established, and lower bounds for products of multiple edge ideals are known. However, a comprehensive identification of classes admitting useful upper bounds on regularity of products remains an active and largely open research direction.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: Fix natural numbers a1,...,ar. Does there exist a number p, depending only on these degrees, such that for every polynomial ring W over k and every homogeneous ideal J with minimal homogeneous generator degrees a1,...,ar, the projective dimension pd(W/J) is at most p, independently of the number of variables of W?
self_contained_problem: Fix a positive integer r and natural numbers a_1, a_2, ..., a_r. Does there exist a number p = p(a_1, ..., a_r), depending only on these degrees, such that for every field k, every polynomial ring W = k[x_1, ..., x_N] (in any number N of variables), and every homogeneous ideal J ⊂ W which admits a minimal homogeneous system of generators of degrees a_1, ..., a_r, the projective dimension pd(W/J) of W/J as a W-module satisfies pd(W/J) ≤ p, with the bound p independent of N?
status_search_result: This is Stillman's conjecture, proved by Ananyan and Hochster in 2016 ("Small Subalgebras of Polynomial Rings and Stillman's Conjecture", arXiv:1610.09268). They established the existence of a uniform upper bound for the projective dimension of any homogeneous ideal generated by forms of prescribed degrees, independent of the number of variables. Subsequent work (e.g., Erman–Sam–Snowden; explicit bounds papers) has refined and reproved the result.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: For a chosen class of homogeneous ideals, obtain good upper bounds on the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous Groebner basis.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $R = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ the standard graded polynomial ring. Fix a monomial order $\prec$ on $R$ (for instance, the degree reverse lexicographic order). For a homogeneous ideal $I \subseteq R$, let $G(I, \prec)$ denote a minimal homogeneous Gröbner basis of $I$ with respect to $\prec$, and define
\[
D(I, \prec) \;=\; \max\{\deg(g) : g \in G(I, \prec)\}.
\]
General upper bounds for $D(I, \prec)$ in terms of the number of variables and the maximum degree of a generating set of $I$ are known to be doubly exponential in $n$, but such bounds are far from tight on many natural families.

Problem. Identify interesting classes $\mathcal{C}$ of homogeneous ideals of $R$ (for example, ideals defined by combinatorial, geometric, or representation-theoretic data, ideals with prescribed Hilbert function, Cohen-Macaulay ideals, ideals of points, determinantal ideals, or ideals in generic coordinates) and, for each such class, prove sharp or substantially improved upper bounds on $D(I, \prec)$ in terms of natural invariants of $I$ (such as the number of variables, the degrees of minimal generators, the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, the projective dimension, the dimension, or the depth of $R/I$). In particular, for a chosen class $\mathcal{C}$ and a chosen monomial order $\prec$, produce an explicit function $f$ of these invariants such that $D(I, \prec) \le f(I)$ for every $I \in \mathcal{C}$, and exhibit examples showing the bound is sharp or near-sharp.
status_search_result: The problem is open-ended: while general doubly-exponential upper bounds (Dubé 1990) and various improvements (e.g., dimension- and depth-dependent bounds for ideals in strongly stable or quasi-stable position) are known, obtaining sharp bounds on the maximum degree of elements in minimal Gröbner bases for specific classes of homogeneous ideals remains an active research direction with no definitive answer.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: Study the properties of multigraded regularity for multigraded rings, ideals, and modules.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $k$, equipped with a multigrading by a finitely generated abelian group $A$ (so each variable $x_i$ is assigned a degree $a_i \in A$, and $\deg$ extends multiplicatively to monomials). Let $B \subseteq S$ be an irrelevant ideal (for example, the irrelevant ideal of a smooth projective toric variety whose Cox ring is $S$). For a finitely generated $A$-graded $S$-module $M$, the local cohomology modules $H^i_B(M)$ are again $A$-graded, and one may define the multigraded Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity $\operatorname{reg}(M) \subseteq A$ (as a subset, or "regularity region," of the grading group) by requiring that for every $i$ and every $\mathbf{p} \in \operatorname{reg}(M)$, the degree-$\mathbf{q}$ piece of $H^i_B(M)$ vanishes for all $\mathbf{q}$ in a prescribed translate of $\mathbf{p}$ depending on $i$.

Investigate the structural properties of this multigraded regularity region. In particular:

(a) Develop intrinsic characterizations of $\operatorname{reg}(M)$ in terms of the shifts appearing in a minimal multigraded free resolution of $M$, generalizing the classical equivalence between cohomological and resolution-theoretic definitions of regularity in the standard $\mathbb{Z}$-graded setting.

(b) Establish sharp bounds relating $\operatorname{reg}(M)$, $\operatorname{reg}(S/I)$, and $\operatorname{reg}(I)$ for an $A$-graded ideal $I \subseteq S$, including behavior under standard operations (sums, products, intersections, quotients, tensor products, and short exact sequences).

(c) Determine effective algorithms, in terms of Gröbner bases with respect to multigraded term orders, for computing $\operatorname{reg}(M)$ and for producing generators of $M$ in prescribed multidegrees lying in $\operatorname{reg}(M)$.

(d) Identify natural classes of multigraded rings, ideals, and modules (e.g., Stanley–Reisner ideals of simplicial complexes with multigradings, edge ideals of bipartite graphs, modules of equivariant sheaves on toric varieties) for which $\operatorname{reg}(M)$ admits a combinatorial or polyhedral description.
status_search_result: Multigraded Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity remains an active research topic. The foundational definition (Maclagan–Smith) has been extended and refined, with recent work on Klyachko filtrations (2021), Gröbner basis characterizations (2024), and sharp resolution-theoretic bounds. The problem is open-ended by nature, and many specific questions about computing and bounding multigraded regularity remain only partially resolved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: If a homogeneous ideal I in S contains a regular sequence of n quadratic forms, does there exist a monomial ideal containing x1^2,...,xn^2 with the same Hilbert function as I?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ the standard graded polynomial ring. For a homogeneous ideal $J \subseteq S$, its Hilbert function is $H_J(d) = \dim_k (S/J)_d$. A sequence $f_1, \dots, f_n \in S$ of homogeneous forms is called a regular sequence if, for each $i$, the image of $f_i$ in $S/(f_1, \dots, f_{i-1})$ is a nonzerodivisor.

Suppose $I \subseteq S$ is a homogeneous ideal that contains a regular sequence consisting of $n$ quadratic forms. Does there necessarily exist a monomial ideal $M \subseteq S$ such that $x_1^2, x_2^2, \dots, x_n^2 \in M$ and $H_M(d) = H_I(d)$ for every $d \geq 0$?
status_search_result: This is the quadratic (all degrees equal to 2) instance of the Eisenbud–Green–Harris conjecture. It remains open in general, but several partial results are known: the case n ≤ 4 was settled earlier, the case n = 5 was proved by Güntürkün and Hochster, and Caviglia–De Stefani proved cases of EGH for fast-growing degree sequences. Specialized cases (monomial regular sequences, ideals with extra structure) are also known to hold.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: For generic homogeneous forms f1,...,fr of prescribed degrees a1,...,ar, determine the generic initial ideal, with respect to reverse lexicographic order, of the ideal (f1,...,fr).
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an infinite field and let $S = k[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables, graded by total degree. Fix positive integers $r$ and $a_1, \ldots, a_r$. For homogeneous polynomials $f_1, \ldots, f_r \in S$ with $\deg f_i = a_i$, let $I = (f_1, \ldots, f_r)$. Consider the graded reverse lexicographic monomial order on $S$ (with $x_1 > x_2 > \cdots > x_n$), and let $\mathrm{gin}(I)$ denote the generic initial ideal of $I$ with respect to this order, that is, the initial ideal of $g \cdot I$ for a generic element $g$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(k)$ acting on $S$.

For a "generic" choice of the forms $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ (i.e., for $(f_1, \ldots, f_r)$ in a Zariski-dense open subset of the space of $r$-tuples of forms of degrees $a_1, \ldots, a_r$), give an explicit description of the monomial ideal $\mathrm{gin}(I) \subset S$ as a function of $n$, $r$, and the degree sequence $(a_1, \ldots, a_r)$.
status_search_result: The problem is the Moreno-Socías conjecture, which predicts that the generic initial ideal of a generic ideal under graded reverse lex is a specific weakly reverse-lexicographic ideal (which would also imply Fröberg's conjecture on Hilbert series). It is proved for n=2 (Moreno-Socías; Aguirre–Jouanolou–Mourrain et al.), n=3 (Cimpoeaș), n=4 (Harima–Wachi), and for degree sequences satisfying d_i > Σ(d_j − i + 1) (Cho–Park). The general case remains open, with recent work (e.g., 2025 preprints) studying variations and additional partial cases.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: For quotient rings R = S/I where I is a monomial ideal or projective toric ideal, find classes of I for which Macaulay-type behavior holds over R: every Hilbert function over R is attained by a lex ideal in R.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $k$, graded by total degree, and let $I \subset S$ be a homogeneous ideal. The quotient $R = S/I$ inherits a standard grading. A monomial ideal $L \subset S$ containing $I$ is called a lex ideal in $R$ if, for every monomial $m \in L$ and every monomial $m'$ of the same degree with $m' \geq_{\mathrm{lex}} m$ (in the lexicographic order on monomials of $S$), one has $m' \in L$. The Hilbert function of a graded $R$-module $M$ is $H_M(d) = \dim_k M_d$.

The ring $R$ is said to be Macaulay-Lex if for every homogeneous ideal $J \subset R$ there exists a lex ideal $L \subset R$ with $H_{R/J} = H_{R/L}$; equivalently, every Hilbert function of a graded quotient of $R$ is attained by a lex ideal in $R$.

Problem. Identify and characterize broad classes of ideals $I \subset S$ for which $R = S/I$ is Macaulay-Lex, in each of the following settings:
(a) $I$ is a monomial ideal of $S$;
(b) $I$ is the homogeneous ideal defining a projective toric variety (i.e., the kernel of a homomorphism $S \to k[t_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, t_m^{\pm 1}]$ sending each $x_i$ to a Laurent monomial, all of the same degree under some grading).

Find general structural conditions on $I$ (combinatorial in case (a), or in terms of the associated lattice/semigroup data in case (b)) that are sufficient, and ideally necessary, for $R$ to be Macaulay-Lex.
status_search_result: The problem remains open in general. Known Macaulay-Lex classes include the Clements–Lindström rings (quotients by powers of variables), squarefree analogues, and certain colored quotient rings (Mermin–Murai and others, ca. 2008–2014). For projective toric rings, Gasharov–Horwitz–Peeva (2008) gave partial sufficient conditions, but no general classification of monomial or toric ideals giving Macaulay-Lex quotients is known.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: Let R = S/I, where I is a monomial ideal or projective toric ideal. For a graded ideal J in R and a lex ideal L with the same Hilbert function, determine when J can be connected to L by a sequence of deformations, and describe the Hilbert scheme parametrizing graded ideals in R with that Hilbert function.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the standard graded polynomial ring. Let $I\subset S$ be either a monomial ideal or the toric ideal of a projective toric variety, and set $R=S/I$. A graded ideal $L\subset R$ is called a lex ideal in $R$ if, in each degree $d$, the set of monomials in $L_d$ (under a chosen monomial $k$-basis of $R$) is an initial segment of the monomials of $R_d$ in the lexicographic order. Assume that the Hilbert function $H$ is attained by some lex ideal $L\subset R$.

Consider the Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}^H(R)$ parametrizing graded ideals $J\subset R$ with Hilbert function $H_{R/J}$ equal to the prescribed function determined by $H$.

(a) Give conditions on $R$ (i.e.\ on $I$) and on a graded ideal $J\subset R$ with this Hilbert function under which $J$ can be connected to $L$ by a sequence of flat deformations within $\mathrm{Hilb}^H(R)$; in particular, determine when $\mathrm{Hilb}^H(R)$ is connected.

(b) Describe the geometric structure of $\mathrm{Hilb}^H(R)$ (irreducible components, dimension, smoothness at $L$, etc.) for the classes of monomial or projective toric ideals $I$ in question.
status_search_result: This is a broad open research problem on lex ideals over quotient rings (monomial or toric) and the structure of associated Hilbert schemes. Macaulay's theorem and Hartshorne's connectedness result are classical for $S$ itself, but analogues over quotients $R=S/I$ for general monomial or projective toric $I$ remain open; only partial classes have been treated (e.g., quotients by certain monomial ideals where Macaulay-type theorems are known).

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: If a graded ideal J in S contains a regular sequence of homogeneous elements of degrees a1,...,aj and there is a lex-plus-powers ideal L containing x1^a1,...,xj^aj with the same Hilbert function as J, are all Betti numbers of L at least the corresponding Betti numbers of J?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ the polynomial ring with the standard grading $\deg(x_i) = 1$. Order monomials of each degree by the lexicographic order with $x_1 > x_2 > \cdots > x_n$. A monomial ideal $L \subseteq S$ is called a **lex ideal** if, in every degree $d$, the set of monomials of degree $d$ in $L$ is an initial segment under the lex order. Given integers $2 \le a_1 \le a_2 \le \cdots \le a_j$ with $j \le n$, a graded ideal $L \subseteq S$ is called a **lex-plus-powers ideal** (with respect to $a_1, \dots, a_j$) if $L = L' + (x_1^{a_1}, x_2^{a_2}, \dots, x_j^{a_j})$, where $L'$ is a lex ideal.

For a finitely generated graded $S$-module $M$, the **graded Betti numbers** are $\beta_{i,j}^S(M) = \dim_k \mathrm{Tor}_i^S(M,k)_j$.

**Problem.** Let $J \subseteq S$ be a graded ideal that contains a regular sequence of homogeneous elements of degrees $a_1, \dots, a_j$. Suppose $L \subseteq S$ is a lex-plus-powers ideal containing $x_1^{a_1}, \dots, x_j^{a_j}$ that has the same Hilbert function as $J$. Is it true that
$$\beta_{i,j}^S(S/L) \;\ge\; \beta_{i,j}^S(S/J) \qquad \text{for all } i, j \, ?$$
category_tag: Lex-plus-powers ideals and graded Betti numbers
status_search_result: The Lex-plus-powers Conjecture (attributed to Evans, with versions by Charalambous–Evans) remains open in general. Substantial partial results are known: Mermin–Murai proved the case where the regular sequence consists of monomials (pure powers); Caviglia–Sammartano (2018) established the conjecture in characteristic zero for regular sequences whose degrees satisfy a growth condition; the almost-complete-intersection case for graded Betti numbers and the case of dimension ≤ 2 are also known. paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: For a fixed Hilbert function, does there exist an ideal with greatest graded Betti numbers among all Gorenstein artinian graded ideals having that Hilbert function?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and $R = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ the standard graded polynomial ring. A homogeneous ideal $I \subset R$ is called Gorenstein artinian if $R/I$ is an artinian Gorenstein $k$-algebra. The Hilbert function of $R/I$ is $h_{R/I}(t) = \dim_k (R/I)_t$, and the graded Betti numbers of $R/I$ are $\beta_{i,j}(R/I) = \dim_k \mathrm{Tor}^R_i(R/I,k)_j$.

Fix a function $h: \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ that arises as the Hilbert function of some Gorenstein artinian graded quotient of $R$. Consider the family $\mathcal{G}(h)$ of all Gorenstein artinian graded ideals $I \subset R$ with $h_{R/I} = h$.

Question: Does there exist an ideal $I^* \in \mathcal{G}(h)$ whose graded Betti numbers are simultaneously maximal in the family, i.e. such that $\beta_{i,j}(R/I^*) \geq \beta_{i,j}(R/I)$ for every $i, j$ and every $I \in \mathcal{G}(h)$?

status_search_result: Migliore and Nagel (2003) showed that for any SI-sequence, there is an arithmetically Gorenstein scheme whose artinian reduction has the weak Lefschetz property (WLP) and attains maximal graded Betti numbers among all such Gorenstein algebras with WLP and the given Hilbert function. The full question, without the WLP assumption and for arbitrary admissible Gorenstein Hilbert functions, does not appear to have been settled in the literature.

original_question: For every artinian graded finitely generated S-module M, are the total Betti numbers bounded below by the Koszul ranks, b_i^S(M) >= binomial(n,i) for all i >= 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field and $S = K[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ the standard graded polynomial ring in $n$ variables. For a finitely generated graded $S$-module $M$, let
$$b_i^S(M) = \dim_K \mathrm{Tor}_i^S(M, K)$$
denote the $i$-th total Betti number of $M$ (the rank of the $i$-th free module in the minimal graded free resolution of $M$ over $S$).

Assume $M$ is artinian (equivalently, $\dim_K M < \infty$). Determine whether the inequality
$$b_i^S(M) \;\geq\; \binom{n}{i}$$
holds for every $i \geq 0$ and every such artinian graded finitely generated $S$-module $M$.
status_search_result: This is the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks rank conjecture (pointwise version). The weaker total rank conjecture, that the sum of Betti numbers is at least $2^n$, was proven by Mark Walker (Annals of Math, 2017) for modules of finite projective dimension over local rings containing a field where 2 is invertible. The stronger pointwise bound $b_i \geq \binom{n}{i}$ remains open in general, with only special cases established (e.g., Charalambous–Evans for certain cases, and partial results by Erman and others).

original_question: For every artinian graded finitely generated S-module M, is the sum of all total Betti numbers at least 2^n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field, let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables with its standard grading, and let $M$ be a finitely generated graded $S$-module. Assume that $M$ is artinian (equivalently, $\dim_k M < \infty$). For each $i \geq 0$, let
$$\beta_i(M) = \dim_k \operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M, k)$$
denote the $i$-th total Betti number of $M$, which equals the rank of the $i$-th free module in the minimal graded free resolution of $M$ over $S$.

Prove or disprove: for every such artinian graded finitely generated $S$-module $M$,
$$\sum_{i=0}^{n} \beta_i(M) \;\geq\; 2^n.$$
status_search_result: This is the Total Rank Conjecture (a weakening of the Buchsbaum–Eisenbud–Horrocks rank conjecture). paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: Determine how the length of the linear strand in the minimal graded free resolution of S/I is related to other invariants of S/I.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $k$, graded in the standard way with $\deg(x_i) = 1$, and let $I \subseteq S$ be a homogeneous ideal. Consider the minimal graded free resolution of the quotient $S/I$:
$$\cdots \to F_2 \to F_1 \to F_0 \to S/I \to 0, \qquad F_i = \bigoplus_j S(-j)^{\beta_{i,j}(S/I)}.$$
The linear strand of this resolution is the subcomplex consisting of those summands $S(-(i+d-1))^{\beta_{i,i+d-1}(S/I)}$ in homological degree $i$, where $d$ is the smallest degree of a minimal generator of $I$; equivalently, it records the Betti numbers $\beta_{i,i+d-1}(S/I)$. The length of the linear strand is the largest $i$ such that $\beta_{i,i+d-1}(S/I) \neq 0$.

Determine how the length of the linear strand of the minimal graded free resolution of $S/I$ is related to other homological and algebraic invariants of $S/I$ (such as projective dimension, regularity, depth, dimension, Hilbert function, or invariants of the generating degrees of $I$).
category_tag: Minimal free resolutions and linear strands
status_search_result: This is posed as an open-ended problem about relating the length of the linear strand of a minimal free resolution to other invariants of $S/I$. While specific results exist (e.g., bounds via regularity, results for edge ideals and componentwise linear ideals, and the linear strand of monomial/Stanley–Reisner ideals studied by Eisenbud–Fløystad–Schreyer, Herzog–Hibi, and others), no general structural answer is known, and the problem is broadly phrased and remains open.

original_question: Let r,q >= 3, let V be the q-th Veronese ring in r variables, and let N_p be the usual syzygy vanishing property. If p <= 3q - 3, does V satisfy N_p?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers r, q ≥ 3. Let S = k[x_1,...,x_r] be a polynomial ring over a field k, and let V = ⊕_{d≥0} S_{qd} denote the q-th Veronese subring of S (equivalently, the homogeneous coordinate ring of the q-th Veronese embedding of P^{r-1}). View V as a graded module over the polynomial ring R generated in degree 1 by a basis of S_q (so V is a quotient of R by the ideal of Veronese relations).

Recall Green–Lazarsfeld's property N_p: a projectively normal graded algebra V (with minimal free R-resolution F_•) is said to satisfy N_p if F_0 = R, and for every 1 ≤ i ≤ p the i-th term F_i is generated in degree i+1, i.e. all syzygies up to homological degree p are linear.

Question: For every integer p with 1 ≤ p ≤ 3q − 3, does the q-th Veronese ring V in r variables satisfy property N_p?
status_search_result: This is the Ottaviani–Paoletti conjecture (1998). Ottaviani and Paoletti proved the bound is sharp (failure of N_{3q-2}) and verified the conjecture for r = 3 (all q) and for (r,q) = (4,3). Greco and Martino later established N_6 for the third Veronese embeddings (q = 3, all r), confirming the conjecture in that case. The general case for r ≥ 5 and q ≥ 4 remains open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: When the positions of potentially nonzero Betti numbers are restricted, describe the generators of the semigroup of Betti diagrams of graded finitely generated S-modules.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring over a field $k$. For a finitely generated graded $S$-module $M$, let $\beta_{i,j}(M) = \dim_k \mathrm{Tor}_i^S(M,k)_j$ denote its graded Betti numbers, and let $\beta(M) = (\beta_{i,j}(M))_{i,j}$ be its Betti diagram, viewed as an element of the free abelian monoid on positions $(i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \times \mathbb{Z}$.

Fix a subset $P \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \times \mathbb{Z}$ of "allowed positions." Define
$$B_P = \{\beta(M) : M \text{ is a finitely generated graded } S\text{-module with } \beta_{i,j}(M) = 0 \text{ for all } (i,j) \notin P\}.$$
Then $B_P$ is a sub-semigroup of $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{P}$ under addition (since direct sums add Betti diagrams).

Problem: For natural choices of restriction set $P$ on the positions where Betti numbers are allowed to be nonzero, describe an explicit set of generators of the semigroup $B_P$.

The problem appears to remain open in general.

original_question: Given a Hilbert function for a set of points in P^{n-1}, determine the possible graded Betti numbers of the defining ideals of point sets with that Hilbert function.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $R = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the homogeneous coordinate ring of projective space $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. For a finite set of points $X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$, let $I_X \subset R$ be its (saturated) defining homogeneous ideal, and let $A_X = R/I_X$ be its homogeneous coordinate ring. The Hilbert function of $X$ is $H_X(t) = \dim_k (A_X)_t$. The minimal graded free resolution of $I_X$ has the form
$$0 \to \bigoplus_j R(-j)^{\beta_{p,j}} \to \cdots \to \bigoplus_j R(-j)^{\beta_{1,j}} \to I_X \to 0,$$
and the integers $\beta_{i,j}(I_X) = \dim_k \operatorname{Tor}_i^R(I_X, k)_j$ are the graded Betti numbers of $I_X$.

Partial results are known (e.g., for small numbers of points, points on a conic, Gorenstein configurations after Diesel/Geramita), but no general characterization is known. The problem remains open in general.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: If X is a generic set of q points in P^{n-1}, is the defining ideal of X generated in degree one more than the least degree d for which the Hilbert function of X equals q?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $S = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring, viewed as the homogeneous coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. For a finite set of points $X \subseteq \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$, let $I_X \subseteq S$ denote its (saturated) homogeneous defining ideal, and let $H_X(t) = \dim_k (S/I_X)_t$ denote its Hilbert function. A set $X$ of $q$ points in $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ is said to be in generic (general) position when $H_X(t) = \min\{\binom{t+n-1}{n-1},\, q\}$ for every $t \ge 0$. Define $d = d(q,n)$ to be the least nonnegative integer such that $H_X(d) = q$, equivalently the smallest degree in which the Hilbert function attains its eventual value $q$.

Question (Ideal Generation Conjecture): For a generic set $X$ of $q$ points in $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$, is the homogeneous ideal $I_X$ minimally generated in degrees $d$ and $d+1$ only? Equivalently, are all minimal generators of $I_X$ of degree at most $d+1$?

The Minimal Resolution Conjecture (which implies the Ideal Generation Conjecture) is known to fail for sufficiently many points in $\mathbb{P}^n$ with $n \ge 6$ (Eisenbud–Popescu), but counterexamples to the Ideal Generation Conjecture itself are not established in general, and the conjecture remains open in many cases.
