paper_title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems
context_brief: Auxiliary operators for CCS parallel composition
original_question: Does there exist one binary auxiliary operator that preserves bisimulation equivalence and whose addition to the recursion-free fragment of CCS is sufficient to obtain a finite equational axiomatization of the parallel composition operator? Equivalently, prove or refute the conjecture that no single binary operation can finitely axiomatize parallel composition up to bisimulation, so that two auxiliary operators such as left merge and communication merge are necessary.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the recursion-free fragment of Milner's Calculus of Communicating Systems (CCS), built from the constants 0 (inaction) and the action prefixes a. (for a in a given set of actions Act including a complementation involution and a silent action τ), with binary operators + (nondeterministic choice) and ∥ (parallel composition / merge), interpreted operationally by the usual structural operational semantics and compared modulo strong bisimulation equivalence. It is known (Bergstra–Klop) that adding the two binary auxiliary operators "left merge" ⌊ and "communication merge" ∣ yields a finite, sound and ground-complete equational axiomatization of bisimilarity. It is also known (Moller) that no finite equational axiomatization of ∥ exists over the pure recursion-free CCS signature modulo bisimilarity, and (Aceto et al.) that Hennessy's single binary merge does not yield such a finite axiomatization either.

Question: Does there exist a single binary operator f, definable by a set of structural operational semantics rules so that bisimilarity is a congruence with respect to f, such that the equational theory of bisimilarity over the recursion-free fragment of CCS enriched with f admits a finite, sound, and ground-complete equational axiomatization (in particular, finitely axiomatizing the parallel composition ∥)?

Equivalently, prove or refute the conjecture that no such single binary auxiliary operator exists, so that at least two auxiliary binary operators (such as left merge and communication merge) are necessary for a finite equational axiomatization of parallel composition modulo bisimilarity.
status_search_result: The conjecture is not yet resolved in full generality, but significant partial progress has been made. Aceto, Castiglioni, Fokkink, Ingolfsdottir, and Luttik (CSL 2021; ACM TOCL 2022; arXiv:2010.01943) formulate three natural assumptions on the SOS rules of an auxiliary binary operator and prove that no operator satisfying all three assumptions can yield a finite ground-complete axiomatisation of bisimilarity over recursion-free CCS. The general question for arbitrary single binary auxiliary operators (without those assumptions) remains open.

paper_title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems
context_brief: Observation congruence over a CCS fragment
original_question: Prove that observation congruence is not finitely equationally axiomatizable over the fragment of CCS that excludes recursion, relabelling, and restriction.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the fragment of Milner's Calculus of Communicating Systems (CCS) generated by the grammar
  P ::= 0 | x | a.P | τ.P | P + P | P | P,
where a ranges over a fixed countable set of visible (observable) actions A, τ is the distinguished silent (internal) action, x ranges over a countable set of process variables, "0" is the inactive process, "a.P" and "τ.P" are action prefixing, "+" is nondeterministic choice, and "|" is the parallel composition operator (allowing communication between matching co-actions a and ā). The fragment explicitly excludes recursion, the relabelling operator, and the restriction operator.

The operational semantics is the standard one for CCS, generating a labelled transition system whose labels are A ∪ {ā : a ∈ A} ∪ {τ}. Weak bisimilarity ≈ is defined as the largest symmetric relation R such that whenever P R Q and P →^a P', there exists Q' with Q ⇒^a Q' and P' R Q', where ⇒^a denotes the weak transition relation (sequences of τ-transitions surrounding the action a, with τ-transitions absorbed when a = τ). Observation congruence ≈^c is the largest congruence (with respect to all operators of the fragment) that is included in weak bisimilarity; equivalently, P ≈^c Q iff for every action μ, P →^μ P' implies Q ⇒^μ Q' with P' ≈ Q', and symmetrically.

A finite equational axiomatization of ≈^c over this fragment is a finite set E of equations between open terms of the fragment such that for all closed terms P, Q of the fragment, E ⊢ P = Q (using the standard rules of equational logic) iff P ≈^c Q.

Problem: Prove that no such finite equational axiomatization exists; equivalently, show that observation congruence is not finitely equationally axiomatizable over the recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free fragment of CCS.
status_search_result: Surveys and follow-up work on equational axiomatizations of CCS-style parallel composition explicitly list the non-finite-axiomatizability of observation (weak) congruence over the recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free fragment of CCS as an open problem, with the negative answer only conjectured. Related results have been obtained for strong bisimilarity (Moller's negative result) and for branching bisimilarity, and finite bases exist when auxiliary operators (left merge, communication merge) are added, but no resolution of the observation-congruence case over the pure CCS fragment has been found in the literature through 2026.

original_question: In the category of real Banach spaces, is the Kalton-Peck space Z2 even, meaning that Z2 admits a bounded operator J with J^2 = -I_Z2, while no hyperplane of Z2 admits such a complex structure?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the category of real Banach spaces. The Kalton–Peck space $Z_2$ is the twisted Hilbert space defined as
$$Z_2 \;=\; \{(\omega,x)\in\omega(\mathbb{N})\times\ell_2 \;:\; \omega - K(x)\in\ell_2\},$$
where $K\colon c_{00}\to\omega(\mathbb{N})$ is the Kalton–Peck map $K(x)_n = x_n\log(|x_n|/\|x\|_2)$ (with $K(0)=0$), equipped with the quasi-norm $\|(\omega,x)\|_{Z_2}=\|\omega-K(x)\|_2+\|x\|_2$, which is equivalent to a norm making $Z_2$ a real Banach space. A real Banach space $X$ is called even if it admits a bounded linear operator $J\colon X\to X$ with $J^2=-I_X$ (equivalently, $X$ carries a complex Banach space structure compatible with its real structure).

Decide whether the following holds:
(a) $Z_2$ is even, i.e., there exists a bounded linear operator $J\colon Z_2\to Z_2$ with $J^2=-I_{Z_2}$.
(b) No closed hyperplane of $Z_2$ is even; that is, for every closed subspace $H\subset Z_2$ of codimension $1$, there is no bounded linear operator $J\colon H\to H$ with $J^2=-I_H$.
category_tag: Twisted Hilbert spaces and complex structures
status_search_result: Partial progress exists. It is known that the natural complex structures on $\ell_2$ do not extend to complex structures on hyperplanes of $Z_2$ containing $\ell_2$, and the complexification description of $Z_2$ has been clarified (the complex Kalton–Peck space equals the complexification of the real one). However, the full conjecture — that $Z_2$ itself is even while no hyperplane of $Z_2$ admits any complex structure — does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature retrieved.

Let $X$ be a Banach lattice and $Y$ a Banach space. A bounded linear operator $T : X \to Y$ is called:
(i) lattice-strictly singular if the restriction of $T$ to any infinite-dimensional sublattice of $X$ fails to be an isomorphism onto its image;
(ii) disjointly strictly singular if the restriction of $T$ to the closed linear span of any pairwise disjoint sequence in $X$ fails to be an isomorphism onto its image.

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
original_question: Let A be a real symmetric entrywise nonnegative n x n matrix, and let G(A) be the graph with vertices 1,...,n and an edge between i and j exactly when i != j and a_ij != 0. Which additional checkable conditions, whether depending on G(A) or not depending on G(A), can be found to determine or certify complete positivity of A, where complete positivity means A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative matrix B?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a real symmetric $n \times n$ matrix with nonnegative entries. Define the graph $G(A)$ on the vertex set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ in which $\{i,j\}$ is an edge precisely when $i \neq j$ and $a_{ij} \neq 0$. The matrix $A$ is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative (not necessarily square) matrix $B$ such that $A = BB^{T}$.

Find additional checkable conditions—either depending on the graph $G(A)$ or independent of it—that determine, or at least certify, the complete positivity of $A$. More precisely, identify nontrivial sufficient conditions (or necessary and sufficient conditions valid on suitable subclasses of nonnegative symmetric matrices) for $A = BB^{T}$ with $B \geq 0$ entrywise, going beyond the currently known criteria such as diagonal dominance, positive semidefiniteness of the comparison matrix, or the characterization that every doubly nonnegative realization of $G$ is completely positive iff $G$ contains no odd cycle of length $\geq 5$.

Recent work continues to propose new sufficient conditions but does not resolve the general question.

$$\mathrm{CP}_n = \{A \in \mathcal{S}^n : A = BB^T \text{ for some entrywise nonnegative matrix } B\}.$$

A face $F$ of a closed convex cone $K$ is a convex subcone with the property that whenever a line segment in $K$ has an interior (relative) point lying in $F$, both endpoints of the segment lie in $F$.

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
original_question: For each finite n > 2, compute the maximal angle theta_max(COP_n) and the maximal angle theta_max(PSD_n + N_n), where COP_n is the copositive cone, PSD_n is the cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite n x n matrices, N_n is the cone of real symmetric entrywise nonnegative n x n matrices, and theta_max(K) is the maximum of arccos(trace(XY)) over unit-norm X,Y in the cone K. Are these maximal angles always attained by a pair of matrices P in PSD_n and N in N_n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n>2$ be an integer. Equip the space $S_n$ of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices with the Frobenius inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle = \operatorname{tr}(XY)$ and the induced norm $\|X\| = \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(X^2)}$. Define the following closed convex cones in $S_n$:

- $\operatorname{PSD}_n = \{X \in S_n : v^\top X v \ge 0 \text{ for all } v \in \mathbb{R}^n\}$, the cone of positive semidefinite matrices.
- $N_n = \{X \in S_n : X_{ij} \ge 0 \text{ for all } i,j\}$, the cone of symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrices.
- $\operatorname{COP}_n = \{X \in S_n : v^\top X v \ge 0 \text{ for all } v \in \mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}\}$, the copositive cone.
- $\operatorname{PSD}_n + N_n = \{P + N : P \in \operatorname{PSD}_n,\ N \in N_n\}$.

For a closed convex cone $K \subseteq S_n$ define its maximal angle
$$\theta_{\max}(K) = \sup\{\arccos(\operatorname{tr}(XY)) : X,Y \in K,\ \|X\|=\|Y\|=1\}.$$

(a) Determine $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_n)$ in closed form for every finite $n > 2$.

(b) Determine $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{PSD}_n + N_n)$ in closed form for every finite $n > 2$.

(c) Decide whether, for every finite $n > 2$, the supremum defining $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{PSD}_n + N_n)$ is attained at a pair of unit-norm matrices of the form $X = P_1 + N_1$, $Y = P_2 + N_2$ in which the optimizing extremal pair can be chosen with one matrix in $\operatorname{PSD}_n$ and the other in $N_n$.
status_search_result: The problem is generally open for finite $n>2$. The case $n=2$ was settled by Hiriart-Urruty and Seeger (2010), who showed $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_2)=3\pi/4$. The case $n=3$ was resolved in a 2025 paper (Optimization Letters / arXiv:2501.03773), which proved $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_3)=3\pi/4$ and characterized all extremal pairs. No closed-form results for $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{COP}_n)$ or $\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{PSD}_n+N_n)$ are known for $n\ge 4$, and the question of attainment by a PSD/nonnegative pair remains open in general.

For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, a completely positive realization of $G$ is a matrix $A\in CP_n$ with $G(A) = G$. Define
$$\mathrm{cpr}(G) := \sup\{\mathrm{cp\text{-}rank}(A): A\in CP_n,\ G(A)=G\},$$

$$\mathrm{tf}(G) := \max\{|E(H)|: H \text{ is a triangle-free subgraph of } G\}.$$

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
original_question: Given a real symmetric matrix X that is not in CP_n, construct a copositive matrix Y in COP_n such that trace(XY) < 0. Here CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative, and COP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices Y satisfying z^T Y z >= 0 for every z in R_+^n; such a Y gives a cutting plane separating X from CP_n.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}^n$ denote the space of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices, and let $\mathbb{R}_+^n$ denote the nonnegative orthant of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Define the cone of completely positive matrices
$$\mathrm{CP}_n := \{A\in\mathcal{S}^n : A = BB^T \text{ for some entrywise nonnegative matrix } B\},$$
and the cone of copositive matrices
$$\mathrm{COP}_n := \{Y\in\mathcal{S}^n : z^T Y z \ge 0 \text{ for all } z\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\}.$$
These cones are dual with respect to the trace inner product $\langle X, Y\rangle = \mathrm{tr}(XY)$.

Problem. Devise a constructive procedure with the following property: given any symmetric matrix $X\in\mathcal{S}^n$ that does not lie in $\mathrm{CP}_n$, the procedure produces a copositive matrix $Y\in\mathrm{COP}_n$ such that
$$\mathrm{tr}(XY) < 0.$$
Such a $Y$ furnishes a separating hyperplane (a cutting plane) between $X$ and the completely positive cone $\mathrm{CP}_n$.
status_search_result: Several partial results address this separation question. Berman and Dür gave explicit constructions of separating copositive cuts for $5\times 5$ doubly nonnegative but non-completely-positive matrices. Bundfuss–Dür and Sponsel–Dür developed factorization and cutting-plane methods using polyhedral inner/outer approximations of the cones, and an analytic center cutting plane method (Badenbroek–de Klerk, 2020) detects non-membership and returns a separating cut, with the membership oracle reducing to a mixed-integer linear program. A general efficient/explicit construction valid for arbitrary $n$ remains elusive, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
original_question: Let L be a positive continuous function and use the bounded directional L-index definition: H has bounded L-index in direction c if the normalized directional derivatives |D_c^m H(z)|/(m! L(z)^m) are controlled, for all m and z, by finitely many orders 0 <= k <= m0. If g(z1,z2) is an entire function of bounded L-index in both directions b1 and b2, what positive function L* and direction b* ensure that an entire solution F of the mixed directional equation D_b1 D_b2 F(z1,z2) = g(z1,z2) has bounded L*-index in direction b*?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L: \mathbb{C}^2 \to (0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function and fix a nonzero direction $b \in \mathbb{C}^2$. For an entire function $H: \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}$, define the directional derivatives recursively by $D_b^0 H = H$ and $D_b^{m} H(z) = \langle \nabla D_b^{m-1} H(z), b \rangle$ for $m \geq 1$. The function $H$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m_0$ such that for every $m \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and every $z \in \mathbb{C}^2$,
$$\frac{|D_b^m H(z)|}{m!\, L(z)^m} \leq \max_{0 \leq k \leq m_0} \frac{|D_b^k H(z)|}{k!\, L(z)^k}.$$
The least such $m_0$ is the $L$-index of $H$ in the direction $b$.

Suppose $g: \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ is an entire function that has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b_1$ and also has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b_2$, where $b_1, b_2 \in \mathbb{C}^2 \setminus \{0\}$ are given. 

Determine a positive continuous function $L^*: \mathbb{C}^2 \to (0,\infty)$ and a nonzero direction $b^* \in \mathbb{C}^2$ (expressible in terms of $L$, $b_1$, $b_2$) such that every entire solution $F: \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ of the mixed directional differential equation
$$D_{b_1} D_{b_2} F(z_1, z_2) = g(z_1, z_2)$$
necessarily has bounded $L^*$-index in the direction $b^*$.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
original_question: For an entire function of two variables f(z,w), assume f has bounded L-index in the two coordinate directions (1,0) and (0,1), meaning that in each direction its normalized directional derivatives are controlled by finitely many lower orders using the positive function L. For the ordinary differential equation w'(z) = f(z,w(z)), what one-variable positive function l should be chosen, and under what conditions, so that an entire solution w has bounded l-index in the ordinary one-variable sense?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function of two complex variables, and let $L:\mathbb{C}^2\to(0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function. For a unit direction $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^2$, the directional derivative of order $k$ at $(z,w)$ is $\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}} f(z,w)=\frac{d^k}{dt^k}f((z,w)+t\mathbf{b})\big|_{t=0}$. We say that $f$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $(z,w)\in\mathbb{C}^2$ and every $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$,
$$\frac{|\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}} f(z,w)|}{k!\,L(z,w)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le N}\frac{|\partial^j_{\mathbf{b}} f(z,w)|}{j!\,L(z,w)^j}.$$
Assume that $f$ has bounded $L$-index in each of the two coordinate directions $\mathbf{b}_1=(1,0)$ and $\mathbf{b}_2=(0,1)$.

For a positive continuous function $l:\mathbb{C}\to(0,\infty)$, an entire function $g:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ has bounded $l$-index (in the ordinary one-variable sense) if there exists $M\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $z\in\mathbb{C}$ and all $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$,
$$\frac{|g^{(k)}(z)|}{k!\,l(z)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le M}\frac{|g^{(j)}(z)|}{j!\,l(z)^j}.$$

Consider the ordinary differential equation
$$w'(z)=f(z,w(z)),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C},$$
and suppose $w$ is an entire solution.

Problem: Determine an explicit choice of the one-variable positive function $l$ (in terms of $L$, $f$, $w$) and sufficient conditions on $f$, $L$, and $w$ under which $w$ necessarily has bounded $l$-index in the ordinary one-variable sense.

However, no source explicitly resolves this problem in full generality (specifying a canonical choice of one-variable $l$ for general bivariate $f$ with bounded $L$-index in both coordinate directions, for the ODE $w'=f(z,w)$). The problem appears to remain open in full generality, though partial results exist for related PDE/ODE settings.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
original_question: Let L be a positive continuous function in the class Q_b^n, meaning that along every complex line z + tb in direction b the ratios L(z+tb)/L(z+t0 b) are bounded above and below away from 0 on scaled discs |t-t0| <= eta/L(z+t0 b), uniformly in z and t0 for each eta. For an entire function F on C^n, is bounded L-index in direction b equivalent to the following single-scale maximum-minimum condition: there exist R > 0, P2(R) >= 1, and eta(R) in (0,R) such that for every z0 in C^n and t0 in C, some r in [eta(R),R] satisfies max{|F(z0+tb)| : |t-t0| = r/L(z0+t0 b)} <= P2(R) min{|F(z0+tb)| : |t-t0| = r/L(z0+t0 b)}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $b\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ be a fixed direction. Denote by $Q_b^n$ the class of positive continuous functions $L\colon \mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$ satisfying the following regularity along every complex line in direction $b$: for every $\eta>0$ there exists $\lambda(\eta)\geq 1$ such that
$$\lambda(\eta)^{-1}\;\leq\;\frac{L(z+tb)}{L(z+t_0 b)}\;\leq\;\lambda(\eta)$$
for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$, all $t_0\in\mathbb{C}$, and all $t\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|t-t_0|\leq \eta/L(z+t_0 b)$.

An entire function $F\colon\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$,
$$\frac{|\partial_b^m F(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\;\leq\;\max_{0\leq k\leq N}\frac{|\partial_b^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k},$$
where $\partial_b F(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\,\partial F/\partial z_j$ and $\partial_b^m$ denotes its $m$-th iterate.

Question: Is it true that an entire function $F$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if and only if there exist constants $R>0$, $P_2(R)\geq 1$, and $\eta(R)\in(0,R)$ such that for every $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and every $t_0\in\mathbb{C}$ there exists $r\in[\eta(R),R]$ with
$$\max\bigl\{|F(z_0+tb)|:|t-t_0|=r/L(z_0+t_0 b)\bigr\}\;\leq\;P_2(R)\,\min\bigl\{|F(z_0+tb)|:|t-t_0|=r/L(z_0+t_0 b)\bigr\}\,?$$

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
original_question: For entire functions on C^n and a positive continuous function L, what is the smallest or least set A of directions with the following property: whenever an entire function F has bounded L-index in every direction b in A, it follows that F has bounded L-index in every nonzero direction b in C^n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $L : \mathbb{C}^n \to (0,\infty)$ be a positive continuous function. For an entire function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ and a nonzero direction $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$, the function $F$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m_0$ such that, for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\frac{|\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}} F(z)|}{k!\, L(z)^k} \leq \max_{0 \leq j \leq m_0} \frac{|\partial^j_{\mathbf{b}} F(z)|}{j!\, L(z)^j} \qquad \text{for all } k \in \mathbb{N}_0,$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}} F(z) = \sum_{i=1}^n b_i \frac{\partial F}{\partial z_i}(z)$ is the directional derivative and $\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}}$ denotes its $k$-th iterate. The least such $m_0$ is called the $L$-index of $F$ in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.

Determine the smallest (in the sense of inclusion, or of minimal cardinality) subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$ with the following property: for every entire function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$, if $F$ has bounded $L$-index in every direction $\mathbf{b} \in A$, then $F$ has bounded $L$-index in every nonzero direction $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$.

original_question: Let {b1,...,bn} be a basis of C^n. Suppose F is entire on C^n and has bounded L-index in each basis direction bi, with L belonging to the corresponding class Q_bi^n for each i. Must F then have bounded L-index in every nonzero direction b that is a complex linear combination b = lambda1 b1 + ... + lambdan bn?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$. For a nonzero direction $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$, let $\mathcal{Q}_{\mathbf{b}}^n$ denote the class of positive continuous functions $L : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{R}_{+}$ satisfying

$$0 < \lambda_1(\mathbf{b}, \eta) := \inf_{z \in \mathbb{C}^n} \inf_{|t_1|, |t_2| \le \eta/L(z)} \frac{L(z + t_1 \mathbf{b})}{L(z + t_2 \mathbf{b})} \le \sup_{z \in \mathbb{C}^n} \sup_{|t_1|, |t_2| \le \eta/L(z)} \frac{L(z + t_1 \mathbf{b})}{L(z + t_2 \mathbf{b})} =: \lambda_2(\mathbf{b}, \eta) < \infty$$

for every $\eta > 0$.

An entire function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$,

$$\frac{|\partial^k_{\mathbf{b}} F(z)|}{k!\, L(z)^k} \le \max_{0 \le j \le m} \frac{|\partial^j_{\mathbf{b}} F(z)|}{j!\, L(z)^j} \qquad \text{for all } k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},$$

where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}} F(z) = \sum_{j=1}^{n} b_j \frac{\partial F}{\partial z_j}(z)$ is the directional derivative.

Let $\{\mathbf{b}_1, \dots, \mathbf{b}_n\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{C}^n$, and for each $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ let $L_i \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathbf{b}_i}^n$. Suppose $F$ is an entire function on $\mathbb{C}^n$ that has bounded $L_i$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}_i$ for every $i = 1, \dots, n$.

Question: Must $F$ have bounded $L$-index in every nonzero direction $\mathbf{b} = \lambda_1 \mathbf{b}_1 + \cdots + \lambda_n \mathbf{b}_n$ (with $\lambda_i \in \mathbb{C}$ not all zero), for some appropriate choice of $L \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathbf{b}}^n$?

original_question: Fix a direction b and an entire function F on C^n with positive continuous L. For each base point z0, define the one-variable slice g_z0(t) = F(z0 + tb) and the slice weight l_z0(t) = L(z0 + tb). What minimal requirements on a set A of base points are enough to ensure that the global directional index N_b(F,L) equals max{N(g_z0,l_z0) : z0 in A}, where N(g_z0,l_z0) is the one-variable l_z0-index of the slice?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ be a fixed direction, let $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ be an entire function, and let $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous positive function. For each $z_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$ define the one-variable slice $g_{z_0}:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ and slice weight $l_{z_0}:\mathbb{C}\to(0,\infty)$ by
$$g_{z_0}(t)=F(z_0+t\mathbf{b}),\qquad l_{z_0}(t)=L(z_0+t\mathbf{b}).$$
Recall that for a (nonconstant) entire function $g$ of one variable and a positive continuous weight $l$, the $l$-index $N(g,l)$ is the least nonnegative integer $m$ (if any) such that for every $t\in\mathbb{C}$,
$$\frac{|g^{(k)}(t)|}{k!\,l(t)^k}\le \max_{0\le j\le m}\frac{|g^{(j)}(t)|}{j!\,l(t)^j}\qquad\text{for all }k\ge 0,$$
and the directional $L$-index $N_{\mathbf{b}}(F,L)$ is the least nonnegative integer $m$ such that for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\frac{1}{k!\,L(z)^k}\Big|\frac{\partial^k F}{\partial \mathbf{b}^k}(z)\Big|\le \max_{0\le j\le m}\frac{1}{j!\,L(z)^j}\Big|\frac{\partial^j F}{\partial \mathbf{b}^j}(z)\Big|\qquad\text{for all }k\ge 0,$$
where $\partial F/\partial\mathbf{b}$ denotes the directional derivative along $\mathbf{b}$.

Determine the minimal conditions on a subset $A\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ of base points that guarantee
$$N_{\mathbf{b}}(F,L)=\sup\{\,N(g_{z_0},l_{z_0}):z_0\in A\,\}.$$
In other words, find the weakest geometric/measure-theoretic requirement on $A$ ensuring that the global directional $L$-index of $F$ can be recovered as the supremum of the one-variable $l_{z_0}$-indices of its slices along $\mathbf{b}$ over base points in $A$.

Let $n\geq 2$ and let $l:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be a continuous positive function. For each $j=1,\dots,n$, define $l_j:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+$ by $l_j(z)=l(z_j)$, where $z=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n$. Let $e_j$ denote the $j$-th standard coordinate direction in $\mathbb{C}^n$.

Recall that an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to be of bounded $l_j$-index in the direction $e_j$ if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$ and all $k\in\mathbb{Z}_+$,
$$\frac{1}{k!}\,\frac{\left|\partial^k F(z)/\partial z_j^k\right|}{l_j(z)^k} \leq \max_{0\le m\le N}\frac{1}{m!}\,\frac{\left|\partial^m F(z)/\partial z_j^m\right|}{l_j(z)^m}.$$
The smallest such $N$ is the $l_j$-index of $F$ in direction $e_j$.

For a fixed point $(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0)\in\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$, the entire function $g(w)=F(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0,w)$ of one variable is said to be of bounded $l$-index if there exists $N\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ (possibly depending on $(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0)$) such that for all $w\in\mathbb{C}$ and all $k\in\mathbb{Z}_+$,
$$\frac{|g^{(k)}(w)|}{k!\,l(w)^k}\leq \max_{0\le m\le N}\frac{|g^{(m)}(w)|}{m!\,l(w)^m}.$$

Suppose an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each $j=1,\dots,n-1$, $F$ has bounded $l_j$-index in the direction $e_j$.
\item For every fixed $(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0)\in\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$, the entire function $w\mapsto F(z_1^0,\dots,z_{n-1}^0,w)$ has bounded $l$-index in $\mathbb{C}$.
\end{enumerate}
Determine whether $F$ must have bounded $l_n$-index in the direction $e_n$ (in the uniform sense, i.e., with a single bound $N$ valid at all points of $\mathbb{C}^n$).

Its current status appears unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems for Entire Functions of Bounded Index in Direction
original_question: For n >= 3, construct an entire function F of n complex variables, a nonzero direction b = (b1,...,bn), and a positive continuous function L such that every one-variable slice t -> F(z0 + tb) has bounded l_z0-index for l_z0(t) = L(z0 + tb), while the full function F(z) has unbounded L-index in direction b.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$. For an entire function $F : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}$, a nonzero direction vector $\mathbf{b} = (b_1, \dots, b_n) \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$, and a positive continuous function $L : \mathbb{C}^n \to (0, \infty)$, recall the following.

(a) The function $F$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists a nonnegative integer $m$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^k F(z)|}{k!\, L(z)^k} \le \max_{0 \le j \le m} \frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^j F(z)|}{j!\, L(z)^j} \quad \text{for all } k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},$$
where $\partial_{\mathbf{b}} F(z) = \sum_{i=1}^n b_i \frac{\partial F}{\partial z_i}(z)$ is the directional derivative. The smallest such $m$ is the $L$-index of $F$ in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.

(b) For each fixed $z_0 \in \mathbb{C}^n$, the slice function $g_{z_0}(t) = F(z_0 + t\mathbf{b})$ is an entire function of one complex variable $t \in \mathbb{C}$. Set $\ell_{z_0}(t) = L(z_0 + t\mathbf{b})$. The slice $g_{z_0}$ is said to have bounded $\ell_{z_0}$-index if there exists a nonnegative integer $m_{z_0}$ such that
$$\frac{|g_{z_0}^{(k)}(t)|}{k!\, \ell_{z_0}(t)^k} \le \max_{0 \le j \le m_{z_0}} \frac{|g_{z_0}^{(j)}(t)|}{j!\, \ell_{z_0}(t)^j} \quad \text{for all } t \in \mathbb{C},\ k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}.$$

Construct an explicit triple $(F, \mathbf{b}, L)$ with $n \geq 3$ such that every slice $g_{z_0}$ has bounded $\ell_{z_0}$-index (the bound $m_{z_0}$ being allowed to depend on $z_0$), while $F$ does not have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.
category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
status_search_result: The analogous two-variable counterexample is known: the function $F(z_1,z_2) = \cos\sqrt{z_1 z_2}$ has bounded index on every slice yet unbounded index in any complex direction. Whether such a construction has been carried out for $n \ge 3$ with the slicewise-bounded $\ell_{z_0}$-index condition stated above is not confirmed in the literature accessible via web search; recent works on slice holomorphic functions of bounded $L$-index in direction develop the theory but do not state a definitive resolution of this construction problem.

paper_title: Magic matrices with their powers, numerical ranges and some open problems
original_question: Let a magic matrix of order n mean an n by n square matrix whose entries are the natural numbers 1, 2, ..., n^2 with no repeated entry, and whose row sums, column sums, main diagonal sum, and antidiagonal sum are all equal. Is it true in general that magic matrices of odd order have full rank, whereas magic matrices of even order have rank strictly smaller than their order?
self_contained_problem:
Define a magic matrix of order $n$ to be an $n\times n$ matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ with real entries such that:
(i) every entry $a_{ij}$ belongs to $\{1,2,\ldots,n^{2}\}$;
(ii) all entries are distinct, i.e. $a_{ij}\neq a_{kl}$ whenever $(i,j)\neq(k,l)$;
(iii) the sum of the entries in each row, in each column, on the main diagonal, and on the antidiagonal are all equal (necessarily to $n(n^{2}+1)/2$).

Decide whether the following statement holds:

For every magic matrix $A$ of order $n$, if $n$ is odd then $\operatorname{rank}(A)=n$, and if $n$ is even then $\operatorname{rank}(A)<n$.

Either prove the statement, or exhibit a counterexample.
status_search_result: Empirical observations and discussions (e.g., Cleve Moler's notes on magic squares in MATLAB) report that odd-order magic squares appear to have full rank, doubly-even ones tend to have rank 3, and singly-even ones have intermediate rank, but a complete proof for arbitrary magic matrices satisfying the stated definition does not appear to be established in the literature found.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: critical exponent elliptic equation in three dimensions
original_question: Let Omega be the unit ball in R^3, let lambda_1 = pi^2 be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of -Delta on Omega, and consider smooth functions u: Omega -> R satisfying -Delta u = u^5 + lambda u in Omega and u = 0 on the boundary. For parameters 0 < lambda <= lambda_1/4, does there exist a nonzero solution u? If such a solution exists in this interval, the source notes that it cannot be positive and radial; it would have to be non-radial and sign-changing.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $\lambda_1 = \pi^2$ denote the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$. For a real parameter $\lambda$ with $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$, consider the boundary value problem
$$-\Delta u = |u|^4 u + \lambda u \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial \Omega,$$
where solutions $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ are sought in the classical (smooth) sense. Note that the nonlinearity has the critical Sobolev exponent $5 = (n+2)/(n-2)$ for $n=3$, and it is known that for $\lambda$ in this range any nontrivial solution must be non-radial and sign-changing. Determine whether there exists a solution $u \not\equiv 0$ to this problem for every $\lambda \in (0, \lambda_1/4]$.
status_search_result: A 2025 preprint ("On Brezis' first open problem: a complete solution", arXiv:2503.06904) claims a complete resolution of this problem, establishing the existence of infinitely many sign-changing, nonradial solutions for the full range of the parameter on the three-dimensional ball, including the previously open regime $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$. The result is recent and pending peer-review confirmation, but it is presented as a complete solution to this open problem.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: global minimality of the radial Ginzburg-Landau solution
original_question: In the same unit-disc Ginzburg-Landau problem with boundary value g(x)=x, let E_epsilon(u) = (1/2) integral_Omega |grad u|^2 + (1/(4 epsilon^2)) integral_Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2 on the class H^1_g(Omega; R^2). Is the radial solution U_epsilon a global minimizer of E_epsilon on H^1_g(Omega; R^2) for every epsilon > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit disc, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be the boundary map $g(x) = x$. For $\varepsilon > 0$ define the Ginzburg–Landau energy
\[ E_\varepsilon(u) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx + \tfrac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_\Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2\,dx \]
on the affine Sobolev space
\[ H^1_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2) : u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}. \]
By symmetrization, there exists a unique radial critical point $U_\varepsilon(x) = f_\varepsilon(|x|)\, x/|x|$, where $f_\varepsilon : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ solves the associated ODE with $f_\varepsilon(0)=0$ and $f_\varepsilon(1)=1$.

Question: Is $U_\varepsilon$ a global minimizer of $E_\varepsilon$ on $H^1_g(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$?
status_search_result: The two-dimensional case is known in two regimes: for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ the radial degree-one vortex $U_\varepsilon$ is the unique global minimizer (Pacard–Rivière and related works), and for $\varepsilon$ large enough (specifically when $E_\varepsilon$ becomes strictly convex on the admissible set) global minimality also holds. However, for intermediate values of $\varepsilon$ in the unit disc with boundary data $g(x)=x$, the question is reported in recent literature as still open; full global minimality for every $\varepsilon>0$ has been established only in dimensions $N\geq 7$ (Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu).

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Consider smooth maps u: R^2 -> R^2 solving the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation Delta u = u(1 - |u|^2) on R^2 and satisfying |u(x)| -> 1 as |x| -> infinity, so that the degree at infinity deg(u,infinity) is defined. For each integer q, the source defines a distinguished vortex V_q(r,theta)=exp(i q theta) g_q(r), with V_0 identically 1. Must every solution u coincide with V_q, up to multiplication by a unit complex number and translation in R^2, where q = deg(u,infinity)?
self_contained_problem:
Consider smooth maps $u:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$, identified with $\mathbb{C}$, that solve the entire Ginzburg–Landau equation
$$\Delta u = u\,(|u|^2-1) \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^2,$$
and satisfy $|u(x)|\to 1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Under this asymptotic condition, the map $u/|u|$ is well-defined for $|x|$ large and has a well-defined topological degree $\deg(u,\infty)\in\mathbb{Z}$ as a map from a large circle to $S^1$. For each integer $q$, let
$$V_q(r,\theta) := e^{i q\theta}\,g_q(r),$$
where $(r,\theta)$ are polar coordinates on $\mathbb{R}^2$, with $V_0\equiv 1$, and where for $q\ne 0$, $g_q:[0,\infty)\to[0,1)$ is the unique solution of the ODE
$$g_q''(r)+\frac{1}{r}g_q'(r)-\frac{q^2}{r^2}g_q(r)+g_q(r)(1-g_q(r)^2)=0,\qquad g_q(0)=0,\ \lim_{r\to\infty}g_q(r)=1,$$
which gives the equivariant vortex of degree $q$.

Determine whether every such solution $u$ must coincide with $V_q$ up to multiplication by a unit complex number and translation of $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $q=\deg(u,\infty)$. That is, must there exist $\alpha\in S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
$$u(x)=\alpha\,V_q(x-x_0)\qquad \text{for all } x\in\mathbb{R}^2\ ?$$
status_search_result: The classification of entire Ginzburg-Landau vortices in the plane is widely cited as an open problem. Partial results exist: for degree $|q|=1$, Mironescu and others established uniqueness/stability properties; in higher dimensions $N\ge 7$, uniqueness of the degree-one equivariant vortex as a minimizer in the unit ball was proved by Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu. However, the full classification in $\mathbb{R}^2$ for all degrees $q$ remains unresolved in the recent literature.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: additional harmonic maps from the disc to the sphere
original_question: Let Omega be the unit disc in R^2 and consider harmonic maps u: Omega -> S^2 satisfying Delta u_i = u_i |grad u|^2 for i=1,2,3, |u|=1 in Omega, and u=g on the boundary. For the boundary condition g(x,y)=(R x, R y, sqrt(1-R^2)) with 0<R<1, the source gives two explicit solutions u and u_bar, with parameters lambda = 1/R + sqrt(1/R^2 - 1) and mu = 1/R - sqrt(1/R^2 - 1). Are there any solutions of this harmonic-map boundary value problem other than those two explicit solutions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the open unit disc. Consider maps $u = (u_1, u_2, u_3): \Omega \to S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ that are weakly harmonic in the sense that they satisfy the Euler–Lagrange system for the Dirichlet energy:
$$\Delta u_i = u_i\, |\nabla u|^2, \qquad i = 1, 2, 3, \qquad |u| = 1 \text{ in } \Omega,$$
with prescribed boundary data
$$u(x,y) = g(x,y) \text{ on } \partial\Omega.$$
Fix a constant $R \in (0,1)$ and choose the boundary datum
$$g(x,y) = \bigl(Rx,\, Ry,\, \sqrt{1-R^2}\bigr), \qquad (x,y) \in \partial\Omega,$$
which maps $\partial\Omega$ onto a horizontal circle of latitude on $S^2$. Define
$$\lambda = \frac{1}{R} + \sqrt{\frac{1}{R^2} - 1}, \qquad \mu = \frac{1}{R} - \sqrt{\frac{1}{R^2} - 1},$$
and consider the two explicit solutions of the above boundary value problem given (in terms of $z = x+iy$) by
$$u(z) = \left(\frac{2\,\mathrm{Re}\,(\lambda z)}{|\lambda z|^2+1},\, \frac{2\,\mathrm{Im}\,(\lambda z)}{|\lambda z|^2+1},\, \frac{|\lambda z|^2 - 1}{|\lambda z|^2+1}\right),$$
$$\bar u(z) = \left(\frac{2\,\mathrm{Re}\,(\mu z)}{|\mu z|^2+1},\, \frac{2\,\mathrm{Im}\,(\mu z)}{|\mu z|^2+1},\, \frac{|\mu z|^2 - 1}{|\mu z|^2+1}\right),$$
both of which match the boundary datum $g$ on $\partial\Omega$.

Question: Does the above boundary value problem admit any weakly harmonic map solution $\Omega \to S^2$ other than $u$ and $\bar u$?
category_tag: Harmonic maps from disc to sphere
status_search_result: Web searches reveal extensive literature on the Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps from the disc into $S^2$ (Brezis–Coron, Jost, Soyeur, and later work on symmetric boundary data and symmetry-breaking), establishing existence of multiple solutions and symmetry phenomena, but no source was found that explicitly resolves the uniqueness-up-to-the-two-explicit-solutions question for this specific axially symmetric latitude-circle boundary datum. The status is therefore not clearly determined by the available evidence.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: In the same B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map setting with smooth boundary data g of degree zero, let E(u)=integral_Omega |grad u|^2 on H^1_g(Omega; S^2). If the minimization is restricted to maps in H^1_g(Omega; S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball, is the infimum of E achieved?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the closed unit ball, and let $g : \partial \Omega \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree zero. Consider the Sobolev class
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)| = 1 \text{ a.e. in } \Omega,\ u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \},$$
equipped with the Dirichlet energy
$$E(u) = \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\, dx.$$
Let $C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2)$ denote the space of continuous $S^2$-valued maps on $\overline{\Omega}$. Determine whether the infimum
$$\inf\bigl\{ E(u) : u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \cap C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2) \bigr\}$$
is attained by some map in $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \cap C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2)$.
status_search_result: The question of whether the Dirichlet energy attains its infimum within the class of continuous $S^2$-valued $H^1$ maps from $B^3$ with prescribed smooth degree-zero boundary data is a long-standing problem connected with the Hardt–Lin Lavrentiev gap phenomenon. The literature on harmonic maps with defects, Brezis–Coron–Lieb type results, and recent surveys on the Lavrentiev gap for harmonic maps into spheres continue to list this attainment question as open; no published proof of attainment or non-attainment was located.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: vanishing singular part for relaxed harmonic-map minimizers
original_question: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed energy R in the B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map problem. The source represents R(u) as integral_Omega |grad u|^2 + S(u), where S(u) measures topological singularities through the distributional Jacobian J u. Must S(u)=0, equivalently J u=0, for such a minimizer? Equivalently, can every such minimizer be approximated strongly in H^1 by maps in H^1_g(Omega; S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to S^2$ be a fixed smooth boundary datum. Consider the Sobolev space
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u|=1 \text{ a.e. in } \Omega,\ u|_{\partial\Omega}=g\}.$$
For $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ define the distributional Jacobian
$$J u = \tfrac{1}{2} \, d\!\left(u^1\, du^2 \wedge du^3 + u^2\, du^3\wedge du^1 + u^3\, du^1\wedge du^2\right),$$
viewed as a distribution; equivalently, writing $D(u) = (u\cdot u_{x_2}\wedge u_{x_3},\ u\cdot u_{x_3}\wedge u_{x_1},\ u\cdot u_{x_1}\wedge u_{x_2})$, one has $\operatorname{div} D(u) = 4\pi \sum_i d_i\, \delta_{a_i}$ for maps with isolated point singularities of degrees $d_i$ at $a_i$. Define the singular ("length of minimal connection") functional
$$L(u) = \sup\Big\{ \int_\Omega D(u)\cdot \nabla\zeta\,dx : \zeta\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega),\ |\nabla\zeta|\le 1,\ \zeta|_{\partial\Omega}\text{ chosen compatibly with }g\Big\},$$
and put $S(u) = 4\pi L(u)$, so $S(u)=0$ if and only if $J u = 0$ (modulo the contribution of the boundary datum $g$). The relaxed Dirichlet energy is
$$R(u) = \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx + S(u),$$
which coincides with the sequentially weak $H^1$-lower semicontinuous envelope of the Dirichlet energy restricted to the maps in $H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$ that are continuous on $\overline\Omega$.

Question: If $u \in H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$ is a minimizer of $R$ on $H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$, must $S(u) = 0$, equivalently $J u = 0$? Equivalently, can every such minimizer be approximated strongly in $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ by maps in $H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$ that are continuous on $\overline\Omega$?
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems, and current literature on minimizers of the relaxed energy for harmonic maps from $B^3$ to $S^2$ (e.g., works of Bethuel–Brezis–Coron and follow-up partial regularity results) discusses partial regularity of such minimizers but does not establish vanishing of the singular part $S(u)$. No publication appears to resolve the question of whether $S(u)=0$ for every minimizer.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: geometric proof and sharp constant for a degree estimate
original_question: For continuous maps f: S^1 -> S^1, Theorem 5.2 gives an estimate of |deg f| by a nonlocal integral over pairs (x,y) for which |f(x)-f(y)| >= sqrt(3). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of this estimate? What is the best possible constant C in that estimate, and is the best constant achieved by some map?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the unit circle equipped with arclength measure, and let $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ denote the topological (Brouwer) degree of a continuous map $f : S^1 \to S^1$. There exists a finite constant $C > 0$ such that, for every continuous $f : S^1 \to S^1$,
$$|\deg f| \;\le\; C \iint_{\{(x,y)\in S^1\times S^1 \,:\, |f(x)-f(y)| \ge \sqrt{3}\,\}} \frac{1}{|x-y|^{2}}\, d\mathcal{H}^1(x)\, d\mathcal{H}^1(y), \qquad (*)$$
where $|f(x)-f(y)|$ denotes Euclidean distance in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the threshold $\sqrt{3}$ is the chord length corresponding to an arc of $2\pi/3$ on $S^1$.

Address the following three questions:

(a) Provide a simpler, more geometric proof of inequality $(*)$ than the existing analytic proofs.

(b) Determine the best (smallest) admissible constant $C$ in $(*)$.

(c) Decide whether this best constant is attained, that is, whether there exists a continuous map $f : S^1 \to S^1$ for which equality holds in $(*)$ with $C$ replaced by the optimal constant.
status_search_result: The inequality belongs to the family of Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen degree estimates. Refinements have been obtained for higher-dimensional spheres, and a recent preprint of F. Hernández (2022) makes progress "towards a refined estimate" in the one-dimensional case, but no published source identifies the sharp constant in the S¹ → S¹ estimate with threshold √3 nor exhibits an extremal map; a purely geometric proof of the estimate is also not reported. The sharp-constant and attainment questions appear to remain open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: minimal fractional Sobolev energy at fixed degree
original_question: For 1 < p < infinity and d in Z, let m_{p,d} be the infimum of the p-th W^{1/p,p} seminorm among maps f in W^{1/p,p}(S^1; S^1) with degree d. Is m_{p,d} = |d| m_{p,1} for all integers d, and is the infimum defining m_{p,d} achieved? If this linear formula fails, is there an explicit formula for lim_{d->infinity} m_{p,d}/d, equivalently inf_{d>0} m_{p,d}/d?
self_contained_problem:
Let $1 < p < \infty$ and identify $S^1$ with the unit circle in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (equivalently with $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$). For a measurable map $f \colon S^1 \to S^1$, define the Gagliardo $W^{1/p,p}$-seminorm
$$[f]_{W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)}^p \;=\; \int_{S^1}\!\!\int_{S^1} \frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{2}}\,dx\,dy,$$
and let $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ be the space of measurable maps with finite seminorm taking values almost everywhere in $S^1$. Each $f \in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ has a well-defined integer topological degree $\deg(f) \in \mathbb{Z}$. For $d \in \mathbb{Z}$, set
$$m_{p,d} \;=\; \inf\!\Big\{ [f]_{W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)}^p \,:\, f \in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1),\ \deg(f)=d \Big\}.$$

(a) Is it true that $m_{p,d} = |d|\, m_{p,1}$ for every $d \in \mathbb{Z}$?

(b) Is the infimum defining $m_{p,d}$ achieved (for every $d \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$)?

(c) If the identity in (a) fails, is there an explicit formula for
$$\lim_{d\to\infty}\frac{m_{p,d}}{d} \;=\; \inf_{d>0}\frac{m_{p,d}}{d}\,?$$
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in works of Brezis and collaborators on fractional Sobolev maps between manifolds (e.g. in surveys on $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ and degree). No publication located in the search resolves whether $m_{p,d}=|d|m_{p,1}$ for all $d$, nor whether the infimum is achieved; related questions about additivity of fractional energies under degree are reported as unresolved.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: universal obstruction to Fourier-magnitude degree recovery
original_question: Does there exist a single map f in C(S^1;S^1), or in VMO(S^1;S^1), such that for every possible summation process, the sums sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} fail to converge to deg f?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1 \subset \mathbb{C}$ denote the unit circle. For a measurable map $f: S^1 \to S^1$, let
$$a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(e^{i\theta}) e^{-in\theta}\, d\theta, \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z},$$
be its Fourier coefficients. For $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ (or more generally $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$, the space of maps of vanishing mean oscillation), the topological degree $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ is well-defined. It is known that, formally,
$$\deg f = \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2,$$
but the series on the right is in general not convergent.

A summation process is, by definition, a family $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}_{n \in \mathbb{Z},\, \varepsilon > 0}$ of real numbers such that, for every fixed $n$, $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \to 1$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, and such that for each $\varepsilon > 0$ the weighted series $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ converges absolutely (one may impose mild regularity such as $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ being bounded and compactly supported in $n$ for each $\varepsilon$).

Question: Does there exist a map $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ (respectively $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$) such that for every summation process $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}$ one has
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \neq \deg f$$
(either the limit does not exist or it differs from $\deg f$)?
status_search_result: Search located the problem within Brezis's published list of favorite open problems and related surveys on VMO degree theory and winding numbers via Fourier series. While a recent complete solution to a different problem ("Brezis' First Open Problem") was found, no source indicates this particular question on universal failure of summation processes has been resolved. Status is therefore inconclusive from available sources.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Brouwer-type fixed point property for VMO maps
original_question: Let B be the closed unit ball in R^N, and let f be a VMO map from B into itself. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0, the approximate fixed-point set {x in B : |f(x)-x| < epsilon} has positive measure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 1$ and let $B$ denote the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Recall that a measurable map $f:B\to\mathbb{R}^N$ belongs to $\mathrm{BMO}(B)$ if 
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}:=\sup_{Q\subset B}\frac{1}{|Q|}\int_Q |f(x)-f_Q|\,dx<\infty,$$
where the supremum is taken over all cubes (or balls) $Q\subset B$ and $f_Q$ denotes the average of $f$ over $Q$. The space $\mathrm{VMO}(B)$ of functions of vanishing mean oscillation consists of those $f\in\mathrm{BMO}(B)$ such that 
$$\lim_{r\to 0}\sup_{Q\subset B,\,\mathrm{diam}(Q)\le r}\frac{1}{|Q|}\int_Q |f(x)-f_Q|\,dx=0.$$

Suppose that $f:B\to B$ is a VMO map (i.e., a VMO map from $B$ into itself). Is it true that for every $\varepsilon>0$ the approximate fixed-point set
$$\{x\in B : |f(x)-x|<\varepsilon\}$$
has positive Lebesgue measure?
category_tag: VMO maps and fixed point theory
status_search_result: Brezis–Nirenberg established a Brouwer-type fixed point result for VMO self-maps of the disk, showing that $0$ belongs to the essential range of $\mathrm{id}-u$. However, the stronger quantitative question of whether the approximate fixed-point set $\{|f(x)-x|<\varepsilon\}$ has positive Lebesgue measure for every $\varepsilon>0$ does not appear to be resolved in the available literature, and no published solution was located.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: blow-up set of unbounded extremal solutions
original_question: For the extremal solution u^* of the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda f(u) in a smooth bounded domain, assume u^* is not essentially bounded. What can be said about the blow-up set of u^*? In particular, when Omega is convex, must the blow-up set consist of a single point?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth bounded domain, and let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a $C^1$, nondecreasing, convex, superlinear nonlinearity (i.e. $f(0)>0$ and $\lim_{t\to\infty} f(t)/t = +\infty$). Consider the family of semilinear Dirichlet problems
$$-\Delta u = \lambda\, f(u) \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u>0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u=0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
indexed by $\lambda>0$. It is classical that there is a finite extremal parameter $\lambda^*\in(0,\infty)$ such that for $\lambda\in(0,\lambda^*)$ this problem admits a minimal classical solution $u_\lambda$, and the pointwise increasing limit
$$u^*(x) := \lim_{\lambda\nearrow\lambda^*} u_\lambda(x)$$
defines a weak ("extremal") solution at $\lambda=\lambda^*$. Define the blow-up set of $u^*$ as
$$\mathcal{B}(u^*) := \{x_0\in\overline{\Omega} : \operatorname{ess\,sup}_{B_r(x_0)\cap\Omega} u^* = +\infty \text{ for every } r>0\}.$$

Assume that $u^*\notin L^\infty(\Omega)$.

(a) Describe the structure of $\mathcal{B}(u^*)$ (size, regularity, possible locations) under general assumptions on $\Omega$ and $f$.

(b) When $\Omega$ is in addition convex, must $\mathcal{B}(u^*)$ consist of a single point?
category_tag: Extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
status_search_result: No publication establishing a general structure theorem for the blow-up set of unbounded extremal solutions, nor a proof that the blow-up set is a single point on convex domains, was located. The question is stated as an open problem in surveys on extremal solutions and no resolution appears in the recent literature found.

context_brief: Sobolev and BV norm control by liminf nonlocal tails

with the convention that $\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p=+\infty$ whenever $u\notin W^{1,p}(\Omega)$?

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: sharp relative isoperimetric inequality for the cube
original_question: Let Q be the unit cube in R^N with N >= 2. For a measurable subset S of Q, let |S| be its volume and P(S) its relative perimeter inside Q, and define f_N(t)=inf{P(S): S subset Q is measurable and |S|=t}. In dimension N=2, an explicit formula for f_2(t) is known. For N >= 3, is there an analogous formula for f_N(t)? In particular, is f_N(t) identically 1 near t=1/2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 2$ and let $Q=[0,1]^N$ denote the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^N$. For a measurable set $S\subset Q$, let $|S|$ denote its Lebesgue measure and let $P(S)$ denote its relative perimeter in $Q$, i.e. the $(N-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $\partial^* S \cap \operatorname{int}(Q)$ (where $\partial^* S$ is the reduced boundary of $S$). Define the relative isoperimetric profile of the cube by
$$f_N(t) \;=\; \inf\{\,P(S) : S\subset Q\text{ measurable},\ |S|=t\,\},\qquad t\in[0,1].$$
In dimension $N=2$ an explicit closed-form expression for $f_2(t)$ is known: for $t\in[0,1/2]$,
$$f_2(t)=\begin{cases} 2\sqrt{t/\pi}\cdot(\pi/2) & \text{if } 0\le t\le \pi/16,\\[2pt] \text{(corresponding circular-arc / straight-line formula)} & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}$$
with $f_2(t)=f_2(1-t)$, and in particular $f_2(t)\equiv 1$ for $t$ in a neighborhood of $1/2$ (the minimizer being a half-cube cut by a straight segment).

Question. For every $N\ge 3$, determine an analogous explicit formula for $f_N(t)$ on $[0,1]$. In particular, decide whether there exists $\delta_N>0$ such that
$$f_N(t)\;=\;1\qquad \text{for all } t\in[\,1/2-\delta_N,\;1/2+\delta_N\,],$$
i.e.\ whether the relative isoperimetric profile of the $N$-cube is identically $1$ in a neighborhood of $t=1/2$.
status_search_result: The explicit form of the relative isoperimetric profile of the unit cube in dimension $N\ge 3$ does not appear in the literature; recent work (e.g. Chambers–Mouillé, 2023) treats only restricted classes (orthogonal polyhedra in $[0,1]^3$) and does not resolve the general profile or the flatness near $t=1/2$. No source found establishing the closed-form formula for $f_N(t)$ or proving $f_N\equiv 1$ near $1/2$ for $N\ge 3$, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Moudafi's open question and simultaneous iterative algorithm for general split equality variational inclusion problems and general split equality optimization problems
context_brief: Strong convergence for alternating SEFP algorithms
original_question: Does there exist a strong convergence theorem for an alternating algorithm that solves the split equality feasibility problem in real Hilbert spaces, where the problem is to find variables x and y in their respective constraint sets satisfying the split equality constraint A x = B y?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H_1, H_2, H_3$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $C \subseteq H_1$ and $Q \subseteq H_2$ be nonempty closed convex sets, and let $A: H_1 \to H_3$ and $B: H_2 \to H_3$ be bounded linear operators. The split equality feasibility problem (SEFP) is to find $x \in C$ and $y \in Q$ such that
$$A x = B y.$$
An alternating algorithm is an iterative scheme that, given current iterates $(x_n, y_n)$, updates $x_{n+1}$ using the current $y_n$ and then updates $y_{n+1}$ using $x_{n+1}$ (rather than updating both coordinates simultaneously). The question is whether there exists an alternating iterative algorithm producing sequences $\{x_n\} \subset C$ and $\{y_n\} \subset Q$ that converge strongly (in norm) to a solution $(x^*, y^*)$ of the SEFP, under reasonable assumptions on $C, Q, A, B$.
status_search_result: Moudafi's original alternating CQ algorithm yielded only weak convergence, and he posed the strong-convergence variant as an open question. Subsequent works have given affirmative answers: improved/relaxed alternating CQ algorithms and simultaneous iterative algorithms have been shown to converge strongly to a solution of the split equality (feasibility) problem in real Hilbert spaces.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: Given a finite pattern p and an integer k, is it decidable whether p is k-avoidable, meaning whether there exists an infinite word over a k-letter alphabet that avoids p?
self_contained_problem:
A pattern is a finite nonempty word p over an alphabet of variables. An infinite word w over a finite alphabet A is said to avoid p if there is no nonerasing morphism h from the free monoid on the variables of p to A* such that h(p) occurs as a factor of w. For an integer k ≥ 1, the pattern p is called k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over some k-letter alphabet that avoids p; otherwise p is called k-unavoidable. The avoidability index of p is the smallest k for which p is k-avoidable (and ∞ if no such k exists).

Question: Is the following decision problem decidable? Given as input a finite pattern p (over a finite set of variables) and a positive integer k, determine whether p is k-avoidable.

Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm that, given (p, k), computes whether the avoidability index of p is at most k?
status_search_result: While Bean–Ehrenfeucht–McNulty and Zimin gave an algorithm deciding whether a pattern is avoidable at all (i.e., k-avoidable for some k), no algorithm is known to decide, for given k and p, whether p is k-avoidable; computing the avoidability index of a pattern remains a long-standing open problem in combinatorics on words. Even individual short patterns (e.g., αα ββ γγ) have unresolved avoidability indices.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: For ternary patterns in partial-word avoidability, where ternary patterns are patterns over the three variables alpha, beta, and gamma, determine the avoidability indices of such patterns, or at least bounds for those indices; also determine a bound on the length of unavoidable ternary patterns.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A partial word over a finite alphabet A is a sequence whose entries are either letters of A or a distinguished "hole" symbol ⋄ (which is compatible with every letter). A pattern p is a (full) word over a pattern alphabet E = {α, β, γ, …} of variables. A pattern p is said to be k-avoidable in partial words if there exists an infinite partial word w over some alphabet of size k such that no factor of w is a "partial-word instance" of p, where a partial-word instance is obtained by applying a non-erasing morphism h: E* → A* (assigning to each variable a nonempty full word) and then allowing some positions of the resulting word to be replaced by ⋄ provided each occurrence pattern is preserved up to compatibility. The partial-word avoidability index μ_p(p) is the least integer k ≥ 1 such that p is k-avoidable in partial words (and ∞ if no such k exists, in which case p is called unavoidable in partial words).

Restrict attention to ternary patterns, i.e., patterns over exactly three variables {α, β, γ}.

Problems.
(a) For every ternary pattern p, determine the partial-word avoidability index μ_p(p), or, failing that, give nontrivial upper and lower bounds for μ_p(p).
(b) Determine an explicit bound L such that every ternary pattern of length greater than L is avoidable in partial words (equivalently, bound the length of the longest unavoidable ternary patterns).
status_search_result: The partial-word avoidability indices of ternary patterns have been computed for most cases by Blanchet-Sadri and collaborators, who classified ternary patterns by index (with 4 patterns of index 5, 24 of index 4, and 209–216 of index 3). However, the indices of a small set of ternary patterns (e.g., αβαγβγ, ααβγγαβ, ααβαγαββα, αββαγααβα) remain undetermined, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: For abelian powers in partial words, determine the minimum alphabet size needed to construct a partial word with infinitely many holes that avoids abelian third powers, fourth powers, and fifth powers. In this setting, abelian n-freeness means that the holes can be filled with alphabet letters so that the word contains no n consecutive factors that are permutations of one another.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $\diamond \notin A$ denote a "hole" symbol that matches every letter of $A$. A partial word over $A$ is an infinite sequence $w \in (A \cup \{\diamond\})^{\mathbb{N}}$; a filling of $w$ is any word in $A^{\mathbb{N}}$ obtained from $w$ by replacing each occurrence of $\diamond$ with some letter of $A$.

Two finite words $u, v \in A^*$ are called abelian-equivalent if they have the same length and the same multiset (Parikh vector) of letters. For an integer $n \geq 2$, an abelian $n$-th power is a finite word of the form $u_1 u_2 \cdots u_n$ where $u_1, \dots, u_n$ are pairwise abelian-equivalent nonempty words. A partial word $w$ is said to avoid abelian $n$-th powers if there exists a filling of $w$ whose infinite word contains no factor that is an abelian $n$-th power.

For each $n \in \{3, 4, 5\}$, determine the minimum size $|A|$ of an alphabet $A$ for which there exists an infinite partial word over $A$ containing infinitely many holes that avoids abelian $n$-th powers.
status_search_result: The question of the minimum alphabet size needed for an infinite partial word with infinitely many holes avoiding abelian n-th powers (for n = 3, 4, 5) appears in the literature on abelian pattern avoidance in partial words as an explicit open problem. While related results have been obtained (e.g., constructions over binary alphabets avoiding abelian 6th powers, and resolved bounds for abelian squares), the exact thresholds for n = 3, 4, 5 with infinitely many holes do not appear to have been determined in subsequent work.

paper_title: Open Problems on Avoidable Patterns in Partial Words
original_question: For binary patterns p in abelian pattern avoidance for partial words, improve the known sufficient length bound: the source states that if the length of p is at least 360, then there exists a binary partial word with infinitely many holes that avoids p in the abelian sense. What smaller bound, if any, can replace 360 while preserving that conclusion?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A partial word over a finite alphabet A is a sequence whose letters belong to A together with a special symbol ⋄ (called a hole) that is regarded as "undefined" and is compatible with every letter of A. Two full words u, v over A of the same length are abelian equivalent (written u ~_ab v) if v is a permutation of the letters of u, equivalently if for every a ∈ A the number of occurrences of a in u equals the number of occurrences of a in v. A pattern is a nonempty word p over a pattern alphabet E = {x_1, x_2, …} of variables. A partial word w over A is said to meet the pattern p in the abelian sense if there exists a non-erasing morphism-like assignment that replaces each occurrence of a variable x_i in p by a factor of w in such a way that the resulting consecutive factors of w are pairwise abelian-equivalent whenever the corresponding variables are equal (and the holes ⋄ in w are treated as wildcards compatible with this equivalence). Otherwise, w avoids p in the abelian sense. A pattern p is called binary if it uses exactly two distinct variables.

Known bound. It is known that for every binary pattern p of length at least 360, there exists an infinite binary partial word containing infinitely many holes that avoids p in the abelian sense.

Problem. Determine the smallest integer N (or improve the value 360 as much as possible) such that the following statement still holds: for every binary pattern p of length at least N, there exists an infinite binary partial word with infinitely many holes that avoids p in the abelian sense.
status_search_result: Search located the original result establishing the length-360 sufficient bound for abelian avoidance of binary patterns by binary partial words with infinitely many holes (Blanchet-Sadri et al., RAIRO ITA 2014). Subsequent improvements for full words (e.g., every binary pattern of length > 14 is abelian-2-avoidable, MFCS 2016) do not address the partial-word setting with infinitely many holes. No source was found that explicitly improves the 360 bound in the partial-word setting, so the status is unclear.

Let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous, decreasing function with $f(0)=b>1$ such that the map $x\mapsto xf(x)$ is increasing and bounded on $[0,\infty)$. For a parameter $h>0$, consider the second-order difference equation with delayed constant-yield harvesting
$$x_{n+1}=x_n f(x_{n-1})-h,\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$

paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
original_question: For the no-delay p-periodic stocking equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) + h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic sequence of nonnegative stocking quotas with positive total stocking over one period, each quota ordering has a globally attracting p-periodic solution. If xbar_av is the average of the attracting p-periodic solution for one ordering of the stocking quotas and xhat_av is the average for a permutation of the same quotas, how are xbar_av and xhat_av related?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the scalar discrete-time population model with no delay and periodic stocking
\[ x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) + h_n, \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots, \]
where:
- $f:[0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ is a continuous, positive function such that $x \mapsto x f(x)$ is a (smooth) "contest competition" map: $x f(x)$ is bounded, has a unique positive fixed point, and is such that the unstocked equation $x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n)$ has a globally attracting positive equilibrium on $(0,\infty)$;
- $\{h_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ is a $p$-periodic sequence of nonnegative real numbers (stocking quotas) with $\sum_{n=0}^{p-1} h_n > 0$.

Under these hypotheses, for every choice (i.e. every cyclic ordering) of the quotas $h_0, h_1, \dots, h_{p-1}$, the equation admits a globally attracting positive $p$-periodic solution $\{x_n^*\}$. Define the temporal average over one period
\[ \bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1} x_n^*. \]

Now let $\sigma$ be any permutation of $\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$, and let $\hat{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$ denote the analogous average of the globally attracting $p$-periodic solution corresponding to the permuted stocking sequence $h_{\sigma(0)}, h_{\sigma(1)}, \dots, h_{\sigma(p-1)}$.

Determine the relationship between $\bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$ and $\hat{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$. In particular, decide whether $\bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}} = \hat{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$ holds for every permutation $\sigma$, every period $p$, and every admissible map $f$; and if not, characterize the orderings of the quotas that maximize and minimize the average $\bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$.

status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on discrete contest competition models with periodic stocking. Related work establishes existence and global attractivity of periodic solutions and partial results for small periods (p = 2, 3), but no general result comparing averages across all permutations of stocking quotas appears to have been established.

paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
original_question: For the Beverton-Holt periodic harvesting equation x_{n+1} = K mu x_n/(K + (mu - 1)x_n) - h_n with K > 0, mu > 1, and a p-periodic sequence h_n of nonnegative harvesting quotas that gives a nonempty persistent set, compare the average of the attracting population cycle for one ordering of the quotas with the average for any permutation of the same quotas. How does xbar_av, the attractor average for h_n, relate to xhat_av, the attractor average for the permuted sequence hhat_n?
self_contained_problem:
Fix constants $K>0$ and $\mu>1$, and let $p\ge 2$ be an integer. Consider the periodically harvested Beverton–Holt difference equation
$$x_{n+1} \;=\; \frac{K\mu\, x_n}{K+(\mu-1)x_n} \;-\; h_n, \qquad n=0,1,2,\dots,$$
where $\{h_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ is a $p$-periodic sequence of nonnegative harvesting quotas. Assume the quotas $(h_0,h_1,\dots,h_{p-1})$ are chosen so that the equation admits a nonempty persistent set (i.e., there exist initial conditions for which $x_n>0$ for all $n$) and a globally attracting $p$-periodic cycle $(\bar x_0,\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_{p-1})$ on this set. Define the attractor average
$$\bar x_{\mathrm{av}} \;=\; \frac{1}{p}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\bar x_n.$$
Let $\sigma$ be any permutation of $\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$, and set $\hat h_n = h_{\sigma(n)}$ extended $p$-periodically. Assume the permuted equation
$$y_{n+1}=\frac{K\mu\, y_n}{K+(\mu-1)y_n}-\hat h_n$$
also has a nonempty persistent set with globally attracting cycle $(\hat x_0,\dots,\hat x_{p-1})$, and let $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{1}{p}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\hat x_n$. Determine the precise relationship between $\bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$ and $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}$: characterize those permutations $\sigma$ for which $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}=\bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$, and for the remaining permutations decide whether $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}\le \bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$ or $\hat x_{\mathrm{av}}\ge \bar x_{\mathrm{av}}$, or otherwise describe how the attractor average changes under permutation of the harvesting quotas.

  x_{n+1} = K·μ·x_n / (K + (μ − 1)·x_n) − h_n,
where K > 0 is the carrying capacity, μ > 1 is the intrinsic growth ratio, and {h_n}_{n≥0} is a nonnegative p-periodic sequence of harvesting quotas determined by a fixed multiset H = {h_0, h_1, …, h_{p−1}}. Assume that for some ordering of H the persistent set is nonempty.

original_question: For the normalized delayed Pielou equation x_{n+1} = b x_n/(1 + x_{n-1}) - h_n, the constant-harvest case h_n = 1 has the invariant I_b(x_n, x_{n-1}) = ((1 + b)/(1 + x_n))((1 + b)/(1 + x_{n-1}))(1 + x_n + x_{n-1}). What becomes of these invariants when the harvesting sequence is perturbed periodically or nonautonomously as h_n = 1 +/- epsilon_n?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order difference equation (a normalized delayed Pielou-type model with harvesting)

    x_{n+1} = (b x_n)/(1 + x_{n-1}) - h_n,    n = 0, 1, 2, ...,

where b > 0 is a parameter, the initial data x_{-1}, x_0 are positive, and h_n is a real sequence ("harvesting") chosen so that the iterates remain positive.

In the constant-harvesting case h_n ≡ 1, the function

    I_b(u, v) = ((1 + b)/(1 + u)) · ((1 + b)/(1 + v)) · (1 + u + v)

is an invariant of the dynamics, in the sense that I_b(x_n, x_{n-1}) is constant along every orbit (x_n) of the recurrence with h_n ≡ 1.

Now perturb the harvesting term to

    h_n = 1 ± ε_n,

where (ε_n) is either a periodic sequence of small real numbers or a more general nonautonomous bounded sequence with ε_n → 0 (or |ε_n| small).

Problem. Determine what happens to the invariant I_b under such perturbations. Specifically:
  (a) Does there exist a modified invariant (a function J_b(n, u, v), possibly depending on n through the perturbation, or an adiabatic/approximate invariant) which is exactly or approximately conserved by the perturbed dynamics?
  (b) Describe the behavior of the quantity I_b(x_n, x_{n-1}) along orbits of the perturbed equation: is it bounded, does it drift, and at what rate (in terms of ε_n) does it evolve?
  (c) In the periodic case ε_{n+p} = ε_n, analyze the long-term dynamics (existence, stability, and structure of periodic orbits) using these (possibly modified) invariants.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a paper on harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models (Zbl 6633387). No subsequent work resolving the fate of the Lyness/Pielou-type invariant I_b under periodic or nonautonomous perturbations h_n = 1 ± ε_n appears in the literature reachable via search; related work on perturbed Lyness equations exists but does not settle this particular question for the delayed Pielou equation with harvesting.

paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
original_question: For the delayed p-periodic stocking equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) + h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic nonnegative stocking sequence with positive total stocking over one period, a p-periodic solution exists and is known to be globally attracting when p = 2. Is that p-periodic solution globally attracting for every period p > 2?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order difference equation with stocking
  x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) + h_n,  n = 0, 1, 2, ...,
where:
- f: [0, ∞) → (0, ∞) is a continuous, strictly decreasing function with lim_{x→∞} f(x) = 0 (so that x f(x) is a contest-competition recruitment function);
- the stocking sequence (h_n) is p-periodic and nonnegative with h_{n+p} = h_n for all n, and satisfies the positivity-of-total-stocking condition h_0 + h_1 + ... + h_{p-1} > 0;
- initial values x_{-1}, x_0 are nonnegative (and not both zero).

It is known that for every such system there exists a positive p-periodic solution, and that when p = 2 this p-periodic solution is globally attracting (i.e., every solution with positive initial data converges to it).

Question: For every integer p > 2, and for every choice of f and p-periodic nonnegative stocking sequence (h_n) as above, is the p-periodic solution of this equation globally attracting?
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a conjecture about delayed periodic stocking in discrete contest-competition models. A web search did not turn up any paper resolving the conjecture for general periods p > 2; related literature treats periodic Beverton–Holt and related models but not this specific delayed stocking conjecture. No evidence of resolution was found, so the status appears to be open.
