paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
original_question: For the delayed p-periodic harvesting equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) - h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic nonnegative harvesting sequence, investigate the global dynamics: characterize persistence and extinction, the structure of any persistent set, boundedness and strong persistence of persistent solutions, periodic attractors or other limiting behavior, and how these properties depend on the sequence h_0, h_1, ..., h_{p-1}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous function (typically a contest-competition-type per-capita growth function, e.g. continuous, positive, and decreasing with $\lim_{x\to\infty} x f(x) < \infty$). Fix an integer $p\ge 1$ and let $(h_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a $p$-periodic sequence of nonnegative real numbers (so $h_{n+p}=h_n$ for all $n\ge 0$). Consider the second-order delayed difference equation with periodic harvesting
$$ x_{n+1} \;=\; x_n\, f(x_{n-1}) \;-\; h_n, \qquad n=0,1,2,\ldots, $$
with nonnegative initial data $x_{-1},x_0\ge 0$, where the iteration is considered only as long as the right-hand side remains nonnegative (otherwise the population is declared extinct).

Carry out a complete global analysis of this equation. Specifically:

(a) Characterize, in terms of the harvesting vector $(h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_{p-1})$ and the function $f$, the set of initial conditions $(x_{-1},x_0)$ that lead to extinction (the orbit becomes nonpositive in finite time) versus those that persist (remain strictly positive for all $n$).

(b) Describe the structure (topological and dynamical) of the persistent set: is it open, connected, bounded, invariant?

(c) Show whether every persistent solution is bounded and strongly persistent, i.e. $0<\liminf_{n\to\infty} x_n \le \limsup_{n\to\infty} x_n <\infty$, and identify sharp conditions on $(h_0,\ldots,h_{p-1})$ ensuring this.

(d) Determine the limiting behavior of persistent solutions: existence, multiplicity, and global attractivity of $p$-periodic (or $2p$-periodic) solutions, and/or the occurrence of more complex attractors.

(e) Describe how the answers in (a)–(d) depend on the harvesting profile $(h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_{p-1})$, including monotonicity in each $h_i$ and bifurcations as the harvesting amplitudes vary.
status_search_result: A web search reveals only partial results: studies of $x_{n+1}=x_n f(x_{n-1})$ under constant-yield harvesting establish some stability, boundedness and persistence facts, and related delayed harvesting models exhibit complex dynamics (period doubling, chaos). No source provides a full global characterization for general $p$-periodic harvesting in the delayed contest-competition model, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: For every epsilon > 0, is there an integer n(epsilon) such that every triangle-free graph on n > n(epsilon) vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most (1/25 + epsilon)n^2 edges?
self_contained_problem:
A graph is triangle-free if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices. A graph is bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two parts so that every edge has its endpoints in different parts. For a graph G, let b(G) denote the minimum number of edges whose deletion from G yields a bipartite graph.

Determine whether the following holds: for every real number ε > 0, there exists an integer n(ε) such that every triangle-free graph G on n > n(ε) vertices satisfies
   b(G) ≤ (1/25 + ε) n².
category_tag: Extremal graph theory (Erdős conjecture on triangle-free graphs)
status_search_result: The full conjecture (with constant 1/25) remains open. The current best known unconditional bound is approximately n²/23.5 (Balogh–Clemen–Lidický, 2021), improving the previous n²/18 bound. The conjecture has been verified for certain ranges of edge density (e.g., density ≤ 0.2486 or ≥ 0.3197), but the asymptotic statement with (1/25 + ε) for all sufficiently large n is not known.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Let k be an integer at least 2. If G is a (k - 1)-connected graph with m edges and n vertices, must G admit a k-partition (V1, V2, ..., Vk) whose size, meaning the number of edges with endpoints in different parts, is at least ((k - 1)/k)m + ((k - 1)/(2k))n + O(1)?
self_contained_problem:
Let k ≥ 2 be an integer. For a graph G with vertex set V(G), a k-partition of V(G) is an ordered family (V_1, V_2, …, V_k) of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets whose union is V(G); its size is the number of edges of G having endpoints in two different parts. A graph G is (k−1)-connected if it has at least k vertices and remains connected after the removal of any k−2 of them.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant C = C(k) such that every (k−1)-connected graph G with n vertices and m edges admits a k-partition (V_1, …, V_k) whose size is at least
   ((k−1)/k) · m + ((k−1)/(2k)) · n − C.
status_search_result: The statement is a conjecture of Bollobás and Scott on connected k-partitions. Surveys and follow-up works on judicious/max k-cut partitions (e.g., the Bollobás–Scott program, the Ma–Yen paper "On several partition problems of Bollobás and Scott", and "Better Bounds for k-Partitions of Graphs") list this connectivity-strengthened lower bound as a still-standing conjecture, with related partial results proved in special cases (e.g., k = 2 corresponds to known Edwards-type bounds for connected graphs), but no general resolution for arbitrary k ≥ 3 has been located.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: For every integer k at least 2, does every graph G with m edges and n vertices have a k-partition (V1, V2, ..., Vk) such that max over all pairs i < j of e(V_i union V_j), the number of edges induced by the union of those two parts, is at most 6m/binom(k + 2, 2) + O(n)? In addition, when the minimum degree delta(G) is at least c(k)n for some constant depending only on k, can the O(n) additive term be removed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k \ge 2$ be an integer. For a (finite, simple) graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, a $k$-partition of $G$ is an ordered partition $(V_1, V_2, \dots, V_k)$ of its vertex set $V(G)$. For $S \subseteq V(G)$, let $e(S)$ denote the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $S$.

(a) Prove or disprove: there exists a function $f_k(n) = O(n)$ (depending only on $k$) such that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges admits a $k$-partition $(V_1, \dots, V_k)$ satisfying
$$\max_{1 \le i < j \le k} e(V_i \cup V_j) \;\le\; \frac{6m}{\binom{k+2}{2}} + f_k(n).$$

(b) Show, moreover, that there exists a constant $c(k) > 0$ such that if the minimum degree $\delta(G) \ge c(k)\, n$, then the additive $O(n)$ term in (a) can be removed; that is, $G$ admits a $k$-partition with
$$\max_{1 \le i < j \le k} e(V_i \cup V_j) \;\le\; \frac{6m}{\binom{k+2}{2}}.$$
status_search_result: The conjecture was described as "wildly open" in the surveyed literature. Subsequent work by Fan and Hou (Random Structures & Algorithms, 2017, "Bounds for pairs in judicious partitioning of graphs") and by Xu and Yu ("Better bounds for k-partitions of graphs", Combinatorics, Probability and Computing) establishes improved bounds approaching the conjectured value and resolves related problems of Bollobás and Scott in the affirmative, providing partial/asymptotic progress, but the exact bound 6m/binom(k+2,2) + O(n) for all k ≥ 2 (and the dense-graph statement without O(n)) does not appear to be fully settled.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Let G be a graph and M a maximum matching in G. A free neighbor of a vertex u not incident with M is a matched vertex x from an edge xy in M such that xu is an edge and yu is not an edge; two such unmatched vertices have different free-neighbor sets if these sets are unequal. Let r(M) be the maximum number of pairs of unmatched vertices such that each pair has different free-neighbor sets with respect to M, and let r(G) be the maximum r(M) over all maximum matchings M of G. Can r(G) be determined in polynomial time?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph and let $M\subseteq E$ be a maximum matching of $G$. Denote by $V(M)$ the set of vertices incident with some edge of $M$. For an edge $xy\in M$ and a vertex $u\in V\setminus V(M)$, say that $x$ is a free neighbor of $u$ (with respect to $M$) if $xu\in E$ but $yu\notin E$. For each $u\in V\setminus V(M)$, let $F_M(u)$ denote the set of free neighbors of $u$. Two unmatched vertices $u,v\in V\setminus V(M)$ are said to have different free-neighbor sets if $F_M(u)\neq F_M(v)$.

Define $r(M)$ to be the maximum number of (vertex-disjoint) pairs $\{u_i,v_i\}$ of unmatched vertices such that $F_M(u_i)\neq F_M(v_i)$ for each pair, and define
$$r(G)=\max\{r(M): M\text{ is a maximum matching of }G\}.$$

It is known that for any fixed maximum matching $M$, $r(M)$ can be computed in polynomial time. Question: can $r(G)$ be determined in polynomial time (in $|V|+|E|$)?
status_search_result: No published resolution of this question could be located via web search. The problem is stated as an open problem in a survey on graph partitions, and no follow-up paper providing a polynomial-time algorithm or a hardness result for computing r(G) appears to be available.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Does every graph G with m edges and minimum degree at least 2 admit a bisection (S, T) such that each of the two induced subgraphs G[S] and G[T] contains at most m/3 edges?
self_contained_problem: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with $m=|E|$ edges and minimum degree at least $2$. A bisection of $G$ is an ordered partition $(S,T)$ of $V$ with $||S|-|T||\le 1$. For a vertex set $X\subseteq V$, let $e(X)$ denote the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $X$. Prove or disprove: every such graph $G$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ satisfying \[ \max\{e(S),\,e(T)\} \le \frac{m}{3}. \] Moreover, determine all graphs for which equality is achieved.
status_search_result: The conjecture (originally posed by Bollobás and Scott) was confirmed by Xu and Yu, who proved that every graph with m edges and minimum degree at least 2 admits a bisection (S,T) with max{e(S),e(T)} ≤ m/3, and characterized the triangle K_3 as the unique extremal graph.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Does every planar graph with n vertices admit a bisection (S, T) whose cut size e(S, T), the number of edges with one endpoint in each part, is at most n?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple planar graph on n vertices. A bisection of G is an ordered partition (S, T) of the vertex set V(G) with ||S| - |T|| ≤ 1. Let e(S, T) denote the number of edges of G with one endpoint in S and the other in T.

Prove or disprove: every planar graph G on n vertices admits a bisection (S, T) such that
    e(S, T) ≤ n.
status_search_result: The statement is a folklore conjecture in graph partitioning. It has been verified for restricted subclasses of planar graphs (e.g., plane triangulations, where a minimum balanced bipartition with at most n cut edges has been shown to exist, with both parts inducing connected near-triangulations) and analogous O(n) or improved bounds are known for planar graphs without separating triangles, but no proof for all planar graphs has been published as of 2025.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c such that every graph G admits a bisection (S, T) with |N_T(u)| >= d_S(u) - c for every u in S and |N_S(v)| >= d_T(v) - c for every v in T?
self_contained_problem: Does there exist an absolute constant $c \geq 0$ such that every finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$ admits a bisection, i.e., a partition $V = S \cup T$ with $\bigl||S|-|T|\bigr| \leq 1$, satisfying the following local degree condition: for every vertex $u \in S$, the number of neighbors of $u$ in $T$ is at least $d_S(u) - c$, and for every vertex $v \in T$, the number of neighbors of $v$ in $S$ is at least $d_T(v) - c$? Here $d_X(w)$ denotes the number of neighbors of $w$ lying in the set $X$.
status_search_result: The question is a constant-error weakening of the Bollobás–Scott bisection conjecture. Recent work (2025) on bisections of graphs under degree constraints describes the weaker version as "widely open" and proves only results obtaining roughly (1/4)d_G(v) in each side, leaving a factor-of-2 gap; no absolute constant c as required is known.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: For positive integers s and t, let g(s,t) be the least minimum-degree threshold such that every graph with minimum degree at least g(s,t) can be partitioned into S and T with delta(G[S]) at least s and delta(G[T]) at least t. On triangle-free graphs, is the sharp threshold g(s,t) equal to s + t?
self_contained_problem: For positive integers $s$ and $t$, define $g(s,t)$ to be the least integer with the following property: every finite simple graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G) \geq g(s,t)$ admits a partition of its vertex set $V(G) = S \sqcup T$ such that the induced subgraph $G[S]$ has minimum degree at least $s$ and the induced subgraph $G[T]$ has minimum degree at least $t$. Restricting attention to the class of triangle-free graphs, prove or disprove that $g(s,t) = s+t$ for all positive integers $s,t$. Equivalently, show that every triangle-free graph with minimum degree at least $s+t$ admits such a partition, and that this bound is sharp.
status_search_result: Kaneko (1998) proved that for triangle-free graphs and any positive integers s,t, every graph with minimum degree at least s+t admits the required partition, settling Stiebitz's question affirmatively. The lower bound s+t is easily seen to be tight, so g(s,t) = s+t on triangle-free graphs.

context_brief: Thomassen partition with prescribed small set
original_question: For every positive integer l, does there exist an integer k(l) such that whenever G is a k(l)-connected graph and X is a subset of V(G) with |X| <= l, the graph G has a partition (S, T) with X contained in S, every vertex of S having at least l neighbors in T, and both induced subgraphs G[S] and G[T] l-connected?
status_search_result: Web searches indicate that this conjecture of Thomassen (with the prescribed-set strengthening of partitioning a highly connected graph into two highly connected parts where vertices of one part have many neighbors in the other) remains open. Related results — Kühn–Osthus on highly connected spanning bipartite subgraphs, Stiebitz's degree-partition theorem, and tournament analogues — represent progress on neighboring questions, but the specific graph version with prescribed X ⊆ S does not appear to have been resolved.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
context_brief: Existence of bisection degree threshold gb(s,t)
original_question: For given integers s and t, does there exist an integer l such that every graph with minimum degree at least l has a bisection (S, T) satisfying delta(G[S]) >= s and delta(G[T]) >= t? If such l exists, what is the smallest such threshold gb(s,t)?
self_contained_problem: Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. A bisection of G is an ordered partition (S,T) of V into two sets whose sizes differ by at most 1. For a subset U⊆V, let G[U] denote the subgraph induced by U, and let δ(H) denote the minimum degree of a graph H. For nonnegative integers s and t, decide whether there exists an integer ℓ=ℓ(s,t) with the following property: every graph G with δ(G)≥ℓ admits a bisection (S,T) such that δ(G[S])≥s and δ(G[T])≥t. If such an integer ℓ exists, determine the smallest such ℓ, denoted gb(s,t). (This is the bisection analogue of Stiebitz's theorem, which asserts that minimum degree at least s+t+1 suffices to guarantee a (not necessarily balanced) bipartition with the analogous induced minimum-degree conditions.)
status_search_result: Recent work (2025) establishes that a threshold function for the bisection analogue of Stiebitz's theorem exists: every graph with minimum degree at least some f(k)=O(k) admits a bisection in which each induced part has minimum degree at least k. Thus existence of gb(s,t) is established (at least when s=t and asymptotically), but the exact value of gb(s,t) remains undetermined, so the problem is only partially solved.

paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
original_question: Does every graph G with minimum degree at least 4 admit a 2-good partition (S, T), meaning min{delta(G[S]), delta(G[T])} >= 2, whose two class sizes are nearly balanced in the sense that floor(|V(G)|/2) - 2 <= |S| <= |T| <= ceil(|V(G)|/2) + 2?
self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph H, let δ(H) denote its minimum degree, and for a subset U ⊆ V(H), let H[U] denote the subgraph of H induced by U. A 2-good partition of a graph G is an ordered partition (S, T) of V(G) into two nonempty parts such that min{δ(G[S]), δ(G[T])} ≥ 2. Determine whether the following statement holds: every (finite, simple) graph G with δ(G) ≥ 4 admits a 2-good partition (S, T) with |S| ≤ |T| satisfying

⌊|V(G)|/2⌋ − 2 ≤ |S| ≤ |T| ≤ ⌈|V(G)|/2⌉ + 2.
status_search_result: The statement is false as stated: the complete graph K_5 has minimum degree 4, yet in any partition (S, T) of its vertex set into two nonempty parts at least one part has size ≤ 2, forcing min{δ(G[S]), δ(G[T])} ≤ 1. Hence no 2-good partition of K_5 exists, contradicting the claimed near-balanced existence.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: For fixed integers k >= 3 and t, let P_t be the path on t vertices, and say that a graph is P_t-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to P_t. In k-Precoloring Extension, the input is a graph G together with a partial k-coloring of some vertices, and the question is whether that partial coloring can be extended to a proper k-coloring of all of G. In List k-Coloring, every vertex v has a list L(v) contained in {1, ..., k}, and the question is whether G has a proper coloring assigning each vertex a color from its list. For bipartite P_t-free graphs, what is the computational complexity of the unresolved cases: k-Precoloring Extension for t = 7, 8, or 9 with k = 3, 4, 5, or any fixed k >= 6, and for t >= 10 with k = 3; and List k-Coloring for t = 7 with k = 3, 4, 5, or any fixed k >= 6, and for t = 8, t = 9, or t >= 10 with k = 3?
self_contained_problem:
Let k ≥ 3 and t ≥ 1 be fixed integers. Let P_t denote the path on t vertices. A graph G is P_t-free if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to P_t. A graph is bipartite if its vertex set admits a partition into two independent sets. A proper k-coloring of G is a function c : V(G) → {1,…,k} with c(u) ≠ c(v) whenever uv ∈ E(G).

Consider the following decision problems restricted to bipartite P_t-free graphs:

(A) k-Precoloring Extension. Input: a bipartite P_t-free graph G and a partial map c₀ : W → {1,…,k} defined on some subset W ⊆ V(G) such that c₀ is a proper coloring of G[W]. Question: can c₀ be extended to a proper k-coloring of G?

(B) List k-Coloring. Input: a bipartite P_t-free graph G together with a list assignment L : V(G) → 2^{{1,…,k}}. Question: does there exist a proper coloring c of G with c(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V(G)?

Determine the computational complexity (polynomial-time solvable vs. NP-complete) of:

  • k-Precoloring Extension on bipartite P_t-free graphs for each of the cases t ∈ {7, 8, 9} with k ∈ {3, 4, 5} or any fixed k ≥ 6, and for t ≥ 10 with k = 3.

  • List k-Coloring on bipartite P_t-free graphs for t = 7 with k ∈ {3, 4, 5} or any fixed k ≥ 6, and for each of t = 8, t = 9, and t ≥ 10 with k = 3.
category_tag: Graph coloring complexity on H-free graphs
status_search_result: A literature search shows continued progress on List k-Coloring and Precoloring Extension restricted to P_t-free bipartite graphs (e.g., NP-completeness of 4-PreExt on P_10-free chordal bipartite graphs, 4-List Coloring on P_8-free chordal bipartite graphs, polynomial-time algorithms for comb-/caterpillar-convex bipartite subclasses in 2023–2024). However, no source resolves the full set of listed open cases on general bipartite P_t-free graphs; the entries remain marked as unresolved in subsequent surveys.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: In Precoloring Extension, the input is a graph G, a positive integer k, and a partial k-coloring of some vertices of G; the question is whether this partial coloring can be extended to a proper k-coloring of all vertices of G. What is the computational complexity of Precoloring Extension when the input graph is restricted to be a grid graph?
self_contained_problem:
A grid graph is a finite induced subgraph of the infinite graph whose vertex set is $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ and in which two vertices $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ are adjacent if and only if $|x_1-x_2|+|y_1-y_2|=1$. (Equivalently, a grid graph is the Cartesian product $P_m \square P_n$ of two paths, or an induced subgraph thereof.)

For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, a proper $k$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c:V(G)\to\{1,\dots,k\}$ such that $c(u)\neq c(v)$ whenever $uv\in E(G)$. A partial $k$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c_0:W\to\{1,\dots,k\}$ defined on some subset $W\subseteq V(G)$ such that $c_0(u)\neq c_0(v)$ whenever $u,v\in W$ are adjacent.

The Precoloring Extension problem takes as input a triple $(G,k,c_0)$, where $G$ is a graph, $k$ is a positive integer, and $c_0$ is a partial $k$-coloring of $G$, and asks whether there exists a proper $k$-coloring $c$ of $G$ such that $c(v)=c_0(v)$ for every vertex $v$ on which $c_0$ is defined.

Determine the computational complexity of Precoloring Extension when the input graph $G$ is restricted to be a grid graph.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an explicit open problem in a recent survey on graph-coloring problems for special graph classes by Paulusma, and web searches did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving the complexity of Precoloring Extension restricted to grid graphs. Related results are known (e.g., NP-hardness of precoloring extension on bipartite graphs, planar graphs, and unit interval graphs, and tractability on graphs of bounded treewidth with bounded number of colors), but the grid case appears to remain unresolved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: For a connected graph, the diameter is the maximum distance between two vertices, where distance is the length of a shortest path. The 3-Coloring problem asks whether a graph has a proper coloring using colors {1, 2, 3}. The List 3-Coloring problem asks whether a graph with lists L(v) contained in {1, 2, 3} for each vertex v has a proper coloring that assigns every vertex a color from its list. What is the computational complexity of 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2, and what is the computational complexity of List 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. The distance $d(u,v)$ between two vertices $u, v \in V$ is the length (number of edges) of a shortest path from $u$ to $v$, and the diameter of $G$ is $\max_{u,v \in V} d(u,v)$. A proper $3$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c : V 	o \{1,2,3\}$ such that $c(u) 
eq c(v)$ whenever $uv \in E$. In the 3-Coloring problem, given $G$, one must decide whether $G$ admits a proper $3$-coloring. In the List 3-Coloring problem, each vertex $v \in V$ is additionally equipped with a list $L(v) \subseteq \{1,2,3\}$, and one must decide whether $G$ admits a proper $3$-coloring $c$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ for all $v \in V$.

Determine the computational complexity of the 3-Coloring problem and of the List 3-Coloring problem when the input graph $G$ is restricted to have diameter at most $2$. In particular, are these problems solvable in polynomial time, or are they NP-complete, on the class of graphs of diameter $2$?
status_search_result: The complexity of 3-Coloring (and List 3-Coloring) restricted to diameter-2 graphs remains a well-known open problem. No polynomial-time algorithm or NP-hardness proof is known. The best known algorithms are subexponential: Mertzios and Spirakis (2012/2016) achieved $2^{O(\sqrt{n \log n})}$, and Dębski, Piecyk, and Rzążewski (ESA 2021 / SIDMA) improved this to $2^{O(n^{1/3} \log^2 n)}$. NP-hardness is known for diameter-3 graphs but not for diameter-2 graphs.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: An asteroidal set in a graph is an independent set S such that every three vertices of S form an asteroidal triple, and the asteroidal number of a graph is the maximum size of such a set. For every pair of fixed integers k >= 3 and p >= 3, what is the computational complexity on graphs with asteroidal number at most p of the following three problems: k-Coloring, which asks for a proper coloring with colors {1, ..., k}; k-Precoloring Extension, which asks whether a given partial k-coloring extends to a full proper k-coloring; and List k-Coloring, which asks whether a proper coloring exists that respects vertex lists contained in {1, ..., k}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. Three pairwise distinct vertices $u, v, w \in V$ form an asteroidal triple if between any two of them there is a path in $G$ that avoids the closed neighborhood of the third. An asteroidal set in $G$ is an independent set $S \subseteq V$ such that every three vertices of $S$ form an asteroidal triple. The asteroidal number of $G$, denoted $\mathrm{an}(G)$, is the maximum size of an asteroidal set in $G$.

For an integer $k \ge 1$, consider the following decision problems on an input graph $G$:
- $k$-Coloring: does there exist a proper coloring $c: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$?
- $k$-Precoloring Extension: given a subset $W \subseteq V$ and a proper coloring $c_W: W \to \{1, \dots, k\}$, does $c_W$ extend to a proper coloring $c: V \to \{1, \dots, k\}$?
- List $k$-Coloring: given lists $L(v) \subseteq \{1, \dots, k\}$ for each $v \in V$, does there exist a proper coloring $c$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ for all $v$?

Problem: For every pair of fixed integers $k \ge 3$ and $p \ge 3$, determine the computational complexity (polynomial-time solvable vs. NP-complete) of each of $k$-Coloring, $k$-Precoloring Extension, and List $k$-Coloring when restricted to the class of graphs $G$ with $\mathrm{an}(G) \le p$.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a recent survey on graph coloring for special graph classes. For the case p = 2 (AT-free graphs), List k-Coloring is known to be polynomial-time solvable for every fixed k, but for general p ≥ 3 the complexity of all three problems remains open. No resolution was found in the search.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: A comparability graph is an undirected graph whose edges can be oriented so that whenever (u, v) and (v, w) are directed edges, (u, w) is also a directed edge. For a graph class F and integer p, F - pe denotes graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by adding at most p edges, and F + pv denotes graphs that can be modified into a graph of F by deleting at most p vertices. What is the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of Coloring on comparability - pe graphs and on comparability + pv graphs?
self_contained_problem:
An undirected simple graph G is called a comparability graph if each of its edges can be assigned a direction so that whenever (u,v) and (v,w) are directed edges of the resulting orientation, (u,w) is also a directed edge (i.e., the orientation is transitive). For a class of graphs F and a non-negative integer p, define:
- F − pe = { G : there exists a set E' of at most p edges of G such that G − E' ∈ F }, i.e., graphs obtainable from a member of F by adding at most p edges; equivalently, graphs that become a member of F after deleting at most p edges.
- F + pv = { G : there exists a set S of at most p vertices of G such that G − S ∈ F }, i.e., graphs from which one can delete at most p vertices to obtain a graph in F.

The Coloring problem asks, given a graph H and an integer k, whether H admits a proper k-coloring (an assignment of colors 1,…,k to vertices such that adjacent vertices receive distinct colors), where the chromatic number is to be determined.

Let F be the class of comparability graphs. Determine the parameterized complexity, with parameter p, of the Coloring problem on the graph classes F − pe and F + pv. In particular, decide whether Coloring on each of these classes is fixed-parameter tractable, in XP, W[1]-hard, or para-NP-hard when parameterized by p.
status_search_result: Coloring on comparability graphs is polynomial-time solvable. For the modified classes, partial results are known: Coloring on comparability+1e and comparability−1e graphs is polynomial-time solvable, while for fixed k ≥ 2, Coloring on comparability+ke graphs is NP-complete (Takenaga–Higashide). The full parameterized-complexity classification with parameter p (FPT vs. W[1]-hard, etc.) for both comparability−pe and comparability+pv does not appear to be settled in the literature found.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: In online graph coloring, vertices are presented one at a time in an externally determined order, and an online algorithm must irrevocably color each vertex using only the already revealed induced subgraph and its colors. For a graph G, chi_OL(G) is the smallest worst-case number of colors used by any online coloring algorithm over all vertex arrival orders. A graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if there is an online coloring algorithm A and a function h such that A uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors on every graph G in the class. Are chordal bipartite graphs online chi_OL-bounded?
self_contained_problem:
In the online graph coloring model, the vertices of a finite simple graph G are presented one at a time in an order chosen by an adversary. When a vertex v is presented, all edges between v and previously presented vertices are revealed, and an online algorithm must irrevocably assign v a color (a positive integer) such that adjacent vertices receive distinct colors; the algorithm has no knowledge of vertices that have not yet been presented. For an online algorithm A and a graph G, let A(G,σ) denote the number of colors A uses on G when vertices arrive in order σ. Define
  χ_OL(G) = min_A max_σ A(G,σ),
where the minimum is over all online coloring algorithms and the maximum is over all vertex arrival orders.

A class 𝒢 of graphs is said to be online χ_OL-bounded if there exists a single online coloring algorithm A and a function h : ℕ → ℕ such that for every G ∈ 𝒢 and every arrival order σ, A uses at most h(χ_OL(G)) colors on G.

A graph is chordal bipartite if it is bipartite and every induced cycle has length exactly 4 (equivalently, it contains no induced cycle of length at least 6 and no odd cycle).

Question: Is the class of chordal bipartite graphs online χ_OL-bounded?
status_search_result: The problem of online χ_OL-boundedness for bipartite graphs (and its restricted subclasses) is described as a long-standing open question; partial positive results exist for P_k-free bipartite graphs for small k (e.g. P_8-free, even P_9-free), but no resolution for the full class of chordal bipartite graphs appears in the literature found. The status appears to be still open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
original_question: In online graph coloring, vertices arrive sequentially and must be colored irrevocably based only on the subgraph seen so far. A graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if some online coloring algorithm has its color usage bounded by a function of chi_OL(G), the optimal online chromatic number of each graph G. Is the class of graphs that are both triangle-free and P6-free, equivalently (C3, P6)-free graphs, online chi_OL-bounded?
self_contained_problem:
In the online graph coloring model, the vertices of a graph are revealed one at a time in some adversarial order. When a vertex v is revealed, all edges between v and previously revealed vertices are also revealed, and the online algorithm must irrevocably assign v a proper color (different from the colors already given to its revealed neighbors), based only on the induced subgraph seen so far. For a graph G, let χ_OL(G) denote the online chromatic number of G, that is, the minimum over all online coloring algorithms A of the maximum, over all presentation orders of V(G), of the number of colors used by A on G.

A class C of graphs is said to be online χ_OL-bounded if there exists a function f: ℕ → ℕ and an online coloring algorithm A such that for every graph G ∈ C and every presentation order of V(G), the algorithm A uses at most f(χ_OL(G)) colors.

For an integer n ≥ 1, let P_n denote the path on n vertices and C_n the cycle on n vertices. A graph G is called (C_3, P_6)-free if it contains neither C_3 nor P_6 as an induced subgraph (equivalently, G is triangle-free and induced-P_6-free).

Question: Is the class of (C_3, P_6)-free graphs online χ_OL-bounded?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published resolution of online χ_OL-boundedness for (C_3, P_6)-free graphs. Known results address the offline chromatic number (Randerath et al. showed χ ≤ 4 for (C_3, P_6)-free graphs) and offline/poly-time coloring for P_6-free graphs, but the online version for this specific class appears unresolved.

paper_title: Some New Results of Two Open Problems Related to Integral Inequalities
context_brief: Power refinement of an integral inequality
original_question: Let [a,b] be a real interval, let f be a nonnegative continuous real-valued function on [a,b], and let α>0 and β>0. Assume that for every x in [a,b], ∫_x^b f(t)^{min(1,β)} dt ≥ ∫_x^b (t-a)^{min(1,β)} dt. Determine conditions on α, β, and an exponent λ under which the strengthened integral inequality ∫_a^b f(x)^{α+β} dx ≥ (∫_a^b (x-a)^α f(x)^β dx)^λ holds.
self_contained_problem:
Let $[a,b] \subset \mathbb{R}$ with $a<b$, let $\alpha>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, and let $f:[a,b]\to[0,\infty)$ be a continuous function satisfying the assumption
$$\int_x^b f(t)^{\min\{1,\beta\}}\,dt \;\geq\; \int_x^b (t-a)^{\min\{1,\beta\}}\,dt \qquad \text{for every } x \in [a,b].$$
Determine all triples $(\alpha,\beta,\lambda)$ of real numbers (with $\alpha,\beta>0$) for which the inequality
$$\int_a^b f(x)^{\alpha+\beta}\,dx \;\geq\; \left(\int_a^b (x-a)^{\alpha}\,f(x)^{\beta}\,dx\right)^{\lambda}$$
holds for every such function $f$. In particular, give explicit admissible values of the exponent $\lambda$ in terms of $\alpha$, $\beta$, and the length $b-a$.

paper_title: Localized Spot Patterns on the Sphere for Reaction-Diffusion Systems: Theory and Open Problems
context_brief: Brusselator DAE equilibria for small spot numbers
original_question: Consider the slow differential-algebraic system for localized spot dynamics of the singularly perturbed Brusselator reaction-diffusion model on the unit sphere. The unknowns are N spot locations x_1, ..., x_N on the sphere and spot strengths S_1, ..., S_N; in slow time sigma = epsilon^2 t, the locations satisfy dx_j/dsigma = (2/A_j(S_j))(I - x_j x_j^T) sum_{i != j} S_i x_i/|x_i - x_j|^2, and the strengths are determined by the nonlinear Green-interaction constraint [I - nu(I - E_0)G]S + nu(I - E_0)chi(S) - (2E/N)e = 0, where G_ij = log|x_i - x_j| for i != j, G_ii = 0, and nu = -1/log(epsilon). Can one prove analytically, using group-theoretic methods for ODEs and stability methods analogous to those for Eulerian point vortices on a ring, the observed equilibrium and orbital-stability behavior for small N: an orbitally stable three-spot ring for N = 3; a tetrahedral four-spot configuration for N = 4; an (N - 2) + 2 configuration for N = 5, 6, 7 consisting of two antipodal polar spots and N - 2 equally spaced equatorial spots; instability of ring patterns for N >= 4; and the breakup of the N = 8 (N - 2) + 2 pattern into a twisted cuboidal configuration?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{S}^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the unit sphere. Fix an integer $N\ge 2$ and a small parameter $0<\epsilon\ll 1$, and set $\nu=-1/\log\epsilon$. Consider $N$ "spots" with locations $x_1,\dots,x_N\in\mathbb{S}^2$ (pairwise distinct) and source strengths $S=(S_1,\dots,S_N)^T\in\mathbb{R}^N$ governed by the slow differential–algebraic system

$$\frac{dx_j}{d\sigma}=\frac{2}{A_j(S_j)}\bigl(I-x_jx_j^T\bigr)\sum_{i\ne j}\frac{S_i\,x_i}{|x_i-x_j|^2},\qquad j=1,\dots,N,$$

on the slow time scale $\sigma=\epsilon^2 t$, coupled to the nonlinear constraint

$$[\,I-\nu(I-E_0)\mathcal G\,]\,S+\nu(I-E_0)\,\chi(S)-\frac{2E}{N}\,e=0,$$

where: $\mathcal G$ is the symmetric $N\times N$ matrix with entries $\mathcal G_{ij}=\log|x_i-x_j|$ for $i\ne j$ and $\mathcal G_{ii}=0$; $e=(1,\dots,1)^T\in\mathbb{R}^N$; $E_0=\frac{1}{N}ee^T$; $\chi:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^N$ acts componentwise with a fixed scalar nonlinearity $\chi$; and $A_j(S_j)$ and the constant $E$ are the prescribed positive scalar quantities arising from the inner core problem of the singularly perturbed Brusselator reaction–diffusion model on $\mathbb{S}^2$.

Using only analytical tools (e.g. equivariant ODE/group-theoretic methods, and stability arguments analogous to those used for Eulerian point vortices on a circle), rigorously prove the following equilibrium and orbital-stability statements for the above DAE system at small $N$:

1. For $N=3$, the symmetric three-spot ring (three equally spaced spots on a great circle) is an equilibrium and is orbitally stable.
2. For $N=4$, the regular tetrahedral configuration is an orbitally stable equilibrium.
3. For each $N\in\{5,6,7\}$, the $(N-2)+2$ configuration consisting of two antipodal polar spots together with $N-2$ equally spaced spots on the equator is an orbitally stable equilibrium.
4. For every $N\ge 4$, any single-ring (coplanar equally spaced) equilibrium pattern is unstable.
5. For $N=8$, the $(N-2)+2$ configuration is unstable, and perturbations of it evolve under the DAE flow to a "twisted cuboidal" equilibrium configuration.
category_tag: Localized spot patterns on the sphere
status_search_result: The conjectured equilibrium and stability behaviors for small spot numbers (N=3 ring, N=4 tetrahedron, (N−2)+2 patterns for N=5,6,7, ring instability for N≥4, and N=8 twisted-cuboidal breakup) appear to remain at the level of numerical observation and formal asymptotics. Subsequent literature on Brusselator spot dynamics on the sphere and related bulk–membrane variants continues to treat these as conjectures established via asymptotic/numerical means rather than via rigorous group-theoretic ODE proofs, and we found no later work providing the requested analytic proof.

paper_title: Localized Spot Patterns on the Sphere for Reaction-Diffusion Systems: Theory and Open Problems
context_brief: Gray-Scott spot dynamics on the sphere
original_question: For the Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion model on the unit sphere, v_t = epsilon^2 Delta_S v - v + B u v^2 and tau u_t = D Delta_S u + (1 - u) - u v^2, in the singular limit epsilon -> 0 with B = O(epsilon/nu) and nu = -1/log(epsilon), the derived slow dynamics for localized spots couples spot locations x_j and strengths S_j through the reduced-wave Green function G satisfying Delta_S G - D^{-1}G = -delta(x - xi) and G(x; xi) approximately -(1/(2pi)) log|x - xi| + R near xi. How can one investigate the dynamics and equilibria of localized spot patterns on the sphere for this Gray-Scott DAE when the reduced-wave Green function and its regular part R are not available in a simple explicit form?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Gray–Scott reaction–diffusion system on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb{R}^3$:
$$v_t = \varepsilon^2 \Delta_S v - v + B\, u v^2, \qquad \tau u_t = D\, \Delta_S u + (1-u) - u v^2,$$
where $\Delta_S$ is the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $S^2$, $D>0$ and $\tau>0$ are fixed, and the feed parameter scales as $B = O(\varepsilon/\nu)$ with $\nu = -1/\log\varepsilon$, in the singular limit $\varepsilon\to 0^+$. In this limit the activator $v$ concentrates near $N$ localized spots at points $x_1(t),\dots,x_N(t)\in S^2$ with strengths $S_1(t),\dots,S_N(t)$. Standard matched-asymptotic analysis yields a differential-algebraic system (DAE) coupling the spot locations $x_j$ and strengths $S_j$ via the reduced-wave Green function $G(x;\xi)$ on $S^2$, defined as the unique solution of
$$\Delta_S G(x;\xi) - D^{-1} G(x;\xi) = -\delta_{S^2}(x-\xi), \qquad x\in S^2,$$
with local behavior $G(x;\xi) = -\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\log|x-\xi| + R(\xi) + o(1)$ as $x\to\xi$, where $R(\xi)$ is the regular part and $|x-\xi|$ denotes the chordal (Euclidean) distance in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Develop a tractable theoretical and computational framework to analyze the slow dynamics, equilibrium configurations (ring patterns, polyhedral configurations, etc.), and linear stability of $N$-spot quasi-equilibrium patterns governed by this DAE in the case where $G(x;\xi)$ and its regular part $R(\xi)$ are not available in simple closed form. Specifically: characterize the equilibrium spot configurations $\{x_j^\ast\}$ and equal-strength equilibria, classify their stability with respect to translational, amplitude, and shape (peanut-splitting) modes, and identify possible bifurcations as $D$, $N$, and the feed strength vary.
category_tag: Localized spot patterns on the sphere
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open direction in work on localized spot patterns for reaction–diffusion systems on the sphere. Subsequent literature (Trinh–Ward and related work on the Brusselator/Schnakenberg on the sphere) has developed numerical-asymptotic frameworks using approximations of the reduced-wave Green function, but a complete analytical theory of Gray–Scott spot equilibria, slow dynamics, and stability on the sphere with the reduced-wave Green function (rather than its Laplace–Beltrami simplification) remains incomplete and is generally treated as still open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For homogeneous universes governed by the basic gravi-dilaton effective string action at tree level, with higher-order and loop corrections neglected, what are the detailed asymptotic limits of the corresponding NS-NS cosmological solutions, and are the known dilaton-moduli-vacuum and axion solutions asymptotically stable?
self_contained_problem:
Consider spatially homogeneous cosmological models derived from the tree-level gravi-dilaton low-energy effective action of string theory in the Neveu–Schwarz–Neveu–Schwarz (NS-NS) sector, with higher-derivative ($\alpha'$) corrections and string-loop corrections neglected. In the simplest setting, the relevant fields are a spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$, a scalar dilaton $\phi$, and a pseudoscalar axion (Kalb–Ramond) field $\sigma$ dual to the NS-NS 2-form $B_{\mu\nu}$, with action (in the string frame)
$$S = \frac{1}{2\lambda_s^{d-1}} \int d^{d+1}x\, \sqrt{-g}\, e^{-\phi}\left( R + (\nabla\phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{12} H_{\mu\nu\rho}H^{\mu\nu\rho}\right),$$
where $H = dB$. Restrict to homogeneous (e.g., Bianchi-type or anisotropic Kasner-like) backgrounds with metric of the form $ds^2 = -dt^2 + \sum_i a_i(t)^2 (dx^i)^2$, dilaton $\phi=\phi(t)$, and axion $\sigma=\sigma(t)$.

Two well-known exact families of solutions are:
(i) the dilaton–moduli–vacuum solutions, obtained for vanishing axion ($\sigma$ constant), which are generalized Kasner-type solutions with $a_i(t)\propto |t|^{p_i}$ and $e^{-\phi}\propto |t|^q$, parametrized by exponents satisfying $\sum_i p_i^2 + (1-\sum_i p_i)^2 = 1$;
(ii) the axion (rolling-axion) solutions, in which a nontrivial $\sigma(t)$ interpolates between two such Kasner-like asymptotic regimes.

Problems:
(a) Give a complete classification of the asymptotic limits (as the cosmological time approaches the initial or final singularity, or infinity) of all such homogeneous NS-NS solutions.
(b) Determine whether the dilaton–moduli–vacuum and axion solutions listed above are asymptotically stable as fixed points / asymptotic regimes of the associated dynamical system on the space of homogeneous backgrounds.
status_search_result: A literature search reveals active ongoing research on dynamical-systems classifications of asymptotic behaviour in tree-level string cosmologies and on the (partial) stability of saxion–axion fixed points. Some classifications of asymptotic behaviour for related gravi-dilaton/axion systems have appeared, and partial stability results are known, but a fully complete asymptotic analysis and stability characterization of all homogeneous NS-NS cosmological solutions, including the dilaton–moduli–vacuum and axion families, does not appear to have been definitively established in full generality.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: When anisotropies are added to tree-level string cosmologies with NS-NS fields, RR fields, or both, what asymptotic regimes occur in simple anisotropic models, which asymptotic decompositions and cancellations are possible, and can one identify lower-parameter attractor solutions that organize the full solution space of these string cosmologies?
self_contained_problem:
Consider tree-level string cosmology in d+1 spacetime dimensions, governed by the low-energy effective action containing the dilaton φ together with NS-NS sector fields (the metric g and the antisymmetric two-form B with field strength H = dB) and/or RR sector p-form field strengths F_{(p)}. Restrict to spatially homogeneous but anisotropic cosmological backgrounds (e.g. Bianchi I or Kasner-like metrics with diagonal scale factors a_1(t), …, a_d(t)), so that the equations of motion reduce to an autonomous dynamical system on a finite-dimensional phase space whose vector field X depends on the dilaton, the Hubble rates H_i = ȧ_i/a_i, and the surviving form-field invariants.

(a) Classify all asymptotic regimes (early-time t → 0⁺ and late-time t → ∞ behaviours, including approach to singularities and to infinity in moduli space) of the resulting dynamical systems for the three cases: (i) NS-NS fields only, (ii) RR fields only, (iii) both NS-NS and RR fields present.

(b) For each regime, determine the asymptotic decompositions of the vector field X (splittings of X into dominant and subdominant pieces in suitable scaling/blow-up coordinates) and identify the asymptotic cancellations (terms that, although individually leading-order, cancel against each other so that the effective leading dynamics is governed by lower-order pieces).

(c) Determine whether there exist lower-parameter attractor solutions—exact special solutions depending on strictly fewer arbitrary constants than the generic solution—such that open families of generic solutions converge to them in the relevant asymptotic limits, and describe the basins of attraction in the full solution space.
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. a 2025 review on classical string cosmology in Gen. Rel. Grav., and 2024 work on anisotropic dark energy from string compactifications) continues to investigate anisotropic tree-level string cosmologies with NS-NS and RR fields, presenting partial results (numerical attractors in restricted Bianchi-I NS-NS sectors, specific α′-corrected models) but no complete classification of asymptotic regimes, decompositions, cancellations, and attractors. The general program therefore appears still open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: Are the cosmological solutions in M-theory that are associated with a BPS state stable under the inhomogeneous perturbations required by such solutions, and how does that stability affect their possible role in the ambient cosmological construction?
self_contained_problem:
Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity (the low-energy limit of M-theory), whose bosonic field content consists of a Lorentzian metric g and a 3-form gauge potential A with 4-form field strength F = dA, governed by the action S = (1/2κ²)∫(R*1 − ½ F∧*F − (1/6) A∧F∧F). A cosmological solution of this theory is a solution (g, A) on a spacetime of the form M = R_t × X (with X a spatial slice) in which the metric and fluxes depend non-trivially on the time coordinate. Such a solution is said to be associated with a BPS state if it preserves a non-zero fraction of the supersymmetries of the theory, i.e. it admits at least one Killing spinor ε satisfying the gravitino variation equation δψ_μ = ∇_μ ε + (1/288)(Γ_μ^{νρσλ} − 8 δ_μ^ν Γ^{ρσλ}) F_{νρσλ} ε = 0. Because BPS-preserving cosmological backgrounds in this setting are generically not spatially homogeneous, perturbations around them must in general be taken to be inhomogeneous (i.e. depending on the spatial coordinates on X as well as on t).

Problem: Determine whether every cosmological solution of eleven-dimensional supergravity that is associated with (i.e. preserves some supersymmetry of) a BPS state is linearly stable under inhomogeneous perturbations of the metric and 4-form field strength. More precisely, for each such background (g, A), study the linearized equations of motion for perturbations (δg, δA) that depend non-trivially on the spatial coordinates, and decide whether all physical modes remain bounded (in a suitable energy norm) as t evolves toward the asymptotic regimes of the solution. Furthermore, analyse how the presence or absence of such stability constrains the role of these BPS cosmological backgrounds within a larger (possibly non-supersymmetric) cosmological construction in which they appear as building blocks or asymptotic regions.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the stability of BPS-associated cosmological solutions in M-theory under inhomogeneous perturbations. The available literature addresses cosmological perturbation theory and stability in modified gravity, but does not provide a general stability theorem for BPS cosmological backgrounds in eleven-dimensional supergravity. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For flat or curved Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universes governed by the full first-order corrected string action with the dilaton term and its coupling to higher-order curvature terms included, what are the relevant asymptotic regimes and stability properties, especially for the vacuum solutions of this effective string theory?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional spatially flat or spatially curved Friedmann–Robertson–Walker spacetime with metric
   ds^2 = -dt^2 + a(t)^2 \gamma_{ij} dx^i dx^j,
where \gamma_{ij} is the metric of a maximally symmetric 3-space of constant curvature k \in \{-1,0,+1\}, together with a scalar dilaton field \phi(t). Take the bosonic string effective action including the leading first-order \alpha' correction:
   S = \frac{1}{2\lambda_s^2} \int d^4x \sqrt{-g}\, e^{-\phi}\Bigl[ R + (\nabla\phi)^2 + \alpha' \bigl( c_1 R_{GB}^2 + c_2 (\nabla\phi)^4 + c_3 R^{\mu\nu}\nabla_\mu\phi\nabla_\nu\phi + \dots\bigr)\Bigr],
where R_{GB}^2 = R^2 - 4 R_{\mu\nu}R^{\mu\nu} + R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}R^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma} is the Gauss–Bonnet term, and the higher-derivative dilaton-curvature couplings are those required by string-frame field redefinition invariance at order \alpha'.

Reducing the equations of motion to an autonomous dynamical system for (H(t), \dot\phi(t), k/a^2(t)) (with H = \dot a/a):

(a) Identify all asymptotic regimes (fixed points, scaling solutions, and behavior as t \to \pm\infty) of this dynamical system, both in the flat (k=0) and curved (k = \pm 1) cases.

(b) Determine the linear stability of each such asymptotic regime, and in particular establish the stability properties of the perturbative string vacuum (H \to 0, \dot\phi \to const, a \to const) as a solution of the full \alpha'-corrected gravi-dilaton equations.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: recent work based on the Hohm–Zwiebach all-order α' action constructs non-singular gravi-dilaton FRW solutions with regular bounces and asymptotic pre-big-bang behavior, and there are stability analyses of de Sitter and FLRW vacua arising from α' corrections. However, a complete classification of asymptotic regimes and stability for the full first-order α'-corrected dilaton-coupled action in both flat and curved FRW cases does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: When the M-theory action is deformed by higher-order Lovelock and Weyl corrections, are the resulting exact 11-dimensional supergravity cosmological solutions stable, what asymptotic modes do their fields admit, and can this analysis establish a no-hair theorem for an inflationary stage in M-theory?
self_contained_problem:
Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity, whose bosonic field content consists of the metric $g_{MN}$ on an 11-dimensional spacetime $M^{11}$ and a 3-form gauge potential $A_3$ with 4-form field strength $F_4 = dA_3$. The classical bosonic action is
$$S_0 = \frac{1}{2\kappa_{11}^2}\int_{M^{11}} d^{11}x\,\sqrt{-g}\Big(R - \tfrac{1}{2}|F_4|^2\Big) - \frac{1}{12\kappa_{11}^2}\int A_3\wedge F_4\wedge F_4.$$
Deform this action by adding higher-order curvature corrections of Lovelock type (i.e. corrections built from the dimensionally extended Euler densities $\mathcal{L}_k = \frac{1}{2^k}\delta^{M_1 N_1\cdots M_k N_k}_{P_1 Q_1\cdots P_k Q_k}R_{M_1 N_1}{}^{P_1 Q_1}\cdots R_{M_k N_k}{}^{P_k Q_k}$) together with Weyl-curvature corrections (scalar polynomial invariants of the Weyl tensor $C_{MNPQ}$, in particular quartic contractions such as $t_8 t_8 C^4$ and $\epsilon_{11}\epsilon_{11}C^4$), yielding a corrected action
$$S = S_0 + \sum_{k\ge 2}\alpha_k \int d^{11}x\,\sqrt{-g}\,\mathcal{L}_k + \sum_j \beta_j \int d^{11}x\,\sqrt{-g}\,\mathcal{W}_j(C),$$
with fixed real coupling constants $\alpha_k,\beta_j$.

(c) No-hair theorem. Using (a) and (b), decide whether an inflationary phase of the 4-dimensional factor (i.e. an epoch in which $a(t)$ undergoes accelerated expansion) is an attractor in the sense of a cosmic no-hair theorem: namely, whether every sufficiently small perturbation of the solution decays so that the late-time geometry approaches the inflationary background, and if so, formulate and prove such a no-hair theorem in this corrected M-theory setting.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: For a three-dimensional Robertson-Walker brane coupled to a scalar field in a five-dimensional bulk, do regular asymptotic solutions exist, and if so can they support the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant while accounting for the role of curvature and the comparison with the Minkowski-brane case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3-dimensional Robertson–Walker brane embedded in a 5-dimensional bulk spacetime, coupled to a bulk scalar field φ. The brane metric is of FRW form with scale factor a(t) and spatial curvature k ∈ {−1, 0, +1}, and the bulk Einstein equations are sourced by the scalar field together with brane stress-energy.

(a) Using the method of asymptotic splittings (i.e., decomposing the vector field of the dynamical system governing a(t), φ(t) and the bulk warp factor into dominant balances and subdominant tails, and analyzing Fuchsian/Kovalevskaya exponents), classify all possible asymptotic behaviors of the solutions near finite-time or infinite-time limits.

(b) Determine whether there exist asymptotic solutions that are regular (free of finite-distance singularities in the metric and scalar field) for the curved cases k = ±1 as well as for k = 0.

(c) For those regular families (when they exist), decide whether they realize the self-tuning program for the cosmological constant: namely, whether a flat (or de Sitter–like with tunable curvature) induced 4-dimensional geometry can be obtained on the brane without fine-tuning of the brane tension / vacuum energy.

(d) Compare these results with the analogous classification for a flat Minkowski brane coupled to the same bulk scalar, and identify the role played by the spatial curvature k of the brane.
status_search_result: The self-tuning problem for the cosmological constant on branes in 5D bulk with a scalar field has been studied in many setups (e.g., holographic self-tuning, P(X,φ) models, bulk black hole configurations), with partial successes for flat Minkowski branes but persistent obstructions (hidden fine-tunings, singularities) in the general case. For curved Robertson–Walker branes analyzed via asymptotic splittings, no complete classification establishing regular self-tuning solutions appears in the literature; the problem is generally regarded as still open.

paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
original_question: If the scalar field and fluid are allowed to interact in Robertson-Walker braneworld models derived from gravi-dilaton string effective actions or their Einstein-frame versions, can those interactions generate regular asymptotics and simultaneously satisfy the three constraints inherited from the previous brane problem?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a Robertson–Walker braneworld cosmological model derived from a gravi-dilaton string effective action (or its Einstein-frame counterpart). On the brane, assume the matter content consists of (i) a scalar field φ with potential V(φ) and (ii) a perfect cosmological fluid with energy density ρ and pressure p = wρ, together with a covariant interaction term Q describing energy–momentum exchange between φ and the fluid, so that the conservation equations take the form

   ρ̇_φ + 3H(ρ_φ + p_φ) = −Q,    ρ̇ + 3H(ρ + p) = Q,

with ρ_φ = ½φ̇² + V(φ), p_φ = ½φ̇² − V(φ), and H = ȧ/a the Hubble rate of the brane scale factor a(t). The modified Friedmann equation on the brane reads

   H² = (κ²/3)(ρ_φ + ρ) + (1/36)(ρ_φ + ρ)² + Λ/3 + 𝓔/a⁴ ± k/a²,

where κ², Λ, and the dark-radiation term 𝓔/a⁴ arise from the bulk and brane tensions.

Determine whether there exists a choice of V(φ), of the fluid equation-of-state parameter w, and of the interaction current Q such that:

(a) every solution (a(t), φ(t), ρ(t)) is geodesically complete and free of curvature singularities for all t ∈ ℝ (regular past and future asymptotics);

(b) the following three constraints are simultaneously satisfied:
   (1) the weak energy condition for the total cosmic fluid holds along the entire evolution;
   (2) the model admits a viable late-time accelerated expansion phase (effective dark-energy regime) consistent with H > 0 and ä > 0 at late times;
   (3) the early-time asymptotic regime matches a bounded, non-singular configuration of the gravi-dilaton string effective action (e.g. a pre-big-bang-type fixed point or a regular bounce).

In other words: can interactions between the scalar field and the fluid produce regular asymptotics while meeting the three conditions above?
status_search_result: No specific resolution of this interacting Robertson–Walker brane problem (regular asymptotics together with the three stated constraints) was located in the literature. While there is extensive work on interacting dark-energy/dark-matter braneworld models and on non-singular pre-big-bang cosmologies, none directly confirm a solution meeting all three conditions in the gravi-dilaton brane setting. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Does the ambient cosmological construction remain valid for all perturbations of Minkowski space that are conformally related to the original metric, so that the construction can be regarded as stable under arbitrary conformally related perturbations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\mathbb{R}^{1,n}, \eta)$ denote Minkowski space with the standard flat Lorentzian metric $\eta$. The Fefferman–Graham ambient construction associates to a conformal class $[g]$ on an $n$-dimensional manifold $M$ an ambient Lorentzian metric on a neighbourhood of $M \times \{0\} \times \mathbb{R}_+$ inside an $(n+2)$-dimensional manifold, in such a way that the cone bundle over $M$ embeds as a hypersurface in the ambient space and the ambient metric restricts to a representative of $[g]$. When $g = \eta$ is flat Minkowski space, this construction reproduces the standard ambient (light-cone) realisation.

Now consider an arbitrary smooth perturbation $\tilde{g}$ of $\eta$, and let $[\tilde{g}]$ denote its conformal class, i.e. the family of metrics $\{\Omega^2 \tilde{g} : \Omega \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^{1,n}), \Omega > 0\}$.

Question: Does the ambient cosmological construction extend to every metric in the conformal class $[\tilde{g}]$ of every perturbation $\tilde{g}$ of $\eta$? Equivalently, is the ambient construction stable in the sense that whenever it applies to a perturbation $\tilde{g}$ of Minkowski space, it applies to every metric conformally related to $\tilde{g}$, so that the global stability of Minkowski space in this framework is preserved under arbitrary conformally related perturbations?

The construction is described as plausibly stable under such perturbations, but a proof appears to be left for future work, and no follow-up resolution was located.

paper_title: On open problems based on fuzzy filters of pseudo BCK-algebras
context_brief: Equivalence of implicative and Boolean pseudo-filters
original_question: Let A be a pseudo-BCK algebra with binary operations customarily written as ⇀ and ⇝, order relation inherited from those operations, and top element 1. In the bounded case, assume A also has a least element 0 in the sense used for bounded pseudo-BCK algebras. A nonempty subset F of A is a pseudo-filter when it is upward closed and closed under the pseudo-BCK filter rule: if x is in F and either x ⇀ y or x ⇝ y is in F, then y is in F. Such a pseudo-filter F is called implicative when, for every x and y in A, membership of (x ⇀ y) ⇀ x in F forces x to be in F and membership of (x ⇝ y) ⇝ x in F forces x to be in F. It is called Boolean when, for every x and y in A, membership of (x ⇀ y) ⇝ x in F forces x to be in F and membership of (x ⇝ y) ⇀ x in F forces x to be in F. In pseudo-BCK algebras, and separately in bounded pseudo-BCK algebras, are the notions of implicative pseudo-filter and Boolean filter equivalent?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A=(A;\rightharpoonup,\rightsquigarrow,1)$ be a pseudo-BCK algebra, where $\rightharpoonup$ and $\rightsquigarrow$ are binary operations on $A$, $1\in A$ is the top element, and the partial order $\le$ is defined by $x\le y \iff x\rightharpoonup y = 1 \iff x\rightsquigarrow y = 1$. A nonempty subset $F\subseteq A$ is called a pseudo-filter if (i) $F$ is upward closed (whenever $x\in F$ and $x\le y$ then $y\in F$), and (ii) for all $x,y\in A$, if $x\in F$ and either $x\rightharpoonup y\in F$ or $x\rightsquigarrow y\in F$, then $y\in F$.

A pseudo-filter $F$ is called an implicative pseudo-filter if for all $x,y\in A$:
- $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightharpoonup x \in F \implies x\in F$, and
- $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightsquigarrow x \in F \implies x\in F$.

A pseudo-filter $F$ is called a Boolean filter if for all $x,y\in A$:
- $(x\rightharpoonup y)\rightsquigarrow x \in F \implies x\in F$, and
- $(x\rightsquigarrow y)\rightharpoonup x \in F \implies x\in F$.

Question: In an arbitrary pseudo-BCK algebra (and separately in a bounded pseudo-BCK algebra, where $A$ additionally has a least element $0$), are the notions of implicative pseudo-filter and Boolean filter equivalent?
status_search_result: Subsequent work titled "Further Complete Solutions to Four Open Problems on Filter of Logical Algebras" (International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems / Atlantis Press, 2019) addresses this question and establishes that in pseudo-BCK algebras the notion of implicative pseudo-filter coincides with the notion of Boolean filter, providing a complete solution to the open problem.

paper_title: Invitation to H-systems in higher dimensions: known results, new facts, and related open problems
original_question: Let n >= 3, let B^n be the unit ball in R^n, let N be a compact closed Riemannian manifold isometrically embedded in R^m, and let pi be the nearest-point projection from a tubular neighborhood of N onto N. For the n-Dirichlet energy E_n[v] = (1/n) integral over B^n of |grad v|^n dx, call u in W^{1,n}(B^n,N) weakly n-harmonic when d/dt at t=0 of E_n[pi o (u+t phi)] is zero for every phi in W_0^{1,n}(B^n,R^m) intersect L^infty(B^n,R^m). Must every such weakly n-harmonic map u be continuous on B^n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ and let $B^n$ denote the open unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Let $N$ be a smooth compact closed Riemannian manifold isometrically embedded in $\mathbb{R}^m$, and let $\pi$ denote the nearest-point projection from a tubular neighborhood of $N$ in $\mathbb{R}^m$ onto $N$. Define the $n$-Dirichlet energy of a map $v \in W^{1,n}(B^n, N)$ by
$$E_n[v] = \frac{1}{n}\int_{B^n} |\nabla v|^n\,dx.$$
A map $u \in W^{1,n}(B^n, N)$ is called weakly $n$-harmonic if
$$\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} E_n[\pi \circ (u + t\varphi)] = 0$$
for every $\varphi \in W_0^{1,n}(B^n, \mathbb{R}^m) \cap L^\infty(B^n, \mathbb{R}^m)$.

Question: Must every weakly $n$-harmonic map $u \in W^{1,n}(B^n, N)$ be continuous on $B^n$?
status_search_result: The continuity/regularity of weakly $n$-harmonic maps from $B^n$ into a general compact Riemannian manifold $N$ (the conformally invariant critical case $p=n$) is a well-known open problem. Regularity is known under symmetry assumptions on the target (e.g., spheres or homogeneous spaces, results by Strzelecki, Toro–Wang, Moser, Duzaar–Mingione, and others), but the general case remains unresolved.

paper_title: Invitation to H-systems in higher dimensions: known results, new facts, and related open problems
original_question: Let Omega be an open subset of R^n, let H: R^{n+1} -> R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u=(u^1,...,u^{n+1}) be in W^{1,n}(Omega,R^{n+1}) as a weak solution of the H-system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = H(u) J_u. If k of the coordinate functions u^i are bounded, for some k in {1,2,...,n}, must u be continuous?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an open set. Let $H : \mathbb{R}^{n+1} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded Lipschitz function. Consider a weak solution $u = (u^1, u^2, \ldots, u^{n+1}) \in W^{1,n}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ of the H-system
$$-\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{n-2} \nabla u\bigr) \;=\; H(u)\, J_u,$$
where $J_u$ denotes the vector whose $i$-th component is the Jacobian determinant of the map $(u^1,\dots,\widehat{u^i},\dots,u^{n+1}) : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$ (with the $i$-th coordinate omitted), with appropriate sign so that the right-hand side represents the prescribed mean curvature term. Suppose that for some integer $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, exactly $k$ of the coordinate functions $u^i$ are bounded in $\Omega$ (the remaining $n+1-k$ need not be bounded beyond their $W^{1,n}$ membership). 

Must $u$ be continuous in $\Omega$?
status_search_result: Known results establish continuity of $W^{1,n}$ weak solutions to the n-dimensional H-system when the full solution $u$ is bounded (in $L^\infty$), or under stronger integrability such as $u \in W^{n-1,n}$. The question of whether boundedness of only $k \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ coordinate components (partial boundedness) is sufficient to imply continuity appears not to have been resolved in the literature; standard regularity techniques (Hardy/BMO, Rivière–Uhlenbeck decomposition, Coifman–Rochberg–Weiss commutator) use boundedness of the whole map. No source establishing or disproving the partial-boundedness implication was found.

context_brief: Endpoint commutator spaces for H-system data
original_question: Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, let u be in W^{1,n}(R^n,R^{n+1}), and set b=H(u), so that b is in W^{1,n}(R^n) intersect L^infty(R^n). self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2. Fix a bounded Lipschitz function H : R^{n+1} → R, and let u ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n, R^{n+1}). Set b := H ∘ u, so that b ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n) ∩ L^∞(R^n). Let H^1(R^n) denote the real Hardy space, let R_α (α = 1, …, n) denote the Riesz transforms on R^n, and let I denote the Riesz potential of order 1 (so that ∇I is essentially the vector of Riesz transforms). For a function b ∈ L^∞, the commutator [b, T] is the operator f ↦ bT(f) − T(bf). A standard H^1-atom a supported in a ball B is said to be a b-atom if, in addition, ∫_B a(x) b(x) dx = 0.

(a) Determine the largest linear subspace V ⊂ H^1(R^n) such that the commutator [b, I] maps V continuously into L^{n/(n−1)}(R^n).

paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
original_question: For a Riemannian manifold M, what topological, Riemannian, or other geometric conditions obstruct the existence of an isometric minimal immersion of M into a Euclidean space? A minimal immersion is understood in the setting of an immersion phi: M -> E^m whose mean-curvature vector H is the object appearing in Beltrami's identity Delta phi = -nH, so the problem asks for intrinsic or topological conditions on M that prevent such a Euclidean minimal realization.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$. An isometric immersion $\varphi:M\to\mathbb{E}^m$ into Euclidean $m$-space is called minimal if its mean-curvature vector field $H$ vanishes identically, equivalently if Beltrami's identity
$$\Delta\varphi=-nH$$
yields $\Delta\varphi=0$, where $\Delta$ is the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $(M,g)$ acting componentwise on the position vector $\varphi$.

Determine intrinsic conditions on $(M,g)$ — of topological nature (e.g., on the homotopy or (co)homology of $M$), of Riemannian-geometric nature (e.g., on curvature invariants such as the Ricci tensor, sectional curvature, scalar curvature, or Chen-type $\delta$-invariants), or of any other intrinsic geometric nature — that obstruct the existence of an isometric minimal immersion $\varphi:M\to\mathbb{E}^m$ for some $m$. In other words, find necessary conditions on $(M,g)$ for the existence of such a minimal isometric immersion into some Euclidean space.
status_search_result: The problem of identifying all obstructions to minimal isometric immersions of a Riemannian manifold into Euclidean space is a long-standing fundamental question. Several partial necessary conditions are known: a classical one is that the Ricci tensor must be nonpositive somewhere (more precisely, for a minimal submanifold in Euclidean space, Ric is not positive-definite everywhere; in fact for compact minimal submanifolds of Euclidean space they cannot exist, so Ric ≥ 0 is incompatible with compactness). Chen's δ-invariants and subsequent work provide further obstructions (in real and complex space forms), and recent results give obstructions for warped-product immersions. However, no complete characterization is known, so the problem remains generally open with substantial partial progress.

paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
original_question: For a Riemannian n-manifold M, what Riemannian conditions obstruct the existence of an isometric Lagrangian immersion M -> C^n? Here C^n is complex Euclidean n-space, and a Lagrangian submanifold is a totally real submanifold whose real dimension equals the complex dimension of the ambient Kahler manifold, equivalently the totally real case with the smallest possible codimension.
self_contained_problem: Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian $n$-manifold, and let $\mathbb{C}^n$ denote complex Euclidean $n$-space endowed with its standard flat Kähler structure (Euclidean metric, standard complex structure $J$, and Kähler form $\omega$). An isometric immersion $f:M\to \mathbb{C}^n$ is called Lagrangian if $f^*\omega=0$; equivalently, $J(df(T_pM))$ is the normal space of $f(M)$ at each $p\in M$, so $f(M)$ is a totally real submanifold whose real dimension equals the complex dimension of the ambient Kähler manifold (the smallest possible codimension for a totally real submanifold). Determine intrinsic Riemannian conditions on $(M,g)$ — formulated purely in terms of curvature invariants (e.g. sectional, Ricci, scalar curvature, or other Riemannian invariants of $g$) — that obstruct the existence of any isometric Lagrangian immersion $f:M\to \mathbb{C}^n$. In particular, find nontrivial necessary conditions that $(M,g)$ must satisfy in order to admit such an immersion.
status_search_result: The problem is a broad research program rather than a single yes/no question. Substantial partial results are known: B.-Y. Chen and collaborators have produced numerous Riemannian obstructions to Lagrangian isometric immersions in $\mathbb{C}^n$ (and more generally complex space forms) via the δ-invariants (Chen invariants) and associated optimal inequalities, beginning with "Some new obstructions to minimal and Lagrangian isometric immersions" (2000) and continuing through work on ideal Lagrangian immersions. However, a complete intrinsic characterization of Riemannian $n$-manifolds admitting an isometric Lagrangian immersion into $\mathbb{C}^n$ is not known, so the general problem remains open.

paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
original_question: What further topological and geometric obstructions prevent Riemannian manifolds from admitting Lagrangian immersions or slant immersions into complex Euclidean or flat Kahler ambient spaces, beyond the known obstruction results surveyed for those two classes of immersions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\tilde M^{2n}, J, g, \omega)$ be a flat Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$ (in particular, the complex Euclidean space $\mathbb{C}^n$ with its standard Kähler structure). An isometric immersion $f: M^n \to \tilde M^{2n}$ of a Riemannian $n$-manifold is called Lagrangian if $f^*\omega = 0$, i.e. $J(f_*T_pM) = (f_*T_pM)^\perp$ for every $p \in M$. More generally, for a constant angle $\theta \in [0, \pi/2]$, an isometric immersion $f: M^k \to \tilde M^{2n}$ of a Riemannian $k$-manifold is called $\theta$-slant if for every $p \in M$ and every nonzero $X \in T_pM$, the angle between $J f_*X$ and $f_*(T_pM)$ equals $\theta$ (Lagrangian immersions correspond to $\theta = \pi/2$).

Known obstructions (of Riemannian, topological, or curvature-theoretic type, e.g. Chen-type $\delta$-invariant inequalities, Maslov-class restrictions, and constraints from the mean curvature) rule out many Riemannian manifolds from admitting such immersions into $\mathbb{C}^n$ or into a flat Kähler ambient space.

Problem. Find further topological and geometric obstructions (beyond the currently known ones) that prevent a Riemannian manifold $M$ from admitting:
(a) a Lagrangian isometric immersion into $\mathbb{C}^n$ (or, more generally, into a flat Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$), and
(b) a $\theta$-slant isometric immersion into $\mathbb{C}^n$ (or into a flat Kähler manifold) for some constant slant angle $\theta \in (0, \pi/2]$.
status_search_result: The problem is an open-ended research question asking for new obstructions to Lagrangian and slant isometric immersions into complex Euclidean / flat Kähler ambient spaces. Recent surveys and papers on δ-invariants and ideal Lagrangian immersions continue to uncover further Riemannian obstructions, but no comprehensive solution exists; the area remains active and the problem is open.

paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
original_question: For a Riemannian n-manifold M, what topological and geometric conditions obstruct an ideal isometric immersion of M into Euclidean space? An isometric immersion phi: M -> E^m is delta(n1,...,nk)-ideal when it attains equality identically in Chen's delta-invariant inequality for the tuple (n1,...,nk), a condition described as receiving the least possible tension from the ambient Euclidean space.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a Riemannian $n$-manifold and let $(n_1,\ldots,n_k)$ be a $k$-tuple of integers with $2\le n_i\le n-1$ and $n_1+\cdots+n_k\le n$. For each point $p\in M$, B.-Y. Chen's $\delta$-invariant is defined by
$$\delta(n_1,\ldots,n_k)(p)=\tau(p)-\inf\{\tau(L_1)+\cdots+\tau(L_k)\},$$
where $\tau$ denotes the scalar curvature, the infimum is taken over all $k$-tuples $(L_1,\ldots,L_k)$ of mutually orthogonal subspaces $L_i\subset T_pM$ with $\dim L_i=n_i$, and $\tau(L_i)$ denotes the scalar curvature of the section $L_i$. For an isometric immersion $\varphi:M\to\mathbb{E}^m$ into Euclidean $m$-space with squared mean curvature $\|H\|^2$, Chen's general inequality states
$$\delta(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\le c(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\,\|H\|^2,$$
where
$$c(n_1,\ldots,n_k)=\frac{n^2\bigl(n+k-1-\sum_i n_i\bigr)}{2\bigl(n+k-\sum_i n_i\bigr)}.$$
The immersion $\varphi$ is called $\delta(n_1,\ldots,n_k)$-ideal if equality holds identically on $M$ (interpreted geometrically as $M$ receiving the least possible tension from the ambient Euclidean space at every point).

Problem: Determine topological and geometric conditions on $M$ that obstruct the existence of a $\delta(n_1,\ldots,n_k)$-ideal isometric immersion $\varphi:M\to\mathbb{E}^m$ for some $m$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a general open problem in submanifold theory. While numerous partial results exist for specific classes (e.g., Lagrangian ideal immersions in complex space forms, ideal hypersurfaces, and obstructions via Casorati curvature), no comprehensive characterization of topological and geometric obstructions to ideal immersions into Euclidean space is known. Recent literature continues to address particular subcases, suggesting the general problem remains open.
